items.body:
## Problem

Authentication runs on a pre-release channel with no decision on record. `app/package.json` pins `next-auth@^5.0.0-beta.32` (installed: 5.0.0-beta.32, `@auth/core` 0.41.3) with `@auth/drizzle-adapter@^1.11.3`. Checked on npm 2026-11-07: `latest` is 4.24.15, `beta` is 5.0.0-beta.32 (published 2026-07-20), and no stable 5.x exists. The caret admits any later beta and a future 5.0.0, so a plain `npm install` can move the auth layer without a PR saying so.

Eighteen files under `app/src` import from `next-auth` or `@auth/*`, including `proxy.ts` (edge `getToken`), `lib/auth/config.ts`, `lib/auth/tenant-adapter.ts` and `lib/db/schema.ts`. Enterprise SSO (dormant since #1845) sits on the same package and resumes in v1.8.

Raised by the external review of `release/1.7` on 2026-11-07 (`claude_code_docs/plans/improvement-plan-2026-11.md`, WS4).

## Reproduction

1. `npm view next-auth dist-tags` → `latest: 4.24.15`, `beta: 5.0.0-beta.32`.
2. `grep next-auth app/package.json` → `^5.0.0-beta.32`.
3. `grep -rl "from \"next-auth\|@auth/" app/src --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' | grep -v __tests__ | wc -l` → 18.
4. No ADR, vault note or issue records why v5 beta was chosen or when it is revisited.

## Cause

The App Router needs Auth.js v5 (v4 has no App Router support), and v5 has been "beta" for the whole life of the project. The choice was forced at the time and never written down, and the version range was left as a caret like any other dependency.

## Expected

A recorded decision (vault `security/` note, linked from this issue) with one of: stay on the beta pinned exactly and name the revisit trigger; upgrade when a stable 5.x ships; migrate to another library. If "upgrade" or "migrate", a follow-up issue with a full drill (auth is a sensitive surface). Whatever the decision, the version is pinned exactly so a move is always a PR.

## Fix (default; the owner can override in a comment)

- This is a decision, taken with the owner in a `/grill` session, not a refactor. The facts to bring: what the app uses from the package (JWT sessions, `forcePasswordChange`, the Drizzle tenant adapter, the SSO providers under `lib/auth/sso`, the edge `getToken` in `proxy.ts`), the cost of a session-format change to signed-in users, and the state of the alternatives (Auth.js stable, Better Auth, hand-rolled sessions).
- Default recommendation: **stay** on 5.0.0-beta.32 pinned exactly (`"next-auth": "5.0.0-beta.32"`, same for `@auth/drizzle-adapter`) in v1.8, with a Dependabot-style check at every release for a stable 5.x; revisit when that ships or when enterprise SSO work starts, whichever comes first. The beta has carried the app through v1.0–v1.7 and every SSO flow is built on it; a migration before launch buys stability on paper and spends a release.
- Not chosen by default: migrating now. Eighteen import sites plus the session format and the SSO code, on the release that is supposed to harden security, not reshape it.
- Out of scope: any change to session shape, tenancy or credentials. Those need their own drill.

## Required tests

- For the decision itself: none; the deliverable is the note and the exact pin.
- For the exact pin: `npm ci` is reproducible (`package-lock.json` unchanged beyond the two range strings); `npm -w app run test` passes the `lib/auth/__tests__` suites; the E2E `auth.spec.ts` shard passes in CI.
- If the decision becomes "upgrade" or "migrate": the follow-up issue carries its own drill and test plan; this issue closes with the link.

items.title: Epic: shared-infrastructure multi-tenancy (SaaS) — awaiting business decision

labels.name: epic
labels.description: Tracking issue for a feature area

items.body:
# Epic: shared-infrastructure multi-tenancy (SaaS)

> **Status: proposal awaiting a business decision — do not start implementation.** This epic exists so the architecture, prerequisite graph, and effort shape are sitting in the tracker when the call is made. If the product ships as customer-managed single-tenant instances (Tier A) plus in-org workspaces (Tier B), this epic stays closed-not-planned and nothing below is wasted — every prerequisite is independently valuable and already tracked.

## The three tenancy tiers (decision frame)

- **Tier A — instance per customer**: ready today modulo the *Platform hardening* milestone (#23 migrations, #24 DSN encryption, secrets ops). The compose stack is the unit; customer data and DSN credentials never leave their infrastructure. This is the default enterprise DQ deployment model.
- **Tier B — workspaces within one org**: #26 PR2 (grants) + the "Scope all global surfaces to connection grants" issue complete it.
- **Tier C — this epic**: multiple customer orgs on shared infrastructure with strict isolation. Only justified if the business model is self-serve SaaS.

## Current readiness: zero tenant awareness, favorable architecture

No `tenant_id` exists on any of the ~15 models; `Connection.name` and user emails are globally unique; JWTs carry no tenant claim; one worker claims all checks; all config (`get_settings()`) is process-global — one LLM key, one encryption key for everyone. **But** the codebase concentrates enforcement into few choke points (auth deps in `security.py`, source access via `connector_for` + `guard_sql`, LLM via `providers.py`, exceptions filters in `_filtered`), which is what makes Tier C a large refactor rather than a rewrite.

The crown-jewel risk to design around: `exception_records.row_data` holds samples of customer data in the shared app DB.

## Prerequisite graph (all already tracked — they ARE the runway)

```
#23 Alembic ──────────────► every schema change below ships as migrations
#26 SSO + grants + tokens ─► identity/membership machinery, resource-scoped authz patterns
   └─ grants-scoping issue ► Phase 0: the choke-point inventory tenant filters will reuse
#24 DSN encryption (enc:v1:) ► versioned prefix is the hook for per-tenant keys (enc:v2:<tenant>)
#25 job-queue worker ───────► where per-tenant fairness/quotas attach
#30 audit log ──────────────► gains a tenant dimension
```

## Phases (each becomes its own issue when/if the decision lands)

### Phase 1 — tenant model & identity
`tenants` table (id, slug, name, status active|suspended, created_at). `tenant_id` FK on `users` and `connections`, **denormalized onto the hot tables** (`datasets`, `checks`, `check_runs`, `exception_records`, `rca_sessions`, `chat_sessions`, `custom_dashboards`, `saved_queries`, `audit_log`) — joins alone are not defense-in-depth. JWT gains a `tenant` claim; OIDC (#26) maps IdP → tenant by issuer/domain. Re-scope uniqueness: `(tenant_id, name)` for connections; **decision required**: emails unique per-tenant (allows one person in two tenants via separate accounts — recommended, simpler) vs global users with memberships. Tenant provisioning API (platform-admin role above `admin`).

### Phase 2 — enforcement: app filters + Postgres RLS
App layer: tenant predicate added to the same choke points the grants-scoping issue inventoried. Database layer: **row-level security policies on every tenant-owned table** keyed to `current_setting('app.tenant_id')`, with the session variable set in `get_db()`/`session_factory()` per request from the JWT claim — so one missed application-side filter is a blank result, not a cross-customer breach. SQLite dev mode: app-layer only (RLS is the prod Postgres net); CI runs the RLS suite against Postgres.

### Phase 3 — per-tenant configuration
Per-tenant rows for: LLM provider/model/key (or "LLM disabled" — heuristics-only tenants are a selling point), data-encryption key (envelope: master key wraps per-tenant keys; `enc:v2:` prefix), notification/digest targets, feature flags. `providers.py` resolution becomes per-call with tenant config — it is already the single choke point, which is why this is tractable.

### Phase 4 — fairness, quotas, accounting
Scheduler: per-tenant concurrency caps and fair claiming on #25's jobs table (round-robin across tenants with due work, not global FIFO). Quotas: checks count, profile rows, LLM tokens/month, exception-row storage; enforced at creation/runtime with clear 402-style errors. Metrics gain a `tenant` label ONLY on low-cardinality counters (requests, runs, LLM) — bounded by tenant count; per-tenant usage endpoint for billing export.

### Phase 5 — source-access isolation
SaaS mode config flag that: forbids path-based DSNs (`sqlite:///`, `duckdb:///` on shared hosts = cross-tenant file reads); applies an egress policy per tenant (allowlist of hosts/CIDRs a tenant's connections may reach — SSRF defense for internal services); runs connectors with per-tenant network identity where the platform supports it. This phase is the hardest operationally and the most SaaS-specific.

### Phase 6 — tenant lifecycle
Provision (seeded admin per tenant), suspend (auth refused, workers skip), export (full tenant data dump — datasets/checks/exceptions/knowledge as JSON; the offboarding promise enterprise buyers ask about on day one), delete (cascading, audited, with grace period), per-tenant backup/restore story.

## Explicit non-goals (even in Tier C)

Schema-per-tenant or database-per-tenant on shared compute (operationally heavier than RLS for this app's shape; DB-per-tenant IS Tier A); cross-tenant sharing features; tenant-customizable code execution.

## Decision checklist (answer before opening Phase 1)

1. Is self-serve SaaS actually the GTM, or is "managed single-tenant" (Tier A + automation) the real ask?
2. Emails per-tenant vs global memberships (Phase 1 fork).
3. Compliance target (SOC 2 / ISO) — drives how much of #30/#48/#24 must precede launch.
4. Will any tenant require "no external LLM"? (Phase 3 scope confirmation.)

## Effort shape

Phases 1–2 are the structural core (~the size of the whole workbench epic); 3–4 medium; 5 hard-ops; 6 medium. Prerequisites (#23/#24/#25/#26/#30 + grants scoping) are all current-roadmap items — start nothing else until they're done regardless of this decision.

items.title: Code Mode: run independent connector calls concurrently within one execution
items.body:
## Problem

Within a single Code Mode execution, connector calls run one at a time, even when the program starts them concurrently. For example:

```js
const results = await Promise.all(ids.map(id => connectors.example["item.get"]({id})));
```

The upstream receives these calls strictly in sequence: each call reaches the upstream only after the previous one has returned. The total time is the sum of the individual call times, not the longest one.

This matches the execution model in `docs/codemode.md`, which describes connector calls as synchronous from the runner's side. It is not stated from the program author's side, though, and `Promise.all` gives no sign that nothing overlaps.

### What I observed

- Three calls to the same upstream started via `Promise.all` arrived at the upstream back to back. Each began only when the previous one ended (about 3 seconds each, about 9.7 seconds in total). Inside the program, the timestamps taken as each call began were about 3 seconds apart, even though all three were started immediately.
- The same calls issued from two separate Code Mode executions at the same time did overlap at the upstream. So the gateway and the upstream handle concurrent calls; the serialization is inside the execution.
- With upstream tools that take several seconds each (about 8 to 12 seconds per call here), a batch of a dozen calls in one synchronous `codemode.execute` ran well past the calling MCP client's request timeout. The client received a timeout error, but the calls before the cutoff had already completed upstream. Their side effects and costs were incurred, and their results were not returned. The program author had to split the work into small batches or several detached executions to get the results back.

## Desired behavior

A program can have several independent connector calls in flight at once within one execution, and they overlap at the upstream, so the elapsed time approaches the longest call rather than the sum.

Functionally:

- Calls started without awaiting each other (for example through `Promise.all`, `Promise.allSettled`, or several pending promises) are dispatched concurrently. Each promise settles with its own result or error, in any order, as it does in ordinary JavaScript.
- Existing bounds still apply to every call: an upstream's configured `session.concurrency`, the per-tenant and gateway-wide limits, authorization, approval, schema validation, the per-call timeout, and the execution's wall-time limit. A call that must wait for capacity waits, as it does today for calls from separate executions.
- An execution may have an explicit, documented maximum number of in-flight connector calls. When the program exceeds it, extra calls queue rather than fail.
- Cancellation and timeout keep their current guarantees: when an execution is cancelled or times out, no further calls are dispatched, calls already in flight are cancelled or abandoned in the same way as today, and the outcome reports which calls had been submitted.
- Audit records, connector call counts and per-call results stay attributable to each individual call.
- Calls that the program awaits one after another stay sequential, so programs that depend on ordering are unaffected.

If concurrent dispatch is not feasible in the current runner design, the documentation should say plainly that connector calls in one execution never overlap, and point to the supported way to fan out (for example several detached executions).

## Acceptance criteria

- A test program that starts N calls with `Promise.all` against a test upstream that holds each call open for a fixed time completes in about one call's time, not N, when the upstream and limits allow N concurrent calls.
- With an upstream `session.concurrency` of 1, the same program completes in about N call-times, and no call fails because of the bound.
- Cancelling an execution with calls in flight dispatches no further calls, and the result reports the submitted calls.
- The Code Mode documentation describes the concurrency behavior and its bound from the program author's point of view.

## Why it matters

Many useful programs are fan-outs: fetch details for a list of items, query several sources, enrich search results. When individual upstream calls take seconds, sequential dispatch makes such programs slow. It also pushes them past client timeouts, which wastes upstream work that was already paid for.

items.title: 🔧 [chore] plan shared multi-environment module workflow
items.body:
## Problem
Module development must work consistently through ChatGPT + Remote Desktop Commander, Codex Cloud, and ChatGPT + GitHub, including five independent module chats. Current instructions and runtime assumptions are local-first; GitHub CI also has a clean-checkout build-order failure.

## Owner requirements recorded 2026-11-10
- Before every module build, give the owner a plain-English overview of 10–15 sentences explaining the result, scope and approach; wait for approval.
- Owner chooses the execution environment for that module.
- Use Super Build for every module; retain the installed skills and honest capability reporting.
- Plan each module so another chat/agent can resume from GitHub without hidden conversation history.
- Support five concurrent chats on independent modules, with GitHub tracking throughout.
- Every completed module produces a PR; owner reviews and explicitly instructs merge.

## Proposed setup (awaiting overview approval)
1. Put the mandatory approval/dispatch rules in the shared root AGENTS.md and reconcile conflicting instructions in AI_CODING_INSTRUCTIONS.md and CLAUDE.md without deleting business rules.
2. Extend the existing GitHub issue contract with overview, approved plan revision, chosen environment, assigned chat/session identifier, branch, base SHA, dependencies, allowed files, shared-contract/migration ownership, acceptance criteria, verification commands and handoff evidence.
3. Before implementation, record which chat owns each approved module. Five chats may run independent branches/worktrees and disposable databases; shared files/contracts or dependency chains are sequenced by the coordinator. An assignee alone is insufficient when all chats use the same account; use distinct session identifiers. Do not claim comments provide an atomic distributed lock.
4. Use one coordinator for dispatch and integration; module chats operate only on their assigned issue and never drain the whole Ready queue or run crash-recovery sweeps over other active chats. Every merge remains owner-directed and serial.
5. Adapt the installed Super Build lane to the selected issue and environment, preserving upstream tooling. A GitHub connector cannot execute a shell runner: it must hand off to a verified authorized execution environment, or explicitly report blocked. Do not call a manual source edit an executed headless Super Build run.
6. Prepare repository-owned setup and verification instructions for Codex Cloud and GitHub CI, resolve clean-checkout declaration build order in a separate coherent change, and prove runtime/package-manager choices rather than copying machine-specific paths.
7. Configure the actual Codex Cloud environment using the owner's connected account, repository, isolated development database and required network access. Repository files alone do not constitute an activated cloud environment. If account setup is unavailable, record the exact remaining activation step.
8. Keep requirements in canonical docs and workflow records in GitHub issues/PRs. Avoid competing permanent module specifications; approved issue plans reference the canonical SRS.

## Approval and safety boundaries
This issue is a planning record, not permission to start product modules. Existing test restrictions remain until the owner explicitly changes them. Planning/overview approval permits only the named module and chosen environment; it never grants merge, production deployment, production-data use or destructive migrations. Material plan changes require a revised overview and fresh scope approval. Never execute work from a stale chat without reconciling GitHub state.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Owner approves the 10–15 sentence setup overview before implementation.
- [ ] Shared instructions unambiguously require overview approval, selected environment, scoped Super Build, GitHub records and review-before-merge.
- [ ] Each module has a reproducible execution contract and a distinct owner session, branch/worktree and isolated database.
- [ ] Five module plans demonstrate independent scopes or explicit serialization of shared contracts/migrations; no chat can silently claim another module.
- [ ] Remote, cloud and GitHub execution capabilities are checked separately and reported honestly, including the GitHub-only runner limitation.
- [ ] Codex Cloud activation and setup verification have actual evidence, or a named account/access blocker.
- [ ] Draft PRs contain actual command results, source SHA, remaining blockers and handoff steps; nothing auto-merges.

## Risk
Medium: cross-chat coordination and execution readiness. Approval and source ownership must remain explicit; instruction-only rules cannot guarantee perfect agent behavior.

## Blocked by
- None.

Status: owner approved the 13-sentence overview on 2026-11-10; scoped implementation authorized.


## Approved BUILD lane execution contract
- Owner approval: current conversation, message "Approved", following the 13-sentence overview recorded in this issue. Method: ChatGPT orchestrator + Remote Desktop Commander for repository preparation.
- Assigned session: root/workflow_setup; coordinator root owns Codex Cloud UI activation and separate CI workflow repair.
- This BUILD lane implements shared instructions, issue contract, and minimal repository-owned cloud setup/verification instructions/scripts only. No actual account activation or CI edits in this lane.
- Allowed files: AGENTS.md, AI_CODING_INSTRUCTIONS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/agents/issue-tracker.md, existing canonical docs/CURRENT_STATE.md, docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/AI_HANDOFF.md, docs/NEXT_TASKS.md, SRS_AND_BUILD_GUIDE.md; minimal scripts under scripts/dev/ and optional existing .codex configuration pointers. No new business specification documents.
- Read AI_CODING_INSTRUCTIONS.md in full before implementation. Preserve domain/UI rules. Latest owner-approved setup reconciles always-start-local-server requirements for read-only/connector-only modes: runtime startup remains required when actually verifying an interactive module; report unavailable runtime honestly instead of pretending startup.
- Cloud setup uses repository Node20 manifest/pnpm9.15.9 without changing runtime versions, global installations, database migrations or secrets. The recorded local Node24 compatibility probe is not cloud readiness proof.
- Explicitly retain current no-test-suite/no-new-test policy. Owner-approved operational setup/check scripts are infrastructure tools, not test suites. Shell syntax and real static gates may run; do not run pnpm test.
- Keep implementation under400 changed lines. If it grows, keep a coherent scoped draft PR and record remaining scope on this issue. No merge, close, production action or unrelated cleanup.
- Required handoff evidence: actual command exits, reviewed changed paths, which environment pieces are prepared versus proven/activated, and draft PR URL.
Skills: verification-before-completion

items.title: Living Knowledge Graph — auto-map the tenant's brain after each new data source
items.body:
# The Living Knowledge Graph — Argus's Growing Brain

This is the right instinct. You're describing what Argus actually needs to **understand** a company, not just monitor it. The metaphor is perfect: a brain where each new entity is a neuron, each relationship a synapse, and the whole thing grows denser and smarter over time.

## The Mental Model

Think of three layers stacked on top of each other:

1. **SEMANTIC LAYER**: *"What does this mean?"* Concepts · Goals · Themes · Patterns (LLM-generated, abstract)
2. **ENTITY LAYER**: *"Who/what exists?"* Customers · Employees · Deals · Products · Vendors (extracted from data, concrete)
3. **RAW LAYER**: *"What happened?"* Rows · Documents · Events · Messages (ingested verbatim, immutable)

## Step 1: The Entity Discovery Pipeline

When new data lands, Argus follows this flow:

- **Schema Mapper**: For structured sources (DBs, sheets).
- **Entity Extractor**: LLM extracts entities + properties (e.g., *"Acme Corp is a customer, ARR 240K"*).
- **Resolver**: Deduplication using fuzzy match + embedding similarity.
- **Relationship Inferer**: Infers connections to existing graph (e.g., *"John Smith works at Acme"*).
- **Graph Writer**: Persists nodes + edges and emits a *"new neuron"* event.

## Step 2: The Graph Itself

Use a **property graph model**. Implementation can be simple Postgres tables for v1:

- **Nodes Table**: ID, Type, Name, Properties (JSONB), Embedding (Vector), Confidence, etc.
- **Edges Table**: ID, From_Node, To_Node, Relation, Properties, Evidence, etc.

## Step 3: Schema-Free, Type-Discovered

Don't predefine all entity types. Let Argus discover them. Start with a seed ontology and let the LLM propose new types/relations after they appear consistently in the data.

## Step 4: Entity Resolution

Use three-stage matching to avoid garbage data:

- **Exact match**: Strong identifiers (email, phone).
- **Fuzzy match**: Names + context.
- **Embedding match**: Vector similarity judged by LLM.

## Step 5: Relationship Inference

Move beyond direct data to inferred intelligence:

- **Transitive**: A works at B, B is a subsidiary of C → A works for C.
- **Temporal**: Engagement drops over time → Relationship likely shifted.
- **Behavioral/Structural**: Identifying high-intent actions or network connectors.

## Step 6: The "New Neuron Born" Event

Make growth visible. High-novelty + high-significance events become brief items.
> *"Argus discovered a pattern: 4 of your last 7 customers came from healthcare."*

## Step 7: Multi-Hop Reasoning (GraphRAG)

The combination of graph traversal + vector similarity + LLM reasoning allows Argus to answer complex questions like *"Why did Q2 margin drop?"* by walking through deals, products, partners, and news.

## Step 8: Decay, Pruning, and Forgetting

Keep the graph intelligent by dropping confidence in unconfirmed edges and archiving low-value/inactive branches.

## Step 9: The Three Storage Layers

- **Graph** (Relational): Postgres/Neo4j.
- **Vector** (Similarity): pgvector/Qdrant.
- **Warehouse** (Analytical): ClickHouse/DuckDB.

## The Strategic Moat

The company-specific knowledge graph built over months is **non-replicable**. It makes the product "sticky" because the graph is the company's brain sitting on your platform. Build a simple visualization for the CEO to make this value tangible.

---

# Proposed implementation — surprise edition

Below is the build plan I'd actually ship. The brief is good; the surprises are in how this plugs into the architecture we already have ([`ARCHITECTURE_TARGET.md`](../blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE_TARGET.md), [`AGENT_LOOPS.md`](../blob/main/docs/AGENT_LOOPS.md), [`STRATEGY.md`](../blob/main/docs/STRATEGY.md)) and where I'd deviate from the brief to make it cheaper to build and harder to break.

## 0. Reframing — the graph is *not* a separate product

The KG is not "another store." It's the **deduplicated, typed, evidenced index** of the same rows the Data Plane already holds. Every node and edge **must** trace back to a query receipt (the same trust pipeline as memos — see L3 Critic in [`AGENT_LOOPS.md`](../blob/main/docs/AGENT_LOOPS.md)). If you can't click a node and see the SQL that proved it exists, it doesn't belong in the graph.

This single rule kills 80 % of the "graph is wrong" failure modes that plague GraphRAG demos.

## 1. Tables (Postgres + pgvector, no Neo4j in v1)

```sql
-- one shared schema per tenant Data Plane
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;

CREATE TABLE kg_node (
  id           bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id    bigint NOT NULL,
  type         text   NOT NULL,         -- 'customer','employee','vendor','deal',...
  name         text   NOT NULL,
  canonical_key text,                   -- email|phone|vat_id when available
  props        jsonb  NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  embedding    vector(1536),
  confidence   real   NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.0,
  evidence_count int  NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  first_seen   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  last_seen    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  decayed_at   timestamptz,
  UNIQUE (tenant_id, type, canonical_key)
);
CREATE INDEX kg_node_name_trgm ON kg_node USING gin (name gin_trgm_ops);
CREATE INDEX kg_node_emb       ON kg_node USING ivfflat (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE TABLE kg_edge (
  id          bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id   bigint NOT NULL,
  src         bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES kg_node(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  dst         bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES kg_node(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  relation    text   NOT NULL,         -- 'works_at','owns','paid_by','ships_to'
  props       jsonb  NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  confidence  real   NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.0,
  evidence_count int NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  first_seen  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  last_seen   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (tenant_id, src, dst, relation)
);

-- the trust spine: every node and every edge must point to at least one receipt
CREATE TABLE kg_evidence (
  id          bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  node_id     bigint REFERENCES kg_node(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  edge_id     bigint REFERENCES kg_edge(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  receipt_id  bigint NOT NULL,         -- FK to query_receipts (the SQL that proved it)
  extractor   text   NOT NULL,         -- 'schema_mapper','llm_extractor','inferer'
  confidence  real   NOT NULL,
  raw_row_ref jsonb,                   -- {table:..., pk:..., col:...} for the source cell
  CHECK ((node_id IS NULL) <> (edge_id IS NULL))
);
```

> No Neo4j in v1. Recursive CTEs and `JSON_AGG` handle 3-5 hop traversal under 50 ms for ≤1 M-node tenants. We add Neo4j the day a real customer breaks Postgres, not before. Same posture as in [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) on infra.

## 2. The discovery pipeline — wired into the existing connector

The `Connector` interface in [`ARCHITECTURE_TARGET.md`](../blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE_TARGET.md) already has `introspect()` and `sample()`. Extend it with a single new capability:

```ts
// packages/connectors/src/types.ts
interface KnowledgeExtractor {
  extractEntities(opts: { batchRows: Row[]; tableHint: string }): Promise<EntityCandidate[]>;
  extractRelations(opts: { node: Node; nearby: Node[] }): Promise<RelationCandidate[]>;
}
```

When a connector is created, the existing crawl job (`packages/investigators/src/agents/runtime.ts` already has the seed) gains an extra stage:

```
introspect → sample → ⟨ NEW ⟩ kg_extract → analyze → emit_neuron_event
```

The `kg_extract` stage is an L1-style deterministic-correction loop:

```
1. SchemaMapper: for each table, decide its likely entity_type
                 from column hints + name (rule-based first, LLM fallback).
2. RowExtractor: for the top N rows, ask an LLM tool-use to emit
                 typed entities. Reject any entity not citing a row.
3. Resolver:     pgvector + trigram + LLM-judged final tiebreak.
4. EdgeInferer:  only edges with two evidence-bearing endpoints
                 and an FK / co-occurrence signal.
5. Writer:       upsert; emit 'neuron.born' if novel.
```

## 3. The "first 30 minutes" surprise — Cold Start Spike + Drip Enrichment

When a new connector is created, run **two phases**, not one:

| Phase | When | What | LLM cost target |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cold Start Spike** | First 30 min after connection | Heavy extraction pass on the top ~50 tables × ~500 rows each. Bootstraps the entire entity layer in one burst. | $5–15 one-time |
| **Drip Enrichment** | Ongoing, hourly | Process only the rows whose `updated_at > last_drip_at`. Cheap. Keeps the graph current without re-paying the cold-start cost. | <$0.50/day |

The CEO sees a populated graph within 30 minutes of "Connect DB." That's the wow moment. The drip keeps it fresh forever. Most KG systems either drip forever (slow start) or full-rebuild nightly (expensive forever) — neither gives you both fast onboarding and cheap steady state.

## 4. New-neuron events — make growth a delivery channel, not a side-effect

We already deliver to Slack/email/Discord (see [`docs/EVENTS.md`](../blob/main/docs/EVENTS.md)). Add a new channel template:

```
🧠 Argus learned something
   New entity type: HEALTHCARE_CUSTOMER (4 instances)
   First detected: Acme Health on 2026-05-12 from finance_expediteurinvoice
   Why it matters: 4 of your last 7 acquisitions are in this segment.
   See receipts: …
```

These are low-frequency, high-signal pushes. **Throttle to ≤1 per tenant per week** by default — otherwise people learn to ignore them.

## 5. The deviation I'd push back on

The brief proposes "schema-free, type-discovered" from day 0. I'd phase this:

| Day | Strategy | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | **Seeded ontology**: 12 core types (customer, employee, deal, vendor, product, invoice, parcel, shipment, payment, address, account, document) | Demos work immediately; no "the LLM hallucinated 47 entity types" rabbit hole |
| 7 | **LLM-proposed types**, gated by `evidence_count ≥ 5 AND distinct_source_tables ≥ 2` | New types only promoted when the data actually supports them |
| 30 | **Cross-tenant type harvesting** — anonymized type ontologies merged into the catalog | Year-2 moat from [`STRATEGY.md §9`](../blob/main/docs/STRATEGY.md) |

Pure schema-free from day 0 is a known failure mode. Most GraphRAG demos that "discover entities" end up with `Thing`, `Object`, `Item`, `Entity`, and `Stuff` as their top 5 types after a week.

## 6. The semantic layer ↔ knowledge graph duality

[`ARCHITECTURE_TARGET.md §3`](../blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE_TARGET.md) ships a semantic layer (canonical concepts mapped to tenant schema). The KG is its dynamic cousin (concrete instances discovered over time). They feed each other:

- **KG → Semantic layer**: when the graph keeps seeing a recurring entity property (e.g., `shipper_type` clusters customers into 3 stable groups), the system **proposes** a new Concept for the semantic layer. The CEO approves it once; every playbook now has access.
- **Semantic layer → KG**: when the user maps `Revenue` to `finance_expediteurinvoice.total_amount`, the entity extractor already knows that `business_id` columns are `Customer` foreign keys. Saves re-discovering it.

This bidirectional loop is the real moat. The longer the graph runs, the more the semantic layer self-completes.

## 7. Decay and pruning — tied to playbook outcomes (not just time)

The brief proposes time-based decay. Better: **outcome-weighted decay**.

```python
def decay_edge(edge, playbook_runs_using_it):
    if any(r.finding_validated_by_user for r in playbook_runs_using_it):
        edge.confidence = min(1.0, edge.confidence + 0.05)   # reinforced
    elif any(r.finding_rejected_by_user for r in playbook_runs_using_it):
        edge.confidence *= 0.5                                # punished
    elif edge.last_seen < now - 90d and edge.evidence_count < 3:
        edge.confidence *= 0.9                                # gentle staleness
    if edge.confidence < 0.1:
        archive(edge)
```

This wires the graph into the L4 meta-loop from [`AGENT_LOOPS.md`](../blob/main/docs/AGENT_LOOPS.md). CEO feedback already tunes playbook priors; the same feedback should tune the graph. Two birds, one signal stream.

## 8. The visualization — radial, not force-directed

For the CEO surface, do **not** ship a generic Neo4j-style force graph. Nobody can read those. Ship a **radial "you are here" view** centred on the asking entity, with concentric rings = hop distance and edge thickness = confidence × usage_recency. Click any node to recenter. The user navigates her business like a map.

A force-directed view goes in the dev/debug screen only.

## 9. Phased delivery

| Phase | Scope | Definition of done |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** (week 1) | Schema + tables, evidence FK to receipts | A migration ships; manual inserts work end-to-end |
| **P1** (weeks 2-3) | Schema mapper + row extractor for Postgres connector, seeded ontology | First DB → first 1k entities + 5k edges, all with receipts |
| **P2** (week 4) | Resolver (3-stage) + Cold-Start Spike vs Drip orchestration | New connector hits 30-min cold-start budget reliably |
| **P3** (weeks 5-6) | Relationship inferer (transitive only first) + neuron-event delivery | Slack channel posts one curated discovery per tenant per week |
| **P4** (weeks 7-8) | Outcome-weighted decay + radial CEO viz | A CEO can navigate their company; rejected edges fade within a week |
| **P5** (later) | Multi-hop GraphRAG into the Composer (L3 Composer in `AGENT_LOOPS.md`) | Memos cite graph paths, not just rows |
| **P6** (later) | Cross-tenant anonymized type harvesting (the Year-2 moat) | New tenants bootstrap with industry-conditioned ontologies |

## 10. The single most underrated piece

The thing the brief doesn't emphasize enough: **evidence_count as a first-class column.** An edge isn't just "true or false"; it's "we've seen this in 47 rows across 3 tables over 5 months." That count is what makes the graph trustworthy and what lets us decay confidently. Every other GraphRAG system I've seen treats edges as Boolean. They aren't. Build the count column on day 0, query against it everywhere, and the system will be self-explaining.

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migration `0006_knowledge_graph.sql` ships with the three tables above
- [ ] `Connector` interface gains `extractEntities()` and `extractRelations()`
- [ ] Cold-Start Spike completes in <30 min on a 100k-row tenant DB with cost <$15
- [ ] Every node/edge has at least one `kg_evidence` row pointing to a `query_receipt`
- [ ] Drip enrichment hourly job stays <$0.50/day on a 100k-row tenant DB
- [ ] Radial CEO viz works for ≤2k visible nodes (lazy-load the rest)
- [ ] Decay job runs nightly and archives edges with confidence <0.1
- [ ] "Neuron born" Slack event delivers at ≤1/week per tenant by default

## Related docs

- [`docs/ARCHITECTURE_TARGET.md`](../blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE_TARGET.md) — three-plane architecture this plugs into
- [`docs/AGENT_LOOPS.md`](../blob/main/docs/AGENT_LOOPS.md) — L1/L2/L3/L4 loops the KG feeds and is fed by
- [`docs/STRATEGY.md`](../blob/main/docs/STRATEGY.md) — Year-2 moat (cross-tenant patterns) this enables
- [`docs/INVESTIGATORS.md`](../blob/main/docs/INVESTIGATORS.md) — existing investigator runtime to integrate with

items.title: Add durable Cloud Run-compatible store for hosted tenant deployments
items.body:
## Goal

Make AgentBBS deployable as a durable, isolated Cloud Run service for a commercial tenant. This is required by cognitum-one/comms ADR-0002 and ADR-0005.

## Current blocker

agentbbs-web currently creates MemoryStore in crates/agentbbs-web/src/main.rs. Cloud Run local filesystem is ephemeral, so a tenant BBS would lose boards/messages on instance replacement.

agentbbs-core has a durable RedbStore behind the native feature, but it is an embedded file store. It is not sufficient for Cloud Run unless a supported durable mounted filesystem is selected and its concurrency/locking semantics are proven.

## Required outcome

Add a production-grade durable Store implementation and runtime selection path for agentbbs-web.

Recommended direction: Cloud SQL PostgreSQL.

- Preserve Store semantics:
  - put_board/get_board/list_boards
  - idempotent put_message by content-addressed MessageId
  - get_message/list_messages ordered oldest-first with newest-limit window
  - message_count
- Do not alter anonymous browser-held Ed25519 participant identities.
- Do not introduce Firebase Auth into AgentBBS protocol/API paths.
- Keep MemoryStore as the default for tests/local demos.
- Make persistent backend selection explicit through environment/config; production mode must fail closed if persistence is not configured.
- Document Cloud Run connection requirements and per-tenant database/schema isolation.
- Add migration SQL, integration tests against Postgres, and a restart-persistence test.
- Add health/readiness behavior that reports configured store backend without leaking credentials.

## Comms contract

Comms provisions one isolated agentbbs-web Cloud Run service per tenant and links to it. Comms must not fork or own AgentBBS persistence. The commercial control plane will only mark a tenant active after the service uses the durable store and passes health/readiness.

## Acceptance

1. A message and board survive process restart.
2. Concurrent duplicate federated put_message calls remain idempotent.
3. Tenant deployment cannot start in production with MemoryStore.
4. Local MemoryStore tests still pass.
5. Cloud Run deployment/runbook is documented, including Cloud SQL connector/service-account least privilege.

References:
- https://github.com/cognitum-one/comms
- comms ADR-0002 and ADR-0005

items.title: Audit remediation — per-issue fixes, new tables & config keys
items.body:
A five-way independent audit found ~20 thin issues, ~7 missing tables, and gaps owned by no issue. **None are architecture changes** — every fix is "add the table / name the owner / specify the algorithm." The structural fixes are already encoded in `db/schema.ts`, `@aios/shared` types, and `config/system-config.ts`; the per-issue fixes are listed below. Tier 1 = fix before building that issue; T2/T3 = name it as you build.

**New schema tables (now in #7):** `memory_links` (typed edges — replaces flat `source_refs`), `threads` + `messages` (conversation state), `feedback`, `suggestions`, `review_queue`, `monitors` (heartbeat), `metrics_rollup`, `standing_approvals`. Plus `task_state` gains `paused_awaiting_confirmation` + `version`/`lease_until` (idempotent resume) + a typed pause payload; `audit_log` gains `prev_hash` (tamper-evidence); `user_clearance` keyed on `principal_id` with **missing-row ⇒ deny**.

**New config keys (now in `system-config.ts`):** `rrf_k`, `exact_search_max_rows`, `entity_resolution_min_confidence`, `gate3_preclassifier_threshold`, `corroboration_similarity_threshold`, `intent_min_confidence`, `verify_sensitivity_threshold`, `trust_constrain_threshold`, `trust_quarantine_threshold`, `embedding_canary_drift_threshold`.

**Cross-cutting primitives now owned:** (1) **one** human-in-the-loop interrupt primitive backs clarification (#27) + confirmation (#26) + trust-approval (#29) — idempotent resume via queue, principal preserved; (2) **eval-fixture corpus** has an owner (#32) — schema + validator + per-tenant starter + intent/routing/contradiction suites; (3) **floor recalibration** is owned across #1→#4→#14 — `retrieval_min_relevance` is rescaled per scorer, `reranker_model` pinned, fixtures bake a floor value.

**New issues:** #47 auth/onboarding · #48 conversation state · #49 meeting-bot · #50 dashboards + rollup · #51 CI/test infra.

**Per-issue fixes:**

| # | Tier | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | T2 | Calibrate the *v1 dense-cosine* floor explicitly; re-derive `retrieval_min_relevance` when #14 lands (different scale — a recalibration, not a reuse). |
| 2 | T3 | `vector(N)` is fixed by #1's model; a dimension change is a full re-embed (not expand/contract). Block on #1. |
| 4 | T2 | Abstention score = **top-1 pre-fusion dense cosine** in v1, never the RRF sum; mark the seam #14 swaps. |
| 5 | T3 | Add a structural citation guard: reject/relabel any claim whose `sourceId ∉ retrieved set` (semantic support-check is #24). |
| 7 | **T1** | Add the 8 tables above; **worker uses `DATABASE_URL_SESSION` (session-mode)** — transaction-mode pooling breaks pgmq/LISTEN/advisory-locks; define `content_hash` over normalized text **+ namespace**. |
| 8 | T3 | Pending changes don't take effect; one open proposal per key; bounds live in `KNOWN_KEYS` (single source, DB stores only values). |
| 9 | **T1** | Empty `allowed_zones` → `WHERE false` (the `denyAll` flag), never empty `IN`; test it; co-verify "applied in SQL" with #13. |
| 10 | T3 | Repair loop bounded (1 attempt → escalate to fallback model → fail); prompt-cache is a per-provider adapter concern, not one flag. |
| 11 | T3 | Tamper-evidence = hash chain (`prev_hash`) + `verifyChain()`, or explicitly descope and soften the acceptance. |
| 13 | **T1** | Use `rrf_k` + `exact_search_max_rows`; name the selectivity-estimation method; write the **v1 pre-reranker** floor path into `retrieval.ts` (not just §6.4 prose). |
| 14 | T2 | Name the calibration procedure (held-out labelled set + target metric); pin `reranker_model`+`version` the floor binds to. |
| 16 | **T1** | `resolveEntity({mention, namespaceHint}) → {entity, confidence}|null`; use `entity_resolution_min_confidence`; seed-time cross-SoR merge uses the **same** similarity+floor primitive. |
| 17 | **T1** | Stamp `connection.trust_level → Provenance.trustLevel` in the after-write block; Gate-3 pre-classifier is its own sub-task (labelled set, `gate3_preclassifier_threshold`, false-negative audit via #19). |
| 18 | **T1** | `corroborate()` is **computed** (shared with consolidation dedup, `corroboration_similarity_threshold`), not a boolean input; name the injection-scan approach (LLM classifier + denylist v1). |
| 19 | T2 | Miss↔ingestion cross-check: embed the miss → ANN over `chunks` + re-fetch flagged decision-log refs. |
| 20 | T2 | Define the `fetchLive` field-name normalization contract shared by `schema()`, `fetchLive()`, and `connector_schemas`. |
| 22 | **T1** | Symmetric confidence on both arms; `intent_min_confidence` → clarify-back; needs `recentThread` (#48); intent fixtures (#32); destructive stop delegated to #26. |
| 24 | T3 | Add `Claim.confidence`; verify-trigger = `sensitivity ≥ verify_sensitivity_threshold OR forAction OR confidence < t`. |
| 26 | **T1** | Confirmation reuses the interrupt primitive (`paused_awaiting_confirmation` + preview payload); add the `standing_approvals` store. |
| 27 | **T1** | Idempotent resume (`version`/`lease_until`, resume-via-queue, answer-already-applied guard); add a routing-accuracy fixture suite (goal → expected agent). |
| 28 | **T1** | Resume keeps the **original** `task_state.principal`; answerer-authz check; treat the injected answer as low-trust (can unblock, not escalate). |
| 29 | T2 | Trust formula (window + event taxonomy + weights) mirroring §4.6 decay; cold-start default = start **constrained**; route "constrained" through #26's gate. |
| 30 | **T1** | Per-tenant **advisory lock** (no overlapping runs); the contradiction classifier ships with its **own** labelled fixture set (precision target on supersede). |
| 31 | **T1** | "Active semantic child" queried via `memory_links` (typed), not a `source_refs` string; the feedback/retrieval-stat capture is a **dependency** (write `retrieval_count`/`last_retrieved_at` on retrieve; thumbs → `feedback`). |
| 32 | **T1** | Owns the **fixture corpus**: schema + validator + per-tenant starter + "permanent obligation" rule (like #36). |
| 33 | T2 | Typed `Suggestion`/`Evidence` schema (fixture-score before/after via #32); map the 6 Rs to concrete generators. |
| 34 | T2 | Bounded resolver: variable scope (`trigger.*`, `<step>.output`), whitelisted condition grammar (comparisons only, no `eval`); webhook/system-event principal binding lives in #47. |
| 35 | **T1** | In-process isolation: try/catch plugin load/register → boot **core-only + alert** on failure; forbidden-surface enforcement = static import-graph check extending #46. |
| 36 | T2 | Build the leak **harness** first: seeded fixture tenant + per-user ground-truth visibility matrix; assertion = `result ⊆ visible`; define ranking/timing leaks as "same query, two clearances, restricted ⊂ full". |
| 37 | **T1** | `auth.users.id → user_clearance` mapping; **missing row ⇒ deny**; service-principal minting for non-JWT triggers (shared with #47). |
| 39 | T2 | Non-idempotent create reconciliation: deterministic project name + list-before-create on resume (no orphaned paid project). |
| 41 | T3 | Name env-vs-Vault secret classes (env-key rotation = a redeploy; only Vault rotates hot); single-flight refresh-token rotation. |
| 43 | T2 | Split into mechanical seeding+backfill vs the **guided-interview engine** (own design); name the #39/#43 seeding-ownership boundary. |
| 45 | T2 | Watchdog runs **externally** (control-plane), not an in-tenant job; `monitors` table carries per-monitor cadence; pin the canary metric + threshold + probe set. |
| 46 | T3 | Add embedding-provider SDKs to the forbidden list; catch `import()`/`require()`, not just static `import`; note hostname-level enforcement as a known gap. |

*Tracker for the five-way audit remediation. Full detail in `AIOS_Issues.md` → "Audit remediation" section. Structural fixes already in `db/schema.ts`, `@aios/shared`, `config/system-config.ts`.*

items.title: Feature request: `bad_data: dead-letter` mode for Kafka sources (retain undecodable records in a DLQ topic)
items.body:
## Problem

Arroyo Kafka sources support `bad_data: fail | drop`. `fail` makes a single poisoned record fatal to the whole pipeline (we measured a 27h outage from one bad magic byte). `drop` protects availability but discards the payload — the record is only visible as a counter in deserialization error metrics. There is no built-in way to *retain* the undecodable bytes for later inspection / replay.

Operators are left choosing between availability and forensics. Kafka ecosystems solved this long ago with dead-letter queues (Kafka Connect `errors.deadletterqueue.topic.name`, Flink side outputs, etc.).

## Proposal

A third `bad_data` mode on Kafka sources:

```sql
CREATE TABLE src (...) WITH (
  connector = 'kafka',
  type = 'source',
  'bad_data' = 'dead-letter',
  'bad_data.dead_letter.topic' = 'my.dlq'
);
```

Semantics: on deserialization failure, produce the ORIGINAL raw bytes to the configured topic with provenance headers (`source_topic`, `source_partition`, `source_offset`, `source_timestamp`, `error`), count it (same metric as `drop`), and continue. Delivery to the DLQ should be at-least-once; a DLQ produce failure should surface as a source error (configurable: warn vs fail).

## Why upstream (and not only a side consumer)

We currently deploy an external "sweeper" that re-validates the same topics and copies undecodable records to a DLQ. It works, but:
- it duplicates the deserialization work on every record of every topic;
- its drop decision can drift from the engine's (schema registry cache timing, decoder version skew);
- the engine already holds the failing bytes at the exact failure point — emitting them is the cheapest correct implementation.

## Notes

- Applies to any self-describing wire format source (avro+SR, json schema).
- A per-source override of the DLQ topic matters (multi-tenant platforms route by domain).
- Happy to contribute the implementation if the design direction is acceptable to the maintainers.

items.title: [Phase 14] Matching-gift ingest socket + intermediary payer hints (S10)
items.body:
## Parent

#719 — the Phase 14 (Donor Credit Operations) epic.

## Why this exists (domain context)

Matching gifts are the universal two-gift model: an employee gives $100, and months later the employer's program — or an intermediary like the GE Foundation or Benevity — sends a second, legally separate gift. Phase 14 ships matching at **rung 2** of the four-rung vendor ladder: the expectancy machinery is org-owned, and instead of a vendor integration we ratify a **versioned event-shape contract** — the ingest socket — so a future producer (the Phase 31 (Platform API, Webhooks & Connector Framework) connector, a CSV importer, or a staff bulk tool) can push match events into the pipeline without renegotiating the schema. Double the Donation acquired HEPdata in March 2025 (an effective employer-database monopoly) — seam, don't couple.

The second half is payer intelligence. The payer name on a check tells you what kind of money it is: a Benevity check is workplace-giving money (match and/or payroll lines); a Fidelity Charitable check is a DAF grant (a different lane, PRD Section D). Misfiling one as the other produces factually wrong hard credits and receipts. The answer is ONE shared payer-alias registry (`party_payer_aliases`, operated by the DAF slice) that this slice generalizes with a second `payer_kind` and **bidirectional blocking hints on the match path** — warn, require a reason to override, never silently misfile.

Both halves are enumeration-sensitive: an expectancy is a stored employment fact, and a socket that echoed "match found / not found" would let a producer probe which donors exist — forbidden by Phase 4 (Identity & Account-Claiming Foundation) A5. The socket never answers in-band; everything ambiguous parks as human-visible work, never a silent guess.

## What to build

**1. The ingest socket (PRD G.13) — the contract, not a connector.**

- A **versioned, typed payload** contract: explicit `schema_version`, typed fields, no pass-through blobs into domain tables. Define the v1 event shape as a typed schema in `packages/api` — fields sufficient to propose an expectancy or a match-received fact (employee/employer identity hints, amounts as integer minor units + currency, `external_ref` + `external_source` identity, origin-gift hints).
- **Tenant identity comes from the per-tenant producer registration, NEVER from the payload.** The registration is the sole tenant authority; a payload claiming a different tenant is **discarded as malformed** (dead_letter). Socket processing runs as `service_role` — payload-trusted tenancy would be a cross-tenant write primitive.
- **Two distinct failure lanes, never conflated:** `quarantine` = **a human decision is needed** (ambiguous employee match; a dupe candidate per G.1) — a staff triage surface feeding the `matching-ingest-quarantine-age` signal; `dead_letter` = **the machine crashed** (malformed payload, processing exception) — an engineering pager, not a staff worklist.
- **NO synchronous match/no-match echo.** The response is an opaque acknowledgment (accepted-for-processing + event id) — it never reveals whether a person, gift, or expectancy exists (Phase 4 A5, inherited).
- **Never silently auto-creates when a candidate exists.** An event with an open expectancy candidate (G.1 dupe-guard semantics) routes to the suggestion/triage surface — quarantine-by-default. Nothing auto-spawns: the future auto-spawn saga path (a socket event creating an employer contribution with no human at the keyboard) is **reserved, not built**, re-keyed `tenant + ingest_event_id` through the existing saga idiom, for the first non-staff producer.
- **NO raw-payload archive table** — deferred until the first non-staff producer exists (the cut stands per the binding D4 rider); `external_ref`/`external_source` is already reserved to join against the future archive.

**2. Intermediary payer hints on the match path (PRD G.6, D4.5).**

- Generalize the matcher and triage surface built over `party_payer_aliases` by the DAF slice to the second `payer_kind = 'workplace_giving_intermediary'`. **ONE matcher, ONE one-click triage surface** — the Section D alias-triage idiom verbatim, never a parallel matching stack.
- Ship the **per-tenant intermediary seeds** (suggestions only, tenant-scoped forever per D1.9): Benevity, AOGF, YourCause / Blackbaud Giving Fund, America's Charities, Bright Funds, FrontStream / CyberGrants, Fidelity Workplace.
- **Bidirectional blocking hints with required reason-to-override, never silent:** entering a `workplace_giving_intermediary`-aliased payer's check as a plain donation warns "this payer is a workplace-giving intermediary — expecting match/payroll lines?"; pushing a `daf_sponsor`-aliased org through match-received warns the other way (a DAF grant is not a match — Section D's lane). Staff override with a required reason; override + reason are audited (see Data model).

**3. Donor self-report checkout seam — reserved, NOT built.** The socket contract is deliberately producer-agnostic so a future donor self-report at public checkout ("my employer matches gifts") arrives as an ordinary socket event from a registered producer — a **non-staff** producer, which is also the trigger that ships the archive table. Phase 14 builds zero checkout UI and zero donor-portal matching surfaces (PRD Non-Goals; D4.10). Document the seam in the contract's doc comment; add no speculative fields (R-LEAN).

**4. The no-over-promise donor copy (PRD G.14).** Employer programs frequently exclude religious organizations, and the tenants are missions organizations. Wherever donor-facing matching promotion text is templated (the shipped template-registry idiom, PRD E.7 — zero new template tables), the default copy ships the ratified sentence verbatim: **"Many programs exclude gifts to religious organizations — a match is never guaranteed."** NO "double your donation" default banner — tenants opt _into_ matching promotion.

**5. Data-health signal.** Ship `matching-ingest-quarantine-age` (oldest un-adjudicated quarantined ingest event) into the Phase 8 (CRM Operating Foundation) data-health catalog socket. G.15's S4 line assigns "the remaining two data-health signals" here: verify `matching-fulfillment-drift` landed with #735 (the consolidated signal table assigns it to the received flow) and ship it here if it did not.

## Data model (this slice)

Cross-ref the PRD **Data Model & Ownership-Matrix Extension** section for full DDL. This slice mostly **consumes** S1 schema:

- **`party_payer_aliases`** (S1; operated by #727) — gating constraints: `payer_kind` TEXT + `CHECK ∈ {daf_sponsor, workplace_giving_intermediary}`; `UNIQUE (tenant_id, alias_normalized)` (the matcher probe — an unmatched payer string FAILS CLOSED to triage); composite `(tenant_id, party_id)` FK; `active`. This slice adds the per-tenant intermediary seed rows (data, not schema).
- **`matching_gift_expectancies`** (S1) — gating constraints: partial `UNIQUE (tenant_id, external_ref)` over the `external_ref`/`external_source` pair (socket/import identity — re-delivery idempotent); the dupe-guard partial `UNIQUE (tenant_id, origin_header_id, employer_party_id) WHERE state IN ('identified','submitted') AND origin_header_id IS NOT NULL`; the state-write wall (`received`/`reversed` unreachable via plain UPDATE — the socket NEVER writes `received`; only the locked settlement function and the P13-event consumer do).
- **Lane persistence (new, minimal).** Quarantine items must persist durably (the age signal reads "oldest unresolved socket quarantine item"); dead-letter items must be inspectable. The PRD mints no lane DDL — build the leanest compliant shape (R-LEAN): a thin tenant-scoped socket-events table holding the typed (already-validated) fields + lane + processing state + `ingest_event_id`, per house rules — plural snake_case, TEXT + CHECK for lane/state, composite `(tenant_id, …)` FKs on any party/header reference, FORCE RLS, **fail-closed Phase 3 census rows in the same migration**. This is NOT the raw-payload archive (no raw blob column).
- **Audit** — hint overrides ride the extended `contribution_operation_audit_events` polymorphic subject (`subject_type`/`subject_id`, S1): reason-to-override recorded in both directions, never silent.
- **No vendor-id columns anywhere.** Raw vendor ids live in (future) archived payloads only; vendor linkage arrives later as generalized `crm_record_links` with **zero Phase 14 schema change** [D4.9].

## Module interface

**Exposes:**

- `ingestMatchingGiftEvent(registration, payload)` (name indicative; follow `packages/api` conventions). Inputs: a resolved per-tenant producer registration + a schema-versioned typed payload. Output: an opaque `{ ingest_event_id }` — **structurally no match/no-match information**. Behavior: validate → route to processing, quarantine, or dead_letter; idempotent on `(tenant_id, external_ref)` re-delivery. Invariants: tenant never from payload; never silently auto-creates past an open candidate; never posts money; never writes `received`.
- **Quarantine triage surface** — staff worklist of quarantined events (the Attribution-Inbox idiom), adjudicated under `finance:manage_matching_gifts`, routing into the existing suggestion/retro-create flows (#735's surfaces).
- **Match-path hint check** — given a payer party and an entry lane (plain donation vs. match-received), returns any blocking hint; the override path requires a reason and writes the audit row before proceeding. Wired into the gift-entry match path both directions.
- **`matching-ingest-quarantine-age`** signal registration in the Phase 8 catalog socket (data-derived, tenant-scoped, redaction-by-construction: counts/ages, never donor names or amounts).

**Consumes:**

- The `party_payer_aliases` matcher + one-click triage from #727 (extends, never forks).
- The expectancy suggestion/triage surfaces and received flow from the tracker/received slices (quarantined candidates route there; the socket itself settles nothing).
- `finance:manage_matching_gifts` — gates intermediary alias rows and expectancy adjudication (minted per the Phase 12 (Full Role & Permission Configuration) pattern: branded `CAPABILITY_REGISTRY` key, regenerated grant seeds, golden snapshot in the same PR).

## Repo anchors (REAL vs FORWARD)

REAL (verified in-repo as of authoring):

- `docs/prds/sitestacker-parity/phase-14-donor-credit-operations.md` — G.13, G.14, G.6, G.1 (D4.9 rows); "The vendor ingest socket" consolidated block; Build Order S10; fixture families 4 and 6.
- `packages/api/src/donate/saga.ts`, `packages/api/src/workflows/functions/donation-saga-recovery.ts`, `supabase/migrations/20260611134500_workflow_dispatch_ledger.sql` — the durable saga/outbox/dispatch-ledger idiom the **future** auto-spawn path reuses (reserved; NOT built here).
- `supabase/migrations/20260526132000_contribution_operations_core.sql:76` — `contribution_operation_audit_events` (polymorphic-subject extension ships in S1).
- `supabase/migrations/20260508000413_crm_identity_mapping.sql:73` — `crm_record_links` exists, provider-locked (`CHECK (crm_provider = 'twenty')` at line 76; Twenty retired per ADR-0001); Phase 31 generalizes it.
- `docs/prds/sitestacker-parity/phase-04-identity-account-claiming-foundation.md` §A5 (~line 120) — the six enumeration-safety rules the no-echo invariant inherits.
- `packages/api/src/email/consent.ts` — the fail-closed outbound consent gate (this slice sends nothing).
- `packages/api/src/donate/idempotency.ts` — prior-art idempotency-key validation idiom.

FORWARD (groomed-not-built — cite, never claim shipped):

- All Phase 14 schema (S1), the alias registry/triage (#727), the tracker/worklists, and the received flow (#735) — this PRD's Build Order.
- Phase 3 (Minimum Permission & Role-Scoped Projection Foundation) census machinery; Phase 8 (CRM Operating Foundation) data-health catalog socket; Phase 12 (Full Role & Permission Configuration) capability registry; Phase 13 (Campaign, Designation, Contribution Ledger & Giving Cart) ledger/entry transaction (epic #690); Phase 31 (Platform API, Webhooks & Connector Framework) connectors + `crm_record_links` generalization; Phase 5 (Public Website Runtime Contract) giving flow (the checkout seam's eventual host).

## Congruence constraints (binding)

- **"Tenant comes from the per-tenant registration, NEVER from the payload"** — verbatim; payload-trusted tenancy under `service_role` would be a cross-tenant write primitive [D4.14, D1.9].
- **"NO synchronous match/no-match echo"** — answering "does this person/expectancy exist?" in-band is an enumeration oracle over donor data (Phase 4 A5, inherited).
- **`quarantine` ≠ `dead_letter`** — human-needed staff worklist vs. crash pager; never conflated.
- **"The socket never silently auto-creates an expectancy when an open candidate exists"** — it routes to the suggestion/triage surface [D4.9].
- **"The raw-payload archive table is DEFERRED until the first non-staff producer exists — the cut stands"** [D4 rider].
- **Blocking hints, both directions, never silent** — required reason-to-override, audited [D4.5].
- **The founder's don't-over-engineer rider is BINDING:** v1 = the leanest compliant shape; the smaller shape wins. No speculative connector machinery, vendor fields, archive, or auto-spawn.
- House rules: TEXT + CHECK (never native enums), integer minor units, composite `(tenant_id, …)` FKs, FORCE RLS, census rows in the same migration as any new table [D1.9, D1.10].
- Socket events and expectancy amounts are **never money** — nothing here enters either money vocabulary; the socket never posts contributions and never writes `received` [D4.7, D4.13].

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A registered producer can submit a schema-versioned typed event; the response is an opaque event id with no match/no-match, person-exists, or expectancy-exists information.
- [ ] A payload naming a tenant other than its registration's tenant is rejected as malformed (dead_letter), zero domain writes.
- [ ] Malformed payloads / crashes land in `dead_letter`; ambiguous matches / open-dupe candidates land in `quarantine`; the lanes are distinct in storage, surfaces, and ownership.
- [ ] Re-delivery of an existing `(tenant_id, external_ref)` is idempotent; an event with an open expectancy candidate never auto-creates — it appears in the staff triage/suggestion surface.
- [ ] The socket path posts no money, mints no credits, sends nothing, and cannot set `received`/`reversed` (the state-wall trigger holds).
- [ ] No raw-payload archive table, no vendor-id columns, and no auto-spawn saga exist in the diff.
- [ ] `party_payer_aliases` matching covers `payer_kind = 'workplace_giving_intermediary'` through the same matcher + one-click triage as DAF sponsors; the seven per-tenant intermediary seeds ship as suggestions.
- [ ] Both hint directions block with a required reason-to-override and write an audit row (polymorphic subject) carrying the reason.
- [ ] `matching-ingest-quarantine-age` registers in the Phase 8 catalog, reporting the oldest un-adjudicated quarantine item; signal payloads carry counts/ages only.
- [ ] Donor-facing matching default copy contains the verbatim ratified sentence; no "double your donation" default banner; matching promotion is opt-in per tenant.
- [ ] Any new table ships FORCE RLS, composite tenant FKs, TEXT + CHECK, and fail-closed census rows in the same migration.

## Testing

Poison fixtures owned or exercised here (PRD Testing & Poison Fixtures):

- **Fixture 22 (Family 4) — Intermediary block:** a Benevity-registered payer pushed through the match path hits the blocking hint with reason-to-override — never a silent pass, either direction [D4.5, D4.14].
- **Fixture 34 (Family 6) — Cross-tenant service-role rejection:** a forged cross-tenant join written as `service_role` fails on the composite `(tenant_id, …)` FK, not merely RLS; the per-generator tier explicitly includes **the ingest socket**.
- **Fixture 35 (Family 6) — Imports fire nothing:** an import/ingest produces zero sends AND zero credits across every generator [D4.14].
- **Socket-contract tests (this slice's own family):** no-echo (the response never varies by whether a candidate exists); tenant-mismatch → dead_letter; malformed → dead_letter; ambiguous match → quarantine; open candidate → triage, never auto-create; re-delivery idempotent; adjudication routes into the existing suggestion surface.
- **Signal test:** `matching-ingest-quarantine-age` fires on an aged unresolved quarantine item, silent on an empty queue.
- **Copy test:** default donor-facing matching template text contains the ratified sentence verbatim; no default promotion banner.

Prior-art test files (REAL, verified): `tests/unit/donation-saga.test.ts`, `tests/unit/packages/api/workflows/donation-saga-recovery.test.ts` (durable-processing/outbox idioms), `tests/unit/packages/api/email/consent.test.ts` (fail-closed gate shape), `tests/unit/reaction-idempotency.test.ts` (idempotent re-delivery shape).

## Blocked by

- #727 — the `party_payer_aliases` registry, matcher, and one-click triage this slice generalizes.
- #735 — the received flow / match path the blocking hints and quarantine adjudication route into.
- External: #503 — Phase 4 (Identity & Account-Claiming Foundation) A5: the socket's no-synchronous-match-echo and never-silently-auto-create-when-a-candidate-exists posture implements its match/duplicate rules.

The whole Phase 14 epic is `status:blocked` on the predecessor spine (Phases 3, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13 builds) per program convention.

---

### Amendment (2026-11-10): Phase 1 / Twenty-retirement reconciliation (AL-2645, PR #2646 pending)

The `crm_record_links` anchor and dependency lines are superseded. `20260818010000_retire_twenty_crm_runtime.sql` dropped the `CHECK (crm_provider = 'twenty')`, but the table remains Twenty-shaped (`crm_provider` default `'twenty'`, NOT NULL `twenty_object_name`/`twenty_record_id`, Twenty-keyed unique indexes). Phase 30 D9 makes it the carrier for CRM/Party source bindings only after owner row-model generalization following a census, the #2295 revoke and a typed audited command. Which phase performs that generalization is an open owner decision (the Phase 30 binding ticket #2554 names the Phase 4/9 owners; the Phase 31 owner constraints describe its connector registry as generalizing the table), so do not treat Phase 31 as the settled owner. D4.9's zero-Phase-14-schema-change rule is unchanged. The Phase 14 PRD is corrected in PR #2646.

items.title: Multi-tenancy and dynamic schema selection
items.body:
Recently, several people asked about implementing dynamic schema selection to enable schema-base multi-tenancy, where tenant isolation is achieved via DDL Schemas. (If you are not familiar with DDL schemas then you can learn the basics e.g. in [PostgreSQL docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-schemas.html)).

I am opening this Epic to do discuss possible solutions, implement necessary improvements and document how to implement multi-tenancy, possibly including an example app.

Related discussions:
- Loopback 4, Model, PostgresDB schema name https://github.com/strongloop/loopback-next/issues/5055
- StackOverflow question: [Schema based Multi tenancy in Loopback 4](https://stackoverflow.com/q/60680275/69868)
- StackOverflow answer: [How to attach a single model (e.g. Product) to multiple datasources]( https://stackoverflow.com/a/28327323/69868) (LB3)
- StackOverflow anwser: [How to prefix model name with tenant id](https://stackoverflow.com/a/53229733/69868) (LB3)

Aspects to consider:
- CLI should recognize dynamic repository/datasource in commands like `lb4 datasource`
- How to boot custom artifacts - we can improve `@loopback/boot` (if needed) or move the registration to a different place (e.g. from a datasource file to a boot script)
- How to migrate/update database tables for all tenants when the model shape changes
- How to onboard a new tenant (create the new schema & all tables)

items.title: Phase 10 Source Explorer + medical library browser + canonical SQLite ingestion
items.body:
## Goal
Build verified **Santo Source Explorer** and **Medical Library Browser** for the user-supplied licensed 7,049 article SQLite corpus: citation -> authenticated original article -> highlight referenced section -> browse nearby sections and all library articles. Desktop panel and mobile full-screen reader. Avoid source leaks or XSS.

## Authority boundaries
- Browser may not supply raw R2 keys, source URLs, tenant or user selectors.
- Citation jumps require existing authenticated verified message/source snapshot and must map exact `libraryId`/`itemKey` to canonical R2 JSON.
- Library browsing remains tenant-authenticated; libraries are currently global and not per-tenant restricted.
- Article display uses strict schema and **plaintext/structured sections**, never raw third-party HTML, script, iframes, data URI or insecure links.
- Only allow media from the approved public R2 media host and normalized `offline_media/` keys. No silent remote image fetch.

## Implementation
- [x] Canonical importer CLI for SQLite -> sanitized article JSON and AI Search-indexable Markdown, versioned stable IDs/section anchors, manifests, checksum and media URL normalization; no licensed bytes committed to GitHub.
- [x] Authenticated source article endpoint with citation snapshot validation and honest section highlight; invalid/stale source must fail closed.
- [x] Authenticated paginated library browse API + article reader without a citation, with bounded query and keys.
- [x] Santo Lit widget reader/side panel, mobile full-screen behavior, section jump and browse UI.
- [x] Royal Bank `/santo` citation control and article viewer integration (or an independent compatible host interface).
- [ ] Full deterministic contract/security tests, staging deploy, authorized browser test, AI Search indexing verification. Do not claim source citation alignment before real indexed corpus.

## Preconditions and acceptance
Owner claims commercial licensing. Do not publish article contents on public R2 or GitHub. Source `all_libraries.zip` is available in ChatGPT container but not on GitHub Actions or Cloudflare R2. Setup private direct ingest with secrets or authenticated uploader. Tests must pass before merge. No full rollout until corpus is uploaded/indexed and validated.
## Implementation evidence — 14 October 2026
- Santo [PR #83](https://github.com/geminiamo0-ship-it/santoreno/pull/83) merged `730a443ec1f327cf14fa6918d5332aa45d093585` after exact PR head `098fae04f7cfffa5feb0a8c4c9e4201ec7fb311e` passed repository policy, formatting, typecheck, unit tests, build and smoke.

- Actual original licensed SQLite exported **locally**: 7,049 structured article JSON; 67,524 indexed-section Markdown; 6 catalog manifests, 74,579 private R2 upload objects total. Package `santo_staging_medical_library_r2_bundle.tar.zst` ~29MiB and SHA256 `5123c335926c73489be3957328b652d91d4ee50538cbdddaa62a4ea067a5f9c4`. No corpus bytes added to GitHub.
- Santo post-merge Verify [38500681584](https://github.com/geminiamo0-ship-it/santoreno/actions/runs/38500681584) **SUCCESS**. Staging Worker deploy/401 unauthorized access smoke [38500681521](https://github.com/geminiamo0-ship-it/santoreno/actions/runs/38500681521) **SUCCESS**. **Content upload and AI Search indexing not yet performed** because chat runtime lacks authenticated private Cloudflare R2 object upload. User's public image R2 URL is read-only and is not the Santo private bucket.

items.title: Hive connector caches table locations by bare table name: same-named tables in different schemas read the wrong files
items.body:
Found during the #108 review (Tier 2). Pre-existing on `main`.

### Problem
`HiveConnectorFactory::locations` (`crates/hive/src/datasource.rs`) caches table storage locations keyed by **table name only**, not `catalog.schema.table`. Within one Arneb process, whichever of two same-named tables in different schemas is read first wins, and queries against the other one **silently read the first table's files**.

### Repro
With both `hive.tpch.orders` (DOUBLE) and `hive.tpch_decimal.orders` (DECIMAL) seeded (`docker compose run --rm tpch-seed` and `TPCH_DECIMAL=1 docker compose run --rm tpch-seed`):
1. In one Arneb process, query `tpch.orders` (e.g. `SELECT avg(o_totalprice) FROM datalake.tpch.orders`).
2. Then query `datalake.tpch_decimal.orders` with the same aggregate.
3. The second result comes from the first table's files (wrong types/values); in a fresh process the order flips which one is wrong. It first looked like a "flaky" DECIMAL AVG.

### Impact
Silent wrong results whenever two schemas (or catalogs) contain tables with the same name — common in real data lakes (`staging.orders` / `prod.orders`, per-tenant schemas). Also affects Iceberg tables redirected through the Hive catalog if they share a name with a Hive table elsewhere.

### Fix direction
Key the cache by the fully qualified `(catalog, schema, table)` (and consider invalidation when HMS metadata changes). Add a test with two same-named tables in different schemas read in one process.

items.title: [Storage] Storage contract + local embedded profile + hosted isolation spikes · EvoBase
items.body:
## Product/storage correction — 03/10/2026

Votable vision đã được hấp thụ vào EvoBase. Issue này **không còn được hiểu là “chọn fixed-layout PostgreSQL làm storage của EvoBase”**. Nó sở hữu **storage contract + conformance**, sau đó mới đo các adapter/profile.

Thứ tự đúng:

1. **Storage contract/conformance:** facts, Ref, constraints, revision/CAS, atomic mutation, receipt/outbox, scan/query budgets.
2. **Local/embedded profile:** adapter nhẹ cho local-first/offline/self-hosted; không cần hosted tenant registry để chạy.
3. **Hosted PostgreSQL spikes:** fixed-layout là candidate; database-per-tenant/schema/shared+RLS là isolation candidates cần benchmark/ADR.
4. **Optional compiled relational adapter:** chỉ ở publish/migration boundary nếu cần hiệu năng; không đổi AppSpec semantics.

Yêu cầu sản phẩm là **logical config không bắt buộc business DDL ở mỗi thao tác Builder**. Physical layout là quyết định của adapter.

## Phạm vi và trạng thái

Thiết kế/skills/PR prompts theo [vision #1](https://github.com/loveoverflowcom/evobase/issues/1). **Chưa triển khai sản phẩm.** Leptos web, CMP mobile và Rust backend là stack đích; lượt này chỉ chuẩn bị design và các PR nhỏ để làm tuần tự. Prototype có dữ liệu mẫu, không auth/backend/SQL/provider thật.

Đo fixed-layout engine store và database-per-tenant, giữ lựa chọn ADR chưa settled production.

Desktop: static design frame, không phải browser screenshot.

Storage contract + local adapter có thể bắt đầu sau #4/#5 và codec/core gates. Hosted isolation/authority acceptance cần #6. Release/evolution nối #8; API/tenant evidence nối #18/#20/#21.

Không bắt local-first profile đợi hosted auth, connector, messaging hoặc chatbot. Fixed-layout/database-per-tenant chỉ được chốt sau conformance + benchmark/ADR.

## Acceptance trước khi bật capability

- [ ] Hai tenant DB + provisioner/runtime role separation; runtime no DDL/BYPASSRLS
- [ ] Thêm logical table/optional field/Ref/publish không business SQL DDL; actual catalog evidence
- [ ] Records/edges/index/unique/revision/outbox atomic; concurrency/restart/failure vectors
- [ ] Tenant negative tests gồm API/Ref/cache/subscription/blob/log/bot; resource/latency measurements + support envelope ADR

## Prompt thực hiện sau khi được yêu cầu code

Đọc linked PR prompt và skills liên quan trước; đối chiếu design pin/vision/current source. Chỉ implement scope của PR kế tiếp, giữ canonical token identity và stable IDs. Đề xuất/chốt ADR qua review gate, cùng unsupported subset ở gate cần thiết, không biến fixture thành lời hứa feature đã chạy. Báo rõ passed/failed/not-run với commit/build/scenario; source→adapter→mounted consumer, web/native CMP và simulated/real provider phải là bằng chứng riêng. Dừng ở draft PR để review; không merge/deploy/default-branch switch, live migration hay legacy retirement.

## Evidence và giới hạn

250 checks là static source/ZIP/hash/contrast checks trên design kit; reviewer đã kiểm anatomy/light-dark/navigation/font provenance. Không phải Leptos browser interaction, native CMP Android/iOS, Rust/storage conformance, benchmark hay provider pass. Builder compact là summary; Runtime mobile là target native anatomy. 1:1/N:M/migration/offline/provider capabilities chỉ bật sau ADR/conformance, chưa coi là baseline đã hỗ trợ.


<!-- evobase-archive-gap-plan-2026-10-03:start -->
## Kế hoạch registry/storage dùng chung — 03/10/2026

Theo [Vision #1](https://github.com/loveoverflowcom/evobase/issues/1); [#15](https://github.com/loveoverflowcom/evobase/issues/15) chỉ theo dõi migration/disposition, tái sử dụng lessons registry/provisioning/CAS/event persistence của archive; không restore OrderRepository/UserRepository/demo tables làm common data model.

**PR-A:** durable tenant/app registry và idempotent provisioning operation identity; persisted progress/ready/failure, restart/retry/recovery. Separate provisioner/migrator/runtime privileges/credentials, verified scope selects binding.

**PR-B:** fixed-store executor consume generic checked writes/event intents (#17/#18). Canonical facts/derived structures/CAS/pin/revision/audit/outbox/receipt atomic; current authority trước replay/commit. Archive transition và publish riêng operations là failure case cần sửa, không implementation để copy.

**PR-C:** real two-tenant/no-DDL/catalog/races/failure-injection/restart/resource measurements; #20 operator status projection, #8 release/evolution.

- [ ] Hai unrelated app schemas dùng cùng fixed store, không thêm business SQL table/repository per app.
- [ ] Registry/provision failure/retry giữ một consistent operation/binding; runtime không dùng admin privilege.
- [ ] Revoked/raced authority và stale CAS reject; state/event/receipt rollback cùng nhau.
- [ ] #21 chỉ stream committed authorized events; invalid writes không phát events.

Sau #6 và supported core gates; không migrate production hoặc chạy DB/CI trong lượt kế hoạch.
