items.title: [Proposal]: Import LangChain and LangSmith traces into the AI asset inventory
items.body:
## Gap
The cross-provider AI asset inventory in #235 calls for a generic format and one ecosystem adapter. LangChain/LangSmith runs can expose agent, model, retriever, and tool relationships, but COPS has no scoped importer that maps those relationships into the inventory with trace provenance.

## Proposed first increment
- Add a **read-only, offline** importer for one documented LangChain/LangSmith trace export format and version. Identify that format during implementation and reject unsupported variants clearly. Do not require a live LangSmith credential or API connector for this increment.
- Map run IDs, parent-child relationships, chain/agent, model, retriever, and tool nodes into #235's asset and trust-boundary schema. Preserve source, tenant, export timestamp, and per-record provenance through the shared evidence envelope (#25).
- Namespace identifiers by source and tenant, make repeat imports idempotent, and handle missing parents, duplicate IDs, conflicting records, and truncated exports without inventing edges.
- Keep sensitive trace content out of inventory summaries; apply existing evidence access and outbound export policy (#238). Treat absent permission, ownership, or tool-effect fields as **unknown**.

## Acceptance criteria
- Offline fixtures cover nested agent/tool/model runs, two tenants with colliding run IDs, repeat import, missing parent, conflicting records, and a truncated export.
- The resulting graph and provenance are inspectable, and unsupported export versions produce an actionable error.
- Documentation names the supported export format/version, required fields, privacy limits, and the distinction between observed trace links and inferred trust boundaries. No live connector or exploitability conclusion is claimed.

Related: #25, #235, #238. LangSmith privacy context: https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/mask-inputs-outputs

items.title: Insurance

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

MediCore currently has no insurance domain at all. Billing treats every encounter as self-pay: a bill is raised, a payment is taken, done. In an Indian hospital that is wrong for the majority of IPD revenue — a typical multi-speciality hospital settles 55–75% of inpatient value through cashless TPA arrangements, corporate panels and government schemes (PM-JAY and state equivalents), not cash at the counter.

Without an insurance domain there is nowhere to record which payer covers a patient, no way to hold a bill in a "payer liability" state, no place for a pre-authorisation to live, and no ledger separating patient co-pay from payer receivable. The consequences are concrete: the billing desk cannot discharge a cashless patient without manually improvising, the TPA co-ordinator works entirely off spreadsheets and email, and finance cannot answer "how much are we owed, by whom, and for how long".

Affected roles: TPA co-ordinator (insurance desk), billing executive, hospital admin, finance controller, and the patient — who is asked to pay a deposit they may not owe.

This issue establishes the **insurance domain foundation** that every other story in this epic depends on: payer master data, plan/tariff linkage, the payer-liability split on a bill, the domain event contract, and the OpenFGA object types. It is deliberately foundational and does not implement any single workflow end to end.

Regulatory context: payer, plan and claim records carry personal and health data and fall under DPDP Act 2023 — sharing a discharge summary with a TPA is a disclosure to a third party and needs a lawful basis and an audit trail. Invoices raised against corporate and TPA payers are B2B supplies and must carry GSTIN and HSN/SAC per GST e-invoicing rules.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** TPA co-ordinator and the billing service
**I want** a first-class insurance domain — payers, plans, patient coverage, and a payer/patient liability split on every bill
**So that** cashless encounters, pre-authorisations and claims can be modelled on real data instead of spreadsheets.

### Scope

**In scope**

* `payer` master: insurer, TPA, corporate panel, government scheme; registration identifiers, GSTIN, contact routing, active date range, tenant-scoped.
* `payer_plan`: product/plan under a payer, with room-rent caps, co-pay percentage, sub-limits, exclusions list reference, and effective dates.
* `payer_tariff_link`: association of a plan to a MediCore tariff/rate card so charge capture prices correctly at the point of order.
* Extension of the bill/invoice model with a liability split — `payer_liability_amount`, `patient_liability_amount`, `non_payable_amount` — and a `settlement_mode` of `cash | cashless | reimbursement | scheme`.
* Domain events on NATS JetStream: `PayerCreated`, `PayerPlanUpdated`, `BillLiabilitySplitApplied`.
* OpenFGA object types `payer`, `payer_plan` and the `insurance_desk` role relation.
* Country Profile hook so payer categories and scheme types are configuration, not enum constants.

**Out of scope**

* Patient-level coverage records and card capture — owned by #220 (Patient insurance profile).
* Real-time eligibility checks against payer APIs — owned by #221.
* Pre-authorisation workflow — #222. Claim documents and submission — #225.
* TPA connector implementations (portal scraping, SFTP, REST) — owned by the TPA integration story in this epic.
* Denial and appeal handling, and reconciliation of remittances — later stories in this epic.

---

## Recommended Solution

Build an `insurance` module inside the Go/Gin modular monolith (`internal/insurance`), with GORM models and a tenant-scoped repository layer so no query can omit `tenant_id`. PostgreSQL 16 row-level security is applied to every new table.

```sql
CREATE TABLE payer (
  id              uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id       uuid NOT NULL,
  code            text NOT NULL,
  name            text NOT NULL,
  category        text NOT NULL,      -- insurer|tpa|corporate|govt_scheme
  irdai_reg_no    text,
  gstin           text,
  country_profile text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'IN',
  active_from     date NOT NULL,
  active_to       date,
  UNIQUE (tenant_id, code)
);

CREATE TABLE payer_plan (
  id                 uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id          uuid NOT NULL,
  payer_id           uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES payer(id),
  name               text NOT NULL,
  room_rent_cap      numeric(12,2),
  copay_pct          numeric(5,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (copay_pct BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
  sum_insured_default numeric(14,2),
  sub_limits         jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  tariff_id          uuid,
  effective_from     date NOT NULL,
  effective_to       date,
  UNIQUE (tenant_id, payer_id, name, effective_from)
);
ALTER TABLE payer ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE payer_plan ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
```

The liability split lives on the existing bill aggregate as a computed, versioned snapshot rather than derived on read, so a bill printed at discharge is reproducible. A `bill_liability_split` row is written whenever the plan, tariff or charge set changes, and the previous row is superseded (`superseded_at`), never updated in place — this satisfies the tamper-evident audit rule.

API surface (all under `/api/v1`, tenant resolved from the token):

| Method | Path |
|---|---|
| `GET/POST` | `/insurance/payers` |
| `GET/PATCH` | `/insurance/payers/{payerId}` |
| `GET/POST` | `/insurance/payers/{payerId}/plans` |
| `PATCH` | `/insurance/plans/{planId}` |
| `POST` | `/billing/bills/{billId}/liability-split:recompute` |
| `GET` | `/billing/bills/{billId}/liability-split` |

Events published to JetStream stream `INSURANCE`:

```json
{ "type": "BillLiabilitySplitApplied", "tenantId": "...", "billId": "...",
  "planId": "...", "payerLiability": 184500.00, "patientLiability": 32500.00,
  "nonPayable": 8900.00, "splitVersion": 3, "occurredAt": "2026-07-20T09:14:22Z" }
```

OpenFGA model additions:

```
type payer
  relations
    define tenant: [tenant]
    define manager: insurance_desk from tenant or finance_admin from tenant
    define viewer: manager or billing_clerk from tenant
```

Sequencing: this issue must land before #220–#225. It depends on the existing tariff/rate-card model in Billing and on the tenant context middleware. Vertex AI OCR (#insurance-document extraction) and TPA connectors consume this model but do not block it.

Risks and mitigations. **Wrong split silently under-billing the patient** — mitigated by making the split immutable and versioned, and by a reconciliation invariant test asserting `payer + patient + non_payable == bill_total` at every write. **Plan changes retro-applying to closed bills** — mitigated by effective-dating plans and resolving the plan by encounter admission date, not `now()`. **Cross-tenant payer leakage** (payers have similar names across tenants) — mitigated by RLS plus an adversarial isolation test in CI.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** a tenant with an active payer "Star Health" and a plan carrying a 10% co-pay and a ₹6,000 room-rent cap
**When** an admitted patient's bill totalling ₹2,25,900 is recomputed with that plan
**Then** a `bill_liability_split` version is written with payer, patient and non-payable amounts summing exactly to the bill total, room charges above the cap classified as non-payable, and `BillLiabilitySplitApplied` is published.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** a billing clerk who holds `billing_clerk` but not `insurance_desk` on the tenant
**When** they call `PATCH /insurance/plans/{planId}` to raise the room-rent cap
**Then** the request is rejected with 403 from the OpenFGA check, no write occurs, no event is published, and the denied attempt is recorded in the audit log with actor, object and relation.

### Edge Cases

* A plan whose `effective_to` fell before the encounter's admission date must not be selectable; the API returns a validation error naming the date conflict.
* Recomputing a split twice with identical inputs is idempotent — no new version row and no duplicate event.
* A plan with `copay_pct = 0` and no sub-limits must still produce an explicit split row rather than leaving the fields null.
* A payer marked inactive mid-admission remains resolvable for existing encounters but cannot be attached to new ones.
* Rounding: co-pay on an odd total must not lose or create a paisa; the invariant test asserts exact equality at 2dp.
* A tenant on the schema-per-tenant premium tier must exercise the same repository path without RLS predicates being bypassed.

---

## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team's agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team's agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* **Expected user or system outcome:** every bill in a tenant with insurance configured carries a reproducible, versioned payer/patient liability split, and the TPA co-ordinator can maintain payers and plans in the console without engineering involvement.
* **Expected business or operational outcome:** finance can report gross payer receivable by payer and by plan from the OLAP store, which is the precondition for measuring claim leakage.
* **Success metric or validation method:** 100% of bills created after release have a split row whose components sum exactly to the bill total (nightly invariant job reports zero violations); `POST /liability-split:recompute` p95 under 250 ms for a bill with 200 charge lines; adversarial cross-tenant isolation suite passes with zero leaks.
* **Monitoring period:** 30 days post-release, with the nightly invariant job alerting on any non-zero violation count.

---

## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

**Guardrail:** Accessibility and User Journey — WCAG level and keyboard navigation.
**Reason:** This story delivers the domain model, API and events. The payer/plan admin screens in the Next.js 16 console are a thin CRUD surface built on existing design-system form components in a follow-up; no bespoke interaction is introduced here.
**Alternative validation:** API contract tests plus design-system component-level accessibility coverage already in place; the follow-up console story carries the full WCAG 2.2 AA check.
**Residual risk:** Low — no end-user-facing surface ships in this story.
**Approved by:** Revenue Cycle Team lead.

items.title: Spec: PulseIntel v1 collaborative market intelligence dashboard

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an agent

items.body:
## Problem Statement

Small teams that track competitive intelligence, market signals, and internal performance data usually stitch together spreadsheets, news feeds, ad hoc scraping, dashboards, and team chat. That makes it difficult to keep observations trustworthy, collaborate around changes in real time, preserve historical context, and act quickly when something meaningful changes.

These teams need PulseIntel: a shared, real-time market intelligence product where a Tenant can organize Workspaces, attach Sources, monitor Metrics and Observations, create Insights, annotate Dashboard trends, and receive Alerts with clear provenance.

## Solution

Build PulseIntel as a multi-tenant SaaS for collaborative market intelligence. Each Tenant has global Users with Tenant Roles and Workspace Roles, a Tenant Home for navigation, tenant-owned Sources, and one or more Workspaces. Each Workspace owns Dashboards, Custom Metrics, Alert Rules, Insights, Annotations, and subscriptions to tenant Sources.

The v1 product will provide:
- Tenant/workspace collaboration with Invitations, memberships, and role-based access control
- Widget-based Dashboards with a Dashboard Time Range and optional widget-level overrides
- Tenant-owned Sources with Source Kinds for RSS feed ingestion, price tracking, KPI ingest, and Manual Source entry
- Immutable Observation History with Evidence and Evidence Snapshots for trust and auditability
- Base Metrics plus workspace-scoped Custom Metrics with strict Unit Validation, Formula Function Set guardrails, and asynchronous Metric Materialization
- Rule-based Alerts with Alert Severity, per-rule Alert Cooldown, durable Alert Events, per-user Alert Subscriptions, in-app history, and email delivery
- Insights and Annotations with Comment Threads, required Insight Evidence Links, and soft locking for finalized findings
- Revisions, Snapshots, archive/restore, Activity Feed, and Audit Trail behavior that preserves history instead of hiding it

## User Stories

1. As a tenant owner, I want to create and manage a Tenant, so that my company has a dedicated market intelligence boundary.
2. As a tenant admin, I want to invite users by email, so that teammates can join the correct Tenant and Workspaces.
3. As a user, I want a single global identity across multiple Tenants, so that I can work with different customer or internal accounts without separate logins.
4. As a user, I want to land on a Tenant Home after accepting an Invitation, so that I can choose the right Workspace quickly.
5. As a tenant admin, I want to assign Tenant Roles and Workspace Roles, so that administration and day-to-day collaboration stay separate.
6. As a workspace admin, I want to manage membership within a Workspace, so that the right people can view, edit, and administer shared intelligence.
7. As a team member, I want to create a Workspace, through tenant administration, so that different initiatives can collaborate without mixing dashboards and alerts.
8. As a workspace member, I want to open a Dashboard with a shared default time range, so that the team sees the same market picture.
9. As a workspace member, I want certain Widgets to override the Dashboard Time Range, so that a single Dashboard can show both short-term and long-term views.
10. As a workspace editor, I want to arrange Widgets on a fixed grid, so that Dashboards are flexible but still structured and versionable.
11. As a workspace editor, I want to clone a Dashboard as an independent copy, so that I can reuse setup without creating hidden linkage to the original.
12. As a workspace editor, I want to create Insights tied to supporting evidence, so that durable findings stay trustworthy.
13. As a workspace member, I want to annotate Widgets, Observations, and time ranges, so that I can add context exactly where a change appears.
14. As a workspace member, I want Comment Threads on Insights and Annotations, so that collaboration stays attached to the relevant evidence.
15. As a workspace editor, I want to lock an Insight after finalizing it, so that the finding stays stable while discussion can continue.
16. As a workspace editor, I want tenant-owned Sources to be reusable across Workspaces through Source Subscriptions, so that we avoid duplicate setup.
17. As a workspace editor, I want Subscription Filters on a Source Subscription, so that each Workspace can focus on the subset of data it actually needs.
18. As a tenant admin, I want to define Source configuration once per Tenant, so that feed and price tracking logic is consistent.
19. As a workspace editor, I want Manual Sources, so that I can capture intelligence even when automation is not ready.
20. As a workspace editor, I want Manual Source entries to require a Citation Note, so that manually entered values are still explainable.
21. As a system operator, I want RSS feed items normalized into Observations with article evidence, so that news fits the same trust model as other signals.
22. As a workspace member, I want repeated sightings of the same article deduplicated into an Article Identity, so that feeds are readable without losing provenance.
23. As a workspace editor, I want price tracking Sources to capture extracted values plus evidence snapshots, so that pricing changes can be verified later.
24. As a workspace member, I want broken source collection to surface Source Health problems, so that missing data is not mistaken for stable conditions.
25. As a workspace member, I want Collection Runs recorded separately from Observations, so that failed collection is distinguishable from no change.
26. As a tenant admin, I want Base Metrics to be tenant-owned and reused, so that source-backed definitions stay consistent across Workspaces.
27. As a workspace editor, I want to define Custom Metrics inside a Workspace, so that each team can build derived intelligence on top of shared data.
28. As a workspace editor, I want Custom Metrics to reference other Custom Metrics through an acyclic Metric Dependency Graph, so that complex derived analysis remains stable.
29. As a workspace editor, I want strict Unit Validation in formulas, so that derived Metrics do not combine incompatible values incorrectly.
30. As a workspace editor, I want a guarded Formula Function Set with arithmetic, comparisons, conditional logic, and time-window helpers, so that formulas are useful without becoming arbitrary code execution.
31. As a workspace member, I want Custom Metric values materialized asynchronously, so that dashboards and alerts remain fast and predictable.
32. As a workspace editor, I want KPI ingest credentials scoped to a Workspace, so that internal metric ownership matches the collaboration boundary.
33. As an integration system, I want to push KPI Observations with optional Metric Dimensions, so that teams can track segmented business performance.
34. As a workspace editor, I want to create Alert Rules on Observations and Metrics, so that meaningful changes are surfaced automatically.
35. As a workspace editor, I want Alert Severity on Alert Rules, so that high-priority changes stand out from routine monitoring.
36. As a workspace member, I want Alert Events recorded durably, so that I can review alert history in-app and not rely only on transient notifications.
37. As a workspace member, I want to acknowledge an Alert Event, so that the team can see that someone has seen it.
38. As a workspace member, I want Alert Cooldown configured per Alert Rule, so that noisy conditions do not overwhelm the Workspace.
39. As a new workspace member, I want alert subscriptions to start unsubscribed, so that joining a Workspace does not immediately flood my inbox.
40. As a workspace member, I want to subscribe only to the Alert Rules I care about, so that notifications stay relevant.
41. As a workspace member, I want Alerts delivered in-app and by email, so that I can respond quickly whether I am in the product or away from it.
42. As a workspace member, I want realtime updates for Alerts, Annotations, Comment Threads, and dashboard content refreshes, so that collaboration feels live without requiring full concurrent editing.
43. As a workspace member, I want immutable Observation History, so that I can trust what the system actually captured at a given time.
44. As a workspace member, I want long-term historical analysis to transparently use downsampled data when needed, so that old trends remain explorable without keeping infinite raw detail.
45. As a workspace editor, I want every change to a Dashboard, Custom Metric, or Alert Rule to create a Revision, so that restore behavior is simple and auditable.
46. As a workspace editor, I want named Snapshots, so that important milestones can be restored intentionally.
47. As a workspace member, I want restoring a Revision or Snapshot to create a new current Revision, so that history is preserved instead of rewritten.
48. As a tenant admin, I want Workspaces archived before deletion, so that shared intelligence is not lost accidentally.
49. As a tenant admin, I want Workspace Restore to recover the full Workspace state, so that archiving acts as a safety measure rather than a teardown.
50. As a workspace member, I want an Activity Feed for collaboration, alert, and source health changes, so that I can understand what the team and system are doing over time.
51. As an administrator, I want an Audit Trail for security, admin, and restore actions, so that accountability exists without exposing everything as user-facing noise.
52. As a product team, I want PulseIntel to treat evidence and provenance as first-class concepts throughout the product, so that trust remains a core differentiator.

## Implementation Decisions

- Build the product as a modular monolith with separate worker processes for ingestion, metric materialization, alert evaluation, and other asynchronous jobs.
- Use a multi-tenant SaaS model from day one with a single global user identity and shared-schema tenant isolation enforced at the application and query level.
- Implement authentication with Auth0 rather than custom JWT infrastructure.
- Target AWS for v1, running the application and workers on ECS Fargate.
- Use PostgreSQL as the primary store with TimescaleDB for time-series workloads.
- Use Redis and BullMQ for background job orchestration.
- Store Evidence metadata in PostgreSQL and Evidence Snapshots in S3.
- Model the core domain around Tenant, Workspace, Dashboard, Widget, Source, Source Subscription, Observation, Metric, Custom Metric, Alert Rule, Alert Event, Insight, Annotation, Revision, Snapshot, Activity Feed, and Audit Trail.
- Keep Sources tenant-owned, with workspace-level Source Subscriptions and Subscription Filters controlling how each Workspace consumes shared Sources.
- Support first-class Source Kinds for RSS feed, price tracker, KPI ingest API, and Manual Source in v1.
- Represent each collection attempt as a Collection Run, distinct from the Observations it may or may not produce.
- Model Observations with a shared envelope for timestamps, provenance, and analysis, plus kind-specific payloads and evidence details.
- Keep Observation History immutable; corrections and recaptures must create new or superseding records rather than overwriting history.
- Deduplicate repeated news items into a stable Article Identity while preserving collection history.
- Define Base Metrics at the tenant level and allow Workspaces to define Custom Metrics locally.
- Support Custom Metrics over workspace-visible Metrics only, with an acyclic Metric Dependency Graph and strict Unit Validation.
- Materialize Custom Metric values asynchronously when upstream Observations or Metrics change.
- Require explicit Metric Unit metadata and support optional Metric Dimensions on ingested metric values.
- Implement Alert Rules as rule-based conditions only in v1, with per-rule Alert Severity, per-rule Alert Cooldown, durable Alert Events, and user-level Alert Subscriptions.
- Evaluate Alert Rules both on relevant data updates and on scheduled sweeps so missing-data conditions can be detected.
- Default new workspace members to an unsubscribed Default Subscription State for Alert Rules.
- Support in-app and email alert delivery in v1, using user acknowledgement rather than a full incident-resolution workflow.
- Allow Viewers to contribute Annotations and Comment Threads, while structural changes remain limited to Editors and Workspace Admins.
- Require every Insight to carry at least one Insight Evidence Link to an Observation, annotation target, or Evidence reference.
- Support soft-locking for Insights: locked Insights are read-only for normal editors, but discussion can continue and authorized users can reopen them.
- Version Dashboards, Custom Metrics, and Alert Rules with automatic Revisions on every saved change plus named Snapshots.
- Restoring historical state must create a new Revision instead of mutating past history.
- Archive Workspaces before deletion and allow full Workspace Restore, including dashboards, subscriptions, alerts, and historical state.
- Provide a Dashboard Time Range with optional widget-level overrides.
- Keep Dashboards workspace-owned; clones are independent copies and not live-linked templates.
- Expose realtime product behavior through REST APIs plus Socket.io events rather than GraphQL subscriptions.
- Build a user-visible Activity Feed for collaboration, alert, and source-health events, distinct from the admin-oriented Audit Trail.
- Capture source failures as Source Health problems and failed Collection Runs instead of silently skipping data or carrying forward stale values as current truth.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test should verify external behavior and user-visible outcomes rather than internal implementation details.
- The primary seam should be the application boundary: REST API contracts, Socket.io realtime behavior, worker-triggered outcomes, persistence-visible revisions/history, and authorization behavior across tenant and workspace boundaries.
- A narrow secondary seam should exist at the source collector adapter boundary so each Source Kind can be tested against a stable collection contract without depending on live third-party systems.
- Test the tenancy and membership model through public auth, invitation, and authorization behavior rather than direct storage assumptions.
- Test Dashboard behavior through creation, widget layout, cloning, time-range defaults/overrides, versioning, archive/restore, and visibility rules.
- Test source ingestion through Collection Run outcomes, Observation creation, evidence capture, Source Health transitions, and source-subscription filtering behavior.
- Test Custom Metrics through formula validation, Metric Unit enforcement, acyclic dependency handling, asynchronous materialization, and historical query behavior.
- Test Alerts through rule evaluation, Alert Cooldown behavior, Alert Event creation, acknowledgement, subscription defaults, delivery fan-out, and realtime propagation.
- Test Insights and collaboration through evidence-link requirements, annotation anchors, comment threads, locking/reopening rules, and Activity Feed visibility.
- Test historical behavior through immutable Observation History, retention/downsampling query behavior, Revision creation, Snapshot restore, and Workspace Restore.
- Prior art in the current repository is effectively none because the codebase is still greenfield; the initial test suite should establish reusable patterns around high-level contract tests and source-adapter tests rather than low-level unit tests of framework plumbing.

## Out of Scope

- Full Google-Docs-style concurrent dashboard editing with live layout conflict resolution.
- Slack delivery in v1.
- Statistical or ML-based anomaly detection in v1.
- App store tracking in v1.
- Full template libraries with linked dashboard inheritance.
- Generic comments on every object in the system.
- Arbitrary code execution or unrestricted scripting inside Custom Metric formulas.
- Per-tenant schemas or per-tenant databases in v1.
- Separate microservices for each product capability in v1.
- Broad connector catalogs beyond RSS, price tracking, KPI ingest, and Manual Source.

## Further Notes

- This spec should be treated as the v1 product and architecture baseline for PulseIntel.
- The domain glossary in CONTEXT.md and the ADRs in docs/adr are part of the contract for future work and should be read alongside this spec.
- The implementation should favor preserving trust, provenance, and historical explainability over aggressively simplifying away domain history.
- The product differentiator is not just monitoring data, but helping teams collaborate around trustworthy evidence and shared interpretation.

Epic: Personal Knowledge Graphs (PKG) with Coherence Actions
items.body:
As a SynapseDX employee, I want a private knowledge graph searchable only by me, so I can use /mykg ask to check my remaining holiday allowance, book travel via TravelTrack, and log an expense, with all results stored only in my PKG, never visible to others, and fully deletable on demand or when I leave the company.

**Success Demo (must pass end-to-end):**

Employee runs /mykg ask "How much holiday do I have left?" → receives ephemeral answer sourced from HRIS; an audit node is written to the employee’s PKG.

Employee triggers TravelTrack booking from Slack (destination + dates) → booking is created via Coherence; booking node & edge stored only in employee’s PKG.

Employee logs an expense (amount, vendor, receipt) via Slack modal → expense node & receipt artifact written only to employee’s PKG.

Admin impersonation is not able to retrieve the employee’s PKG contents.

Employee runs “Forget me” → PKG data is deleted; re-running HRIS query still works (fresh pull), but prior travel/expense nodes are gone.

Offboarding event auto-deletes the PKG and revokes access tokens.

Labels: epic, personal-knowledge-graph, slack-integration, coherence-actions, privacy-compliance, demo

**Definition of Done (Epic)**

Private graph schema and storage live in dev/test/prod.

Slack app installed with proper scopes and manifest disclosure.
Definition of Done (Epic)

All blocking issues closed; end-to-end demo passes exactly as defined; privacy tests confirm non-disclosure; “Forget me” and offboarding deletion verified.

Runbook + README updated (setup, scopes, env vars, demo steps, rollback).



**Technical/Compliance Notes**

Slack Scopes: commands, chat:write, users:read, files:read, im:history (for DM context).

API Contracts: Secure REST/GraphQL for PKG CRUD; all requests signed and scoped to the employee’s identity.

Encryption: Data encrypted at rest and in transit; secrets managed via environment variables and GitHub Actions secrets.

Compliance: Adhere to Salesforce/Slack AI Data Policy—explicit disclosure to workspace admins that the app exports selected messages to a private knowledge graph.

**Dependencies:**

1️⃣Foundational / Blocking

“PKG Schema, Isolation & Storage” – create per-employee namespaces, enforce tenant isolation, encryption, and audit nodes.

“Identity, AuthZ, and Ephemeral Responses” – map Slack/SSO to each PKG and guarantee that only the owner can query it; ephemeral Slack replies only.

“HRIS Connector for Holiday Balance” – build the read-only HRIS integration (or stub if you haven’t selected a vendor yet).

“Privacy, Deletion (‘Forget me’), and Offboarding” – implement on-demand purge and automatic deletion on employee exit.

2️⃣ Interaction Layer

“Slack Commands, Shortcuts & Modals” – add /mykg ask, message shortcut, and modal UI for adding or querying personal data.

3️⃣ Coherence Action Connectors

“Coherence Action Connectors (TravelTrack & Expenses)” – wire PKG to Coherence so employees can book travel and log expenses, persisting those nodes privately.

4️⃣ Observability & Proof

“Observability & Proof of Non-Disclosure” – dashboards and audit logs proving only the owner accessed their PKG.

5️⃣ End-to-End Validation

“Demo Script & Automated Test (End-to-End)” – full CI scenario:

/mykg ask returns holiday balance,

TravelTrack booking and expense logging succeed,

no cross-tenant access,

“Forget me” purges all personal data.

6️⃣ Policy & Legal

“Policy & App Disclosure (Slack/Salesforce AI)” – update Slack manifest and Data-Processing Agreement to disclose outbound data use and guarantee no 3rd-party training.

items.body:
## Goal
Complete the existing `/api/v1` as the canonical read-only representation of everything available in the Reports dashboard, then make the HTML/htmx dashboard consume the same shared application/service contract. Future WebOS/Android clients are **out of scope**.

## Existing baseline (avoid duplication)
- `src/ocpp_reports/api_v1.py` already exposes `/api/v1/summary`, `/connectors`, `/transactions`, `/stations`, `/filters`, `/openapi.json`, registered by `web.py`.
- `web.py` also exposes legacy `/api/snapshot`, `/api/event-group`, and HTML transaction detail. These are existing routes; prior Reports HTTP contracts are not a compatibility requirement after coordinated fleet upgrade.
- Current v1 has incomplete parity: transactions only support view/page with hardcoded empty term/status/location/date and UTC; no JSON transaction detail, event group/history, source synchronization/freshness, timezone options, or complete dashboard filter/view semantics. Current dashboard still assembles HTML data via `read` rather than consuming the v1 contract.
- Preserve existing login/auth middleware, source allowlists, admin/operator/customer separation, tenant isolation and no-write behavior. Coordinate with #111, #114, #162, #185/#188 rather than duplicating their fixes.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Inventory all dashboard panels and fields (status summary, connectors/station 0/individual, source/station/location filters, transaction list/details, event groups, active energy, power, SoC, synchronization and provenance/freshness, timestamps and selectable timezones). Record field-to-endpoint parity matrix and unknown/unavailable semantics.
2. Versioned JSON schemas with stable pagination, validation, timestamps, timezone behavior, explicit nulls, error handling, OpenAPI examples; reuse existing warehouse projections and business rules (no second business logic).
3. Tenant and role-scoped authorization on **every** endpoint, including ID enumeration, details, filters, pagination, event history; reject cross-tenant requests, no information leakage, no unsafe CORS or unauthenticated fallback.
4. Dashboard and API use one application service/query layer; migrate dashboard without breaking HTML, htmx refresh/scroll, login/profile/password, current supported URLs. Preserve p95 <1s benchmark target.
5. Automated parity tests (HTML vs JSON for identical filters), negative auth/tenant tests, rebuild-from-forwarders verification (cursor-zero replay, counts, transaction/event evidence) and empty data tests, timezone/DST, energy/status aggregation and pagination, OpenAPI contract tests.
6. CI green, review and merge incremental PRs; deploy through the existing idempotent Ansible pipeline once, verify live API/dashboard and document acceptance. Follow the repository FIX-FORWARD policy: correct defects with a subsequent tested commit/deployment; preserve historical source SQLite evidence and rebuild Collector from retained Forwarder journals; old Reports binaries, prior HTTP contracts and unsupported export schemas need not remain compatible. Rollback, version reversal and Ansible compensations are not acceptance criteria. No WebOS/Android UI implementation.

## Upgrade scope
All Reports installations will be upgraded to the new version. No backwards compatibility requirement for old Reports releases or retired HTTP endpoints. Verify the supported current producer export schema separately; do not retain `ocpp-csms/export/v1` solely for compatibility unless it remains a supported input. Preserve Forwarder source SQLite evidence. Rebuild the Collector from a new empty database by replaying its complete retained local replication journals, verifying per-source cursors, counts and evidence. Collector schema migration is not mandatory when rebuild succeeds; do not delete old Collector before acceptance. This is a coordinated FIX-FORWARD upgrade.

## Suggested increments
A. Extract shared dashboard query/projection layer + parity inventory; B. complete v1 endpoints/filters/detail and schemas; C. migrate HTML/htmx to shared contract; D. auth/performance regression, deploy and field validation.

Do not close until deployed API and dashboard are verified against the same data and source-scoped identities.

## Collector rebuild acceptance (preproduction, November 2026)
- Audit retention/purge paths and confirm each Forwarder local `replication_changes` journal can be replayed from sequence zero. Absence of manual purges alone is not sufficient proof.
- Validate isolated new Collector ingest with paginated journal replay, matching source-specific event/transaction/rating/connector evidence, last sequence, and idempotent retries.
- **Current forwarder state is monotonic:** `forward_cursors` persists acknowledgments and `save_cursor` refuses regressions. A new Collector at cursor zero cannot be repopulated by an unchanged running Forwarder with an advanced cursor. Design and test an explicitly authorized, bounded replay/reseed mechanism before any real cutover; do not mutate production cursors during CI.
- Retain old Collector and all Forwarder databases until reconstruction has passed and been explicitly approved. No automatic rollback or Ansible compensation.
- A partial retained history must be reported as partial, not silently labeled complete. No compatibility requirement for old Reports releases or retired HTTP contracts.

items.title: Xero: no bring-your-own-app path for self-hosted operators (HubSpot has one, Xero does not)
items.body:
**What I want:** a bring-your-own-app path for Xero, like the one HubSpot already has.

**Why:** Xero has no long-lived static token. A non-AU/NZ/UK/US organisation can only use the Web app auth-code flow, which requires a Xero app the operator registers themselves — client id, secret, and a redirect URI they control. A self-hoster cannot borrow the project's app.

**How:**

1. Three operator-supplied fields, stored the way the HubSpot token already is:
   `XERO_CLIENT_ID`, `XERO_CLIENT_SECRET`, `XERO_REDIRECT_URI` (default `http://localhost:8088/xero/callback`).
2. Run the auth-code exchange; persist the refresh token and the selected tenant id.
3. **Manual fallback:** let the operator paste the full `...?code=...` URL back in. A browser outside the container cannot reach a callback listener inside it, so without this the flow is unusable in any container / remote / headless deployment.
4. Let the operator pick the tenant after consent — one grant can cover several, and the first one is often a demo company.

Two hard constraints worth building in from the start:

- The redirect URI host must be the literal `localhost`. `127.0.0.1` is rejected by Xero's WAF as a **blank 403** before the consent screen renders.
- The refresh token **rotates on every refresh**. Persist it atomically or the connection dies and needs full re-consent.

No credentials here — I'll paste my own into the UI once this exists.

---

Detail in the comments below: full entity/field schema, paging and incremental mechanics, the traps that produce *wrong numbers* rather than errors, and whether Xero's schema is fixed (it is).

items.title: Multi-tenancy: per-tenant ClickHouse database isolation via X-Scope-OrgID
items.body:
## Goal

Multi-tenancy: isolate each tenant's data in a **separate ClickHouse database**, with tenant identity carried by the de-facto ecosystem tenancy header **`X-Scope-OrgID`** (the same header the compatible metrics/logs/traces clients already send). One PulsusDB deployment serves many tenants; tenant A never sees tenant B's series/logs/traces.

## Tenant identification
- Every ingest and query request carries `X-Scope-OrgID: <tenant>`. Resolve the tenant from that header.
- Trust model: `X-Scope-OrgID` is trusted as set by an upstream auth gateway (standard for this ecosystem) — PulsusDB does not authenticate it; document that assumption.
- No-header / default behaviour: configurable — either a single default tenant (single-tenant back-compat) or reject with a clear error. Decide the default.

## Storage isolation
- Per-tenant ClickHouse **database** (e.g. one DB per `X-Scope-OrgID`). All table families (metrics/logs/traces + the sharding families) live inside the tenant's DB.
- **Schema/catalog reconcile per tenant:** the migration/reconcile machinery (crates/pulsus-schema) must create + migrate a tenant's DB on first use (or on provisioning), and keep every tenant's DB at the current migration version.
- Ingest routes writes to the tenant's DB; query reads from it.

## In-memory subsystems are per-tenant
The resident optimizers are per-tenant (each tenant has its own label/series space): the metrics `LabelCache`, the series-index membership set ([[link to #186 when built]]), the read-path resolution. Memory footprint scales with tenants × series — this needs a story (per-tenant cache sizing / eviction / the writer-vs-reader role split).

## Touchpoints (verify in source when designed)
- HTTP layer (all ingest + query routes: `/loki/api/v1/*`, `/api/*`, `/tempo/api/*`, PromQL, etc.) — extract + thread the tenant through the request.
- `pulsus-schema` catalog/reconcile — per-tenant DB provisioning + migration.
- Ingest (metrics/logs/traces) — tenant-scoped table targets.
- Query/read-path — tenant-scoped DB + per-tenant caches.
- Tenant lifecycle: create-on-first-write vs pre-provisioned; tenant listing; optional per-tenant limits (cardinality/rate).

## Note
This is a substantial architectural addition touching ingest, query, schema, and the in-memory caches — it likely warrants a **design spike first** (like the series-index spike #186) before implementation. Relates to the pure-database scope (PulsusDB is a datastore; tenancy is a datastore concern, not a monitoring one).

items.title: 🌱 🩺 [Admin] Task · Integration health board — per-connector status for webhooks, Google, SSO and email
items.body:
## 🎯 Goal
Silent integration failure is how trust in an integration layer dies. An admin today cannot tell that a webhook has been failing for a week, that a user's Google Calendar token expired, or that the SSO certificate is about to lapse — even though the product faithfully records all three. We already proved the pattern works for email; this task applies it to every other connector on one screen. It is mostly reading data that already exists and rendering it, which makes it a well-bounded first issue.

## 🔍 Current state
- **The pattern to copy**: `src/lib/emailHealth.ts:11-46` — an `EmailHealth` interface (`lastOkAt`, `lastErrorAt`, `lastError`, `failuresSinceOk`, `attempts24h`), derived from the `EmailLog` ledger rather than a separate marker *"so the two can never drift apart"*, with `sanitizeEmailError` at `:25-28` stripping anything address-shaped before it leaves the module.
- **Google Calendar**: `prisma/schema.prisma:2636-2639` stores `lastSyncAt` and `lastError` with the comment *"Operational state, so a broken connection is visible in the UI instead of failing silently"* — but it is only rendered on the user's own `/account` card (`src/components/GoogleCalendarCard.tsx`), never to an admin. `src/app/api/admin/integrations/google/status/route.ts` reports configured/enabled/connection-count only.
- **Webhooks**: nothing to read yet — the delivery log arrives with #1681/#1695. Until it lands, derive what is derivable (subscription count, active/paused, last created) and leave a clearly-marked slot for delivery health.
- **SSO**: certificate expiry is not surfaced anywhere; `docs/sso-saml.md` has the current picture.
- **Inbound receivers**: `src/app/api/webhooks/jaas/route.ts` and `src/app/api/inbound-email/route.ts` both answer 404 when unconfigured — worth showing as configured/not-configured.
- The page this lands on is `src/app/admin/integrations/page.tsx` (client component, loads `/api/admin/webhooks`, `/api/admin/api-keys` and `/api/admin/integrations/google/status` in one `Promise.all`).
- **#1607** is building `/admin/operations` (scheduled-job runs + error rate) and will call this task's `GET /api/admin/integrations/health` for a summary roll-up. That route is therefore a shared read surface, not a page-private helper — see § Scope boundary.

## 🛠 What to build
1. `src/lib/integrationHealth.ts` — one `getIntegrationHealth()` returning an array of `{ connector, state: 'ok' | 'degraded' | 'failing' | 'not_configured', lastOkAt, lastErrorAt, lastError, detail }`, each entry derived from the ledger that connector already writes. Reuse `getEmailHealth()` for the email row rather than re-deriving it.
2. `GET /api/admin/integrations/health` with a route-level `requireAdmin()` in the same shape as the sibling admin routes. Keep the response shape stable and self-describing — #1607's operations console counts states from it.
3. A health section on `/admin/integrations`: one row per connector, a coloured state badge, "last ok" and "last error" as relative times (`src/lib/relativeTime.ts` is already imported by that page), and the sanitized error text. EN/TR/DE strings in the existing `integrations` block (`src/i18n/dictionaries.ts:2155`).
4. Every error string passes through a shared sanitizer before rendering — generalise `sanitizeEmailError` rather than writing a second one. A Google error can contain an account address; an SSO error can contain a certificate subject.

## ✅ Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One screen shows the state of email, webhooks, Google Calendar, SSO and the two inbound receivers
- [ ] A connector that has never been configured reads "not configured", not "failing"
- [ ] No rendered error text contains an email address or a token
- [ ] The health route checks ADMIN in the handler, not in the component
- [ ] Health is derived from the existing ledgers — no new "last state" column is introduced that could drift
- [ ] `GET /api/admin/integrations/health` returns a per-connector `state` a caller can count without parsing prose (#1607 depends on this)
- [ ] `npm run build` passes
- [ ] `npm run check:i18n` passes
- [ ] an e2e spec asserts the board renders and that a non-admin gets 401/403 from the route
- [ ] a release fragment `releases/unreleased/integration-health-board.json` is added (`bump: minor`, EN/TR/DE `notes`)

## 🇹🇷 Türkçe özet
Sessiz entegrasyon arızası, bir entegrasyon katmanına duyulan güvenin ölme biçimidir. Bugün bir yönetici bir webhook'un bir haftadır başarısız olduğunu, bir kullanıcının Google jetonunun süresinin dolduğunu ya da SSO sertifikasının bitmek üzere olduğunu göremiyor — üstelik ürün üçünü de düzgünce kaydediyor (`GoogleCalendarConnection.lastError` şemada var, hiçbir yönetici ekranı okumuyor). E-posta için bu deseni zaten kanıtladık: sağlık, ayrı bir "son durum" sütunundan değil, bağlayıcının zaten yazdığı kayıttan türetiliyor ki ikisi asla ayrışmasın. Bu görev aynı deseni tek bir ekranda diğer bağlayıcılara uyguluyor. Tek katı kural: ekrana basılan hiçbir hata metni e-posta adresi veya jeton içermemeli — mevcut `sanitizeEmailError` genelleştirilecek, ikincisi yazılmayacak. Ağırlıklı olarak var olan veriyi okuyup göstermek olduğu için staj için uygun. **Kapsam:** entegrasyon sağlığının tek sahibi bu görev; #1607'nin `/admin/operations` sayfası bu rotayı sadece özet olarak okuyup buraya link verecek.

## 🤖 Agent prompt
```
Repo: 21072026/internship. Task under story #1987 (epic #1977). Junior-friendly.

Objective: one admin health board showing the state of every integration connector,
derived from the ledgers each connector already writes.

Open first:
  src/lib/emailHealth.ts:11-46             (THE pattern — copy its shape and its reasoning:
                                            derive from the ledger, scrub PII at :25-28)
  prisma/schema.prisma:2617-2646           (GoogleCalendarConnection.lastSyncAt/lastError)
  src/app/api/admin/integrations/google/status/route.ts
  src/components/GoogleCalendarCard.tsx    (where lastError is shown to the USER today)
  src/app/admin/integrations/page.tsx      (the page you extend; note its Promise.all load)
  src/app/api/admin/webhooks/route.ts:16   (the requireAdmin shape to copy)
  src/i18n/dictionaries.ts:2155            (integrations block — EN/TR/DE)
  src/app/api/webhooks/jaas/route.ts, src/app/api/inbound-email/route.ts

Constraints:
- Derive health from existing ledgers. Do NOT add a new "last state" column — the email
  module's own comment explains why a separate marker drifts.
- Generalise sanitizeEmailError; never render raw error text that may hold an address,
  a certificate subject or a token.
- requireAdmin() inside the route handler, not in the component.
- Webhook delivery health arrives with #1681/#1695 — leave a clearly-marked slot rather
  than inventing a second delivery record.
- This task owns integration health for the whole product. #1607 (/admin/operations) will
  call GET /api/admin/integrations/health for a state roll-up, so keep the per-connector

  Give any new input a data-testid.
Done: e2e for the board + non-admin refusal, build green, release fragment, PR opened
with the preview URL posted.
```

## 🔗 Scope boundary

#1607 and this issue both surface integration health to an admin. **This issue owns integration health**: the derivation module `src/lib/integrationHealth.ts`, the route `GET /api/admin/integrations/health`, the generalised error sanitizer and the per-connector board on `/admin/integrations`. #1607 owns the **scheduled-job runs and the error rate** on `/admin/operations`, and consumes this route for a one-line state roll-up that links here. Do not create a second integration-health module, route, sanitizer or board — and do not build job-run or error-rate surfaces in this task.

items.title: Cloudflare Tunnel per tenant: API, token scope, limits, edge-certificate coverage, cloudflared on the sidecar
items.body:
Part of #179

## Question

Cloudflare Tunnel facts the reach design depends on, from primary sources (developers.cloudflare.com, api.cloudflare.com schema, cloudflared docs/releases):
- API: create a tunnel per tenant with an account-scoped token (`POST /accounts/{account}/cfd_tunnel`), get its **connector token** (`…/cfd_tunnel/{id}/token`), remote-managed ingress config (`PUT …/configurations`: ingress rules with `hostname`, wildcard hostnames like `*.web12.tc42.uk`, `originRequest` {`originServerName`, `caPool`, `noTLSVerify`, `http2Origin`}), CNAME target `<uuid>.cfargotunnel.com` (proxied), delete tunnel + cleanup of connections. Minimum token permissions (Account › Cloudflare Tunnel › Edit, Zone › DNS › Edit, Zone › Zone › Read?) and whether one token can serve both the existing DNS-01 use and tunnels.
- Limits: tunnels per account, ingress rules per tunnel, hostnames per zone, connections per tunnel, and rate limits.
- **Edge certificates**: exactly what Universal SSL covers (apex + one label?), what a name like `web12.e2e.sc.tc42.uk` or `*.web12.tc42.uk` needs (Advanced Certificate Manager, Total TLS, cost), and whether a tunnel hostname that Universal SSL does not cover fails or serves an untrusted cert.
- cloudflared on the sidecar: Debian trixie packaging (apt repo), running as a systemd unit with a connector token, replicas/HA, how config changes propagate (remote-managed), CPU/memory footprint, outbound requirements.
- Origin TLS: does cloudflared verify a publicly trusted (Let's Encrypt) origin cert by default, and how `originServerName` interacts with SNI; behaviour with staging (untrusted) certs for e2e.

Deliver `docs/research/cloudflare-tunnel-per-tenant-2026-09-13.md` with a recommendation on token scope, config management and edge-certificate strategy.

items.title: Owner control center: live dispatcher/Muse status, visible approvals, natural-language instructions
items.body:
## Start here — owner operating guide (November 9, 2026)

**[Open the live status and dependency map](https://github.com/killbill2792/aicafe/issues/411#issuecomment-6752417190)** · **[Read the permanent product blueprint and original decision links](https://github.com/killbill2792/aicafe/blob/main/docs/plans/owner-living-blueprint.md)** · [See the proven blueprint change, PR #416](https://github.com/killbill2792/aicafe/pull/416).

**Everyday use:** Open the status/map for pending decisions, each PR's next actor and verification; open the linked original PR before approving its exact scope. For a new idea/fix, tell your connected ChatGPT conversation **“Read the AI CAFE blueprint and current GitHub PRs; brainstorm and show me the changed architecture and PR tasks before coding.”** When satisfied, say **“Record my exact approval in GitHub on the related issue/PR, and update the existing blueprint and authorized task queue as needed.”** Check that the GitHub write succeeded; a chat message by itself does **not** become an authenticated approval. The existing dispatcher then reconciles GitHub and continues eligible tasks through Muse/ChatGPT/Claude. To request a read-only status update, comment `refresh status` here and reload this page when the trusted GitHub workflow has finished.

**What works now:** PR #416 merged the read-only living blueprint and GitHub-derived dependency map into the *existing* Actions-owned dashboard comment; dispatcher reconciliation is automatic but GitHub's five-minute schedule is best-effort. **What is not yet automatic:** writing every future chat decision into GitHub, regenerating prose decisions without a reviewed GitHub change, push/live-refreshing this already-open browser tab, or hosting an authenticated standalone GitHub Pages website. Those are **future scoped proposals**, not permissions to create a second dispatcher, expose private data, or bypass owner/CI/Codex gates. Preserve this issue as the single place to design the trusted chat-to-GitHub write-through and owner-view enhancements if requested.

---

## Live owner dashboard

[**Open the current AI CAFE dispatcher status**](https://github.com/killbill2792/aicafe/issues/411#issuecomment-6752417190). This single GitHub Actions-owned comment updates in place with verified reconciliation results. Reply **refresh status** to this issue to request a read-only refresh; answer scoped approvals on the exact linked PR, not in the dashboard comment.

---

## Owner request — one understandable control center for the EXISTING dispatcher and Muse
The AI CAFE owner cannot currently see where a task is stuck, where approval was requested, whether Muse actually delivered a GitHub continuation, or why a clean Codex review did not cause a draft to merge. The owner wants to **read and speak in normal English** to the dispatcher and Muse from one owner-friendly place, without editing JSON or hunting for invisible PR-body markers.

This is a **tracking/design request, not authorization to code, expand task paths, deploy, approve existing questions, or override merge/production gates**. Obtain an exact, owner-approved implementation scope and reuse the current dispatcher/queue/ledger/courier paths under AGENTS.md. No second task queue, agent, cron, secret store, or parallel approval authority.

### Concrete observed failures (November 9, 2026)
- #404 (POS0e) is an open draft, has red baseline and two P1 Codex findings. Its actionable owner scope question appears in [issue comment #6741376971](https://github.com/killbill2792/aicafe/pull/404#issuecomment-6741376971) with the `needs-owner-decision` label, but no matching live `aicafe-owner-question` marker in PR body; the private ledger's pending owner-alert list omitted this question. An owner should never have to inspect an HTML comment or know a parser rule to see an approval.
- #405, #406 and #407 have owner questions in PR bodies, but private owner notices were still `planned` and had **no verified Muse owner-notice delivery** at the inspection. Show this distinctly from "delivered" or "approved."
- Private ledger showed three `repair_ci` courier actions for POS0b/c/d in `planned`, with no submitted receipt. Do not claim that Muse failed or that a prompt was delivered without checking its authenticated receipt.
- #406/#407 have clean Codex current-head evidence in their PR conversation, yet the full baselines failed; #407 acceptance execution was skipped. All #405–407 are stacked on unmerged #404. Correctly explain why drafts cannot auto-ready/merge and distinguish gate status from stale ledger Codex summary.
- Dispatcher auto-ready/merge work landed in #410, but current full-proof barriers and actual runtime settings/receipts need operator visibility. Do not equate code merged with a verified live automation cycle.

### Required one owner-facing dashboard
1. **Today / Needs me / Tasks / Dispatcher history / Muse deliveries** in one clear private, authenticated view. Plain language first, with exact source links and last-refreshed timestamp. Owner must see what happened while offline, what's currently executing, what's queued, what is held, and next responsible party.
2. For each task show: task name and PR; coding scope approval (independent of production permission); coder; dependency/stack base; draft/ready/merged; CI broken job and execution link; exact-head Codex clean/findings; acceptance artifact status; integrated_proven; last commit/activity; owner question and direct actionable link; dispatcher proposed/sent action; Muse assigned/planned/submitted/receipt/uncertain and next eligibility/retry.
3. **Owner decisions must never disappear:** reconcile every open `needs-owner-decision` label, owner question in PR body AND trusted owner question in PR conversation/comments. Surface a visible full question with source URL, options, what permission would change, affected files/PR, and whether already answered. Do not treat an HTML comment as user-facing notice; do not infer approval from a courier receipt, clean Codex, PR merge, or chat transcript.
4. **Human-readable chronological history:** task/PR status transitions; dispatcher reconciliations; approval requests and recorded decisions; queued/rescheduled/cancelled actions; Muse delivery receipt; verified code activity; tests/reviews; why each merge gate passed/failed. Preserve source GitHub IDs, SHAs, workflow URLs and timestamps; distinguish `observed`, `inferred`, `not verified`, and `not delivered`.
5. **Talk to dispatcher/Muse in normal English:** the owner can ask "What is blocked?", "Show my pending approvals", "Why not merged?", "Tell Muse to continue the existing chat", "Hold task X", and "Approve precisely this scope". Translate only authorized actions into the existing trusted GitHub owner-question/queue path with a preview/exact effect and immutable audit receipt; require explicit owner confirmation for approval/scope/production changes. Never rely on private ChatGPT transcript as implicit GitHub approval. Muse remains a courier, not a coding/decision agent.
6. **No false green:** distinguish Codex review completed/clean at current SHA from all CI jobs, unresolved review threads, acceptance evidence job+artifact, stacked predecessor merged-main integration, owner decision and production gates. Display actionable failed checks and next owner (coder vs dispatcher vs Muse vs human).
7. **Privacy/security:** preserve private ledger/prompts, chat URLs, user identifiers, auth tokens and HMAC signals in the existing private boundary. Do not leak them to public issue/PR/workflow logs, and do not expose a privileged action endpoint without authenticated owner checks.
8. **Proof:** red-to-green tests for missing #404 comment question, hidden-marker visibility, planned-not-delivered Muse receipt, stale Codex summary despite current-head clean, red CI blocking auto-merge, correct post-receipt follow-up, duplicate suppression, owner-approved instruction routing, safe read-only history, and zero bypass of existing approval/merge rules. Demonstrate a complete owner journey from PR owner question -> dashboard notice -> authenticated owner decision -> dispatcher correction -> Muse verified delivery -> coder activity/CI -> proof-gated ready/merge (using disposable/test PRs, no production action).

### Required first step
Provide a small architecture/file-ownership and security plan on this issue for owner approval, identifying which **existing** dispatcher/ledger/owner-event code will be extended and where the authenticated owner view should live. Do not start a second workflow. Do not interrupt current POS0 PR repair or alter their signed scopes merely to make a UI look green.

**Owner-visible success criterion:** The owner opens one page, immediately knows whether GitHub, Muse, a coder, failing tests, an unresolved comment, or the owner is the next actor, and can give authorized instructions in normal English with tracked receipt and no hidden requests.

items.body:
## Current context

**Current state:** GitHub records this issue as closed.

**Context:** Azure SQL change data capture (CDC) records row changes for Debezium, the connector that reads SQL Server changes into Kafka. Kafka is the event log used by the platform. This issue covers the self-hosted CI runner, database permissions, and the security boundary for the capture path. **Why it matters:** the runner and grants determine whether the container checks can exercise the same tenant onboarding and CDC path used by the platform.

**Outcome:** PRs #160, #161, and #163 merged on 2026-08-25. They delivered the runner foundation and tenant database grants. Follow-on issue #68 was implemented in merged PRs #183, #186, and #187: the onboarding and connector path now carry the SQL Server signaling-table behavior and a Kafka Connect Filter, a record transform that drops signaling-table rows from the business event stream, needed for incremental snapshots. Current `main` at `fb29eeb3160bbce0c42469560609d254aabc272f` is not one consistent public contract. `docs/blueprint.md` and `docs/specs/11-infra-disposable.md` still contain Outbox-only and read-only wording, while `tools/onboarding/tenant-onboarding.sql` and `connect/connectors/connector-template.json` contain the `dbo.DebeziumSignal` CDC and Filter path. The documentation correction remains an explicit follow-on boundary.

**Repository evidence:** [PR #160](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/cdc-platform-azure/pull/160), [PR #161](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/cdc-platform-azure/pull/161), and [PR #163](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/cdc-platform-azure/pull/163) (merged 2026-08-25); [PR #183](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/cdc-platform-azure/pull/183), [PR #186](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/cdc-platform-azure/pull/186), and [PR #187](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/cdc-platform-azure/pull/187) (merged 2026-08-27). The current source files are [tenant-onboarding.sql](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/cdc-platform-azure/blob/fb29eeb3160bbce0c42469560609d254aabc272f/tools/onboarding/tenant-onboarding.sql) and [connector-template.json](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/cdc-platform-azure/blob/fb29eeb3160bbce0c42469560609d254aabc272f/connect/connectors/connector-template.json).

## Unknowns

The current code and public documentation disagree about whether SQL Server CDC includes `dbo.DebeziumSignal` and whether the connector has a write grant on that table. The repository does not claim live Azure snapshot behavior or production-scale proof here.

## Historical evidence

The original issue body is retained below unchanged. It preserves the original behavior, blockers, paths, verification method, acceptance checklist, scope boundaries, size forecast, dates, and links.

<details>
<summary>Original issue body</summary>

## Behavior

An onboarding runner reads the tenant manifest and applies, per tenant database: the tenant schema including the Outbox table with its TraceParent column and the DebeziumSignal watermarking table, CDC on `dbo.Outbox` only, Change Tracking on `dbo.WorkflowTask` only, `ALLOW_SNAPSHOT_ISOLATION` on the database, and the TenantInfo claim row. Running it twice changes nothing and throws nothing. This T-SQL is the canonical definition of the tenant schema for the whole repository.

## Blocked by

- #31 (D3)

## Paths

- `tools/onboarding/`
- `tests/Lexfield.TestSupport/`
- `tests/Lexfield.Onboarding.Tests/`

## Verification

Method: containers

Run the runner against a Testcontainers SQL Server. Assert tables exist, including `dbo.DebeziumSignal`; `sys.databases.is_cdc_enabled`; a capture instance on `dbo.Outbox` and none on `dbo.WorkflowTask`; `sys.change_tracking_tables` contains `WorkflowTask` and nothing else; `sys.databases.snapshot_isolation_state` is on; the `TenantInfo` row holds the expected tenantId. Then run the whole thing a second time and assert nothing changed and nothing threw, which is the actual idempotency claim.

## Acceptance checklist

- [ ] `dbo.Outbox` is created with the nullable `TraceParent` column
- [ ] `dbo.DebeziumSignal` is created per tenant database for incremental-snapshot watermarking
- [ ] CDC is enabled on `dbo.Outbox` and on no other table
- [ ] Change Tracking is enabled on `dbo.WorkflowTask` and on no other table
- [ ] `ALLOW_SNAPSHOT_ISOLATION` is enabled on each tenant database
- [ ] The grant of INSERT and SELECT on `dbo.DebeziumSignal` only, to the connector identity, is authored in the canonical onboarding T-SQL; business and CDC tables stay read-only. Its execution against a real Entra user is verified in the live user-creation ticket
- [ ] The `TenantInfo` row holds the tenantId from the manifest
- [ ] A second run of the whole runner changes nothing and throws nothing, asserted rather than argued
- [ ] TestSupport switched to execute the canonical onboarding scripts; provisional DDL deleted

## Out of scope

- `CREATE USER FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER` and the execution of its grants (including the `dbo.DebeziumSignal` grant), which need a real Entra-backed server and are a separate live ticket. The grant T-SQL is authored here as part of the canonical scripts; only its execution is out of scope
- Connector registration, which is the connect area
- Any change to the schema contract itself; this ticket implements the contract, it does not redesign it

## Size forecast

8 files, 420 lines

---

Area: `infra/disposable` | Wave 2 | Plan id `D4` | Generated from `docs/specs/` by /to-tickets.
