items.title: [SPEC] §4.2 Full 35-Schema DDL (Schemas 13-35): Remaining schema DDL for credit, coaching, pathway, billing, notification, partner, application, event-log, audit-log, vector-embeddings, BAI, marketplace, lender, EDO, and telemetry schemas
items.body:
---
owner: service:platform
depends_on: ["1625"]
blocks: []
spec_sections: ["§4.2"]
blueprint_sections: ["§17", "§33"]
maturity_target: Foundation
acceptance:
  - DDL committed for schemas 13-35 covering: credit (personal and business bureau data, tradeline inventory, CLI tracking), coaching (session logs, prompt registry, coaching milestones), pathway (capital plan, product eligibility, submission history), billing (subscription tiers, invoice history, referral fee ledger), notification (email/SMS event log), partner (lender partner profiles, cohort subscriptions), application (loan application submissions, outcome tracking), event-log (immutable platform event stream), audit-log (PII access and mutation audit trail), vector-embeddings (Pinecone record references), BAI (BPFS model outputs, BLIN lender intelligence snapshots, BII industry benchmarks, BMS macro signals), marketplace (capital product catalog, deal flow records), lender (lender profiles, underwriting criteria), EDO (EDO tenant profiles, licensing terms), and telemetry (Snowflake staging tables)
  - Every schema has tenant_id column with PostgreSQL RLS policies enforcing per-tenant isolation
  - Every schema has created_at, updated_at timestamps and soft-delete pattern (deleted_at nullable) where applicable
  - Foreign key relationships documented between schemas with explicit cascade and restrict policies
  - Service ownership declared for each schema: which service has write access, which services have read-only access
  - Index strategy documented per schema: primary key indexes, tenant_id composite indexes, high-cardinality lookup indexes
  - All PII-containing columns tagged in DDL comments per §4.4 field classification standard (#1653)
  - Schemas 13-35 DDL passes forward and rollback migration tests per §14.1 (#1697)
---

## Details

Engineering spec §4.2 covers the full DDL for all 35 proprietary data schemas that form the BANKABLE IQ data moat described in Blueprint §33. Issue #1625 covered schemas 1-12 (identity, org, readiness, compliance, vault, credit, coaching, pathway, billing, notification, partner, application). Issue #1650 covered two specific tables (identity.users and readiness.snapshots). This issue covers the remaining schemas 13-35 that are referenced throughout the spec but not yet tracked as implementation work.

The 35-schema architecture is the defensive moat described in Blueprint §33 and §34: the compounding data strategy where each platform interaction adds signal to the proprietary dataset that eventually enables the BPFS predictive model to outperform any competitor without that dataset.

Key decisions:
- Schema count: Blueprint v1.8 specifies 35 schemas (25 readiness + 5 credit + 5 BAI-powered). The DDL must account for all 35.
- Event log schema is append-only (no updates, no deletes) - enforced at the application layer with RLS that blocks UPDATE and DELETE
- Audit log requires field-level encryption for any PII per §4.4 (#1653)
- Telemetry schemas are Snowflake staging tables, not PostgreSQL — they receive data from the Kafka/EventBridge event bus via a Snowflake Kafka connector or Fivetran feed

Must align with §4.1 Schemas 1-12 (#1625), §4.4 Data Lifecycle (#1653), §4.3 Data Warehouse (#1674), §8.4 Message Queue (#1693), Blueprint §33 Data Moat Architecture (#1640), and §34 35 Data Schemas.

References: engineering-spec-v1.0.html §4.2 35 Schemas Full DDL

items.title: RFC: Omni as event backbone — event contracts, ingress idempotency, causality, and declarative subscription
items.body:
# RFC: Omni as event backbone — event contracts, ingress idempotency, causality, and declarative subscription

## Motivation

Today, omnichannel means "text channels" (WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram, Discord). But the architecture already underneath — NATS JetStream, event envelope, automations, webhook sources, DLQ, replay — is a **generic event bus** that only happens to serve messages.

This RFC's thesis: **embrace omni as the platform's event controller**, where any source (GitHub, ClickUp, Drive, calendar, LLM provider billing, meeting minutes, third-party apps via webhook) emits events that agents "listen" to and act on — with deterministic trace-back of the causal chain and state that can be rebuilt/diffed from the journal.

This is not a pivot. It formalizes what the code already half-does, closing the gaps that today prevent plugging in external sources safely.

## Current state (audited in the code)

What already exists and where:

| Piece | Where | State |
|---|---|---|
| Bus | NATS JetStream, subjects `{eventType}.{channelType}.{instanceId}` (`packages/core/src/events/nats/`) | ✅ live, `consumer_offsets` with gap detection |
| Envelope | `OmniEvent` in `packages/core/src/events/types.ts` — `id`, `type`, `payload`, `metadata` (`correlationId`, `traceId`, `timings`, `ingestMode`, `streamSequence`, `envelopeVersion`/`tenantId`) | ✅ versioned, tenant-aware (G5/ADR-0008) |
| Journal | event persistence (`packages/api/src/plugins/event-persistence.ts`) + `payload_storage_config` with per-type retention | ✅ ~349k events today |
| Handler dedup | `processed_events` (PK `event_id + handler`) via `packages/api/src/lib/idempotency.ts` | ✅ but CONSUMER-side only |
| DLQ | `dead_letter_events` with auto/manual retry, `next_auto_retry_at` | ✅ |
| External ingress | `webhook_sources` — name, `expected_headers`, enabled, stats | ⚠️ validates header presence only, no schema, no dedup |
| Routing | `automations` — trigger by type + conditions (11 operators, and/or) + actions (`webhook`, `send_message`, `emit_event`, `log`, `call_agent`) + debounce + priority + `automation_logs` | ✅ but imperative wiring |
| Replay | replay sessions (`packages/core/src/events/replay.ts`), journey tracing via checkpoints | ✅ |
| Namespaces | `core` / `custom.*` / `system.*` (`isCoreEvent`/`isCustomEvent`/`isSystemEvent`) | ✅ convention exists |

The event backbone's skeleton **is already standing** — and the automation engine is more robust than it looks from the outside: per-instance queues with bounded concurrency and backpressure (`maxQueueDepth`), per-conversation debounce, subscription reconciler. The gaps below are all at the **edge** (ingress) and in the **event's semantics** (identity, causality, contract), not in execution — the work is surgical, not structural.

> Gaps G0–G5 were verified by reading the actual execution paths (`routes/v2/webhooks.ts`, `services/webhooks.ts`, `automations/engine.ts`, `automations/actions.ts`), not just the schema.

## Gaps and proposals

### G0 — Ingress security → extracted to its own issue: #928

Hardening of the generic receiver (source signature verification, `autoCreate` off by default, dedicated ingress route) has a dedicated issue: **#928**. Only the dependency remains here: it is a **prerequisite for Phase 3** — no real external source gets plugged in before it closes.

### G1 — Event contract registry (payload schemas)

**Today (verified):** the payload enters as-is — literal comment on the route: "The payload is passed through to the event system as-is". A `custom.github.push` event has no guaranteed shape — consumers just hope it's right.

**Aggravating factor — type collapse:** the webhook event type is fixed: `custom.webhook.{source}`. GitHub push, PR, issue, and release ALL arrive as `custom.webhook.github`, and telling them apart is left to payload conditions in each automation. The registry must include **source→semantic-type mapping** (e.g., extract from `X-GitHub-Event` → `custom.github.push`), otherwise each schema becomes a giant per-source union.

**Proposal:** an `event_schemas` table (`event_type` unique → JSON Schema + version). Rules:

- Every automation `emit_event` and every webhook-source ingress validates against the registered schema BEFORE publishing to the bus. Invalid payload → DLQ with reason `schema_validation_failed`, never enters the journal as a valid fact.
- Core types keep schemas derived from the TS types (auto-generated, not manually duplicated).
- New external source = register the types it emits + their schemas. CLI: `omni events schema register/list/get`.
- Schema evolution is additive (new optional field) or a version bump in the `event_type` (e.g., `github.push.v2`) — never silent mutation.

Without this, the bus becomes a payload dump and every consumer reimplements defensive validation.

### G2 — INGRESS idempotency (dedup at the door, not in the handler)

**Today (verified):** `processed_events` dedupes by `(event_id, handler)` — it protects a consumer from reprocessing the SAME event. But `WebhooksService.receive()` calls `generateId()` fresh on every request and publishes directly, with no dedup lookup anywhere on the path. If GitHub redelivers a webhook (and it does), that becomes two distinct events in the journal → two automation firings.

**Proposal:** an `idempotency_key` column on the persisted event, with a unique index, derived from the SOURCE's identity:

```
github:   "github:{X-GitHub-Delivery}"
clickup:  "clickup:{event_id}"
slack:    "slack:{team_id}:{channel}:{event_ts}"
generic:  configurable template per webhook_source (e.g., "{source}:{payload.id}")
```

- Insert collision = duplicate → respond 200 to the emitter (ack), create no event, bump the source's dup counter.
- `webhook_sources` gains an `idempotency_key_template` field (required for new sources; existing sources migrate with default `{source}:{sha256(body)}`).
- Internal events (`emit_event`) derive the key from the parent event: `derived:{parent_event_id}:{automation_id}:{action_index}` — re-running the same automation over the same event doesn't duplicate the emission.

Principle: **the database dedupes via unique index, not application logic.**

### G3 — Explicit causality (`causationId`)

**Today (verified):** `metadata.correlationId` groups a flow and `traceId` links to tracing, but no field points to **which event caused this event**. Correlation gives you the flow's bag of events; it doesn't give you the tree.

**Aggravating factor — the correlation chain ALREADY breaks between hops today:** `executeEmitEventAction()` propagates `correlationId: context.payload.correlationId` — it reads from the **payload** (almost always empty), not from the triggering event's `metadata.correlationId`. And webhook `receive()` sets `correlationId = eventId` (self-reference). Result: the chain `webhook → automation → emit_event → automation → agent` is born with a fresh correlation at every hop — the tracing we think we have, we don't.

**Proposal:** `metadata.causationId` (id of the immediate parent event), stamped automatically:

- Automation `emit_event` → `causationId = the event that triggered the automation`.
- Message sent by an agent in response → `causationId = the message.received that woke the agent`.
- External ingress event → `causationId` null (root), fresh `correlationId`.

With that:

1. **Deterministic trace-back:** `omni events trace <id>` walks the chain up to the root and down the fan-out — "why did the agent send this message?" becomes a recursive query, not log archaeology.
2. **Queryable causality graph:** which root events generate the most work, where flows die midway, which automation amplifies events (1→N).
3. **Diff between states:** since the journal is immutable and ordered (streamSequence), any projection's state at T1 vs T2 = replay of the range. Replay sessions already exist; formalizing a "projection" as a named consumer with its own offset makes diffing a first-class operation.

Cost: one column + stamp discipline at the 3 publish points. Highest return per line of code in this RFC.

### G4 — Declarative subscription (the agent declares what it listens to and what it emits)

**Today:** wiring event→agent means hand-creating an automation (`--trigger X --action call_agent`). It works, but the wiring is imperative and external to the agent: you can't ask "who listens to `clickup.task.status_changed`?" or "who is allowed to emit `deploy.requested`?" without sweeping automations.

**Proposal:** the agent (record in `agents`) gains a subscription manifest:

```yaml
accepts:
  - event: clickup.task.status_changed
    filter: { list_id: "901300373349" }
publishes:
  - event: review.parecer.ready
```

- `accepts` generates/compiles the routing automations (the `automations` table becomes the compiled plan, not the source of truth).
- `publishes` is an allowlist: an agent only emits declared types, payload validated by the registry (G1). Emission outside the manifest → refused + DLQ.
- The agent↔event graph becomes queryable: `omni agents graph` shows who produces/consumes what — the living documentation of inter-agent dependencies.

Phase 2 of this RFC — depends on G1 (schemas) and G2 (derived keys).

### G5 — Transactional publication (a run's emissions only go out if the run completes)

**Today (verified):** actions execute sequentially and **continue on failure, by design** — literal comment in `executeActions()`: "We don't stop on failure - just log and continue [...] failures logged but don't stop sequence". It was a requirement of the original wish and makes sense for `log`/`send_message`, but for `emit_event` it means partial effects on the bus are the default behavior: an `emit_event` executes even after a failed previous action, and a `call_agent` failing afterwards undoes nothing.

**Proposal:** emissions requested during a run (of an automation or an agent) are **accumulated** and published in order only when the run completes successfully. A failed/cancelled run publishes zero — the retry (which already exists via DLQ) restarts clean, and G2 guarantees a successful retry doesn't duplicate.

Contained scope: changes the automation executor and the agent dispatch path; the bus doesn't change.

### G6 (future, out of scope for this RFC) — Waits/continuations

An agent publishes a request and stays "waiting" for a future event matching type + fields (e.g., emitted `vendor.fix.requested`, wakes when `vendor.metric.updated` for that resource arrives). Recorded here as direction; depends on mature G3/G4.

### G7 — Subscription surface (consumer-attached pub/sub)

This RFC's sub side is entirely **platform-push**: `accepts` (G4) compiles to routing that pushes to a consumer via `call_agent`/`webhook` — the platform knows and manages every consumer (durability, retry, DLQ). What's missing is the second mode every mature event system has: **consumer-attaches** — an external, possibly ephemeral client (a CLI agent session, a dashboard, a debugging human) subscribing to the bus with a filter and receiving events, without becoming an HTTP endpoint or appearing in any manifest. NATS (already the bus underneath) has subscribe; Kafka has consumers; Postgres has LISTEN — omni exposes none of it outside the runtime.

Dogfooding surfaced the cost (#925 dogfood comment): agent sessions orchestrating flows wait for effects with hand-rolled polling (`until`-loops, `tail -f`, repeated `messages search`) because there is no way to just *attach and wait*.

Concrete path:
- **First step is filed as #966**: expose custom events in the journal/stream (today `events stream` filters by type but custom events never appear in it) and add `omni events wait` — a one-shot blocking subscription (type + payload-field filters, timeout, event JSON on stdout). Ephemeral, broadcast, no durable state — the cheapest useful attach primitive, and the CLI-level stopgap for G6.
- **Later**: durable named consumers with offsets — which dovetails with the `consumer_offsets` table that already exists in the schema for NATS gap detection; a registered consumer with its own cursor is also exactly what makes a "projection" (G3's diff-between-states) first-class.

Relationship to G6: waits/continuations are the *in-runtime* special case (a suspended agent's wait is durable, single-consumption, managed); G7 is the *external* general case (ephemeral, broadcast, self-service). They share the matching semantics (same payload-field matcher as automation conditions) and should be specified together.

## Candidate sources to plug in (value order, after G1+G2)

1. **GitHub** (native webhook, `X-GitHub-Delivery` as key) — PR/push/release/issue → today it's polling in several internal flows.
2. **ClickUp** (native webhook) — card status changes → replaces pollers.
3. **LLM provider billing** (email/API → `billing.threshold` event) — act BEFORE credit hits zero, not after the prod error.
4. **Meeting minutes** (action items with deadlines → events with dates) — automatic follow-up before they expire.
5. **Drive/Calendar/Gmail** — via Workspace webhooks/push notifications.

Each source = 1 webhook source + N registered schemas + a key template. Zero new ingress code per source.

## Phasing

| Phase | Delivery | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | G1 (schema registry) + G2 (ingress idempotency) | — |
| 2 | G3 (causationId + correlationId propagation fix + `omni events trace`) | — (parallel to phase 1) |
| 3 | Plug in 2 real external sources (GitHub + ClickUp) as proof | 1, #928 |
| 4 | G4 (accepts/publishes manifest, compiled automations) | 1, 2 |
| 5 | G5 (transactional publication) | 4 |
| — | G7 first step (#966: custom events in stream + `events wait`) | independent — can ship with the pre-RFC fix wave |

## Open questions

1. Schema registry: plain JSON Schema, or Zod-first with generation? (the repo is already TS/Drizzle — Zod as source with JSON Schema as exported artifact seems the lowest-friction path)
2. Retroactive `idempotency_key`: backfill the existing 349k events or forward-only? (proposal: forward-only; the past has no reliably derivable key)
3. G4: does the manifest live in the agent's DB record or in a versioned file in the agent's repo? (deploy friction vs auditability via git)
4. Multitenancy: schemas and webhook sources per tenant or global with override? (the G2/G5 additive-tenancy pattern suggests: global + nullable `tenant_id`, same playbook)

items.title: Physical Tenant - Elasticsearch/OpenSearch Secondary Storage Support

labels.name: kind/epic
labels.description: Categorizes an issue as an umbrella issue (e.g. OKR) which references other, smaller issues

items.body:
[PDP epic](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/issues/51949)

From [DL tasks breakdown](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hLdPXbKNZvijRxwFn-N1QUW8pAMXX4vZtrrnpAr9TGM/edit?tab=t.jread4etvuh3)

**Goal:** Give each Physical Tenant an isolated ES/OS read path, write path, and schema lifecycle so that a noisy or unhealthy tenant cannot affect another tenant's querying, exporting, or background tasks, and so that index prefixes, clusters, and credentials can be configured independently per tenant.

**Scope:** per-tenant ES/OS client registry, schema initialization, exporter writer stack, search-client reader bundles, backup repositories, and observability tagging. No RDBMS path, no connector changes, no configuration surface (TASK-1.x delivered separately).

## Supported deployment modes

- **Separate cluster per tenant** — each tenant declares its own `connect.url` (and optionally its own credentials and TLS). From the data layer's perspective: N clients, one cluster each.
- **Shared cluster with `indexPrefix` per tenant** — clients may target the same cluster URL but are still instantiated per tenant; all `IndexDescriptor` / `IndexTemplateDescriptor` instances are built with the tenant's prefix.

Mixing RDBMS and ES/OS across tenants in the same cluster is not supported.

## Architecture

**Client registry (`SearchClients`)** — replaces the current singleton `ElasticsearchClient` / `OpenSearchClient` beans. One client per tenant is built at startup from that tenant's `ConnectConfiguration` via the existing `ElasticsearchConnector` / `OpensearchConnector`, held in a `Map<String, ElasticsearchClient>`, and closed on shutdown.

**Schema initialization (`SearchEngineSchemaInitializer`)** — refactored to iterate the per-tenant config map and run one `SchemaManager` per tenant. A `DescriptorFactory` produces a fresh set of `IndexDescriptor` / `IndexTemplateDescriptor` instances per tenant prefix. Readiness is tracked in a `Map<String, SchemaReadiness>` and exposed via `isSchemaReadyForUse(physicalTenant)`.

**Writer path (`CamundaExporter`)** — `context.getPhysicalTenant()` (TASK-2.2) identifies the tenant; `ClientAdapter.of()` is called with the tenant-scoped `ConnectConfiguration` and descriptor set. `BackgroundTaskManagerFactory` is threaded with the tenant so that archiver, incident-updater, history-deletion, and audit-log repositories all target the correct tenant's async client. Retention settings (`history.*`) are resolved per tenant.

**Reader path (`CamundaSearchClients`)** — `SearchClientConfiguration` builds a `SearchClientReaders` record per ES/OS tenant wired against the tenant's client and descriptor set. `CamundaSearchClients.forPhysicalTenant(name)` (TASK-2.1) dispatches to the correct bundle; reader implementations remain tenant-unaware.

**Backup (`BackupRepository`)** — singleton backup-repository bean replaced by a `Map<String, BackupRepository>`. Each entry uses the tenant's client and a tenant-scoped `WebappsSnapshotNameProvider` that prefixes snapshot names with the physical-tenant id.

**Observability** — every meter registered at per-tenant construction sites carries a `physical_tenant` tag via `MeterRegistry.config().commonTags(...)`.

## Parent

#1 — Spec: AI agent action layer for Feishu Docs (v1)

## What to build

The Feishu connector's connection layer: user OAuth (authorization code grant) against Feishu Open Platform, per-tenant Feishu app credentials from T3, encrypted token storage (user_access_token + refresh_token), and transparent automatic refresh before expiry with refresh locking. Establishes Seam B: a mock Feishu HTTP server (auth endpoints + token refresh) that the connector tests run against, so no real Feishu credentials are needed in CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] OAuth flow: CLI/admin starts the flow, user authorizes in Feishu, callback exchanges the code for tokens, a connection record is created
- [ ] Tokens are encrypted at rest (per-tenant key) and never logged
- [ ] Access token refresh happens automatically before expiry (mock server advances time); refresh is single-flight (no concurrent refreshes)
- [ ] Refresh failure (e.g. revoked refresh token) surfaces a structured `auth_expired` error and marks the connection needing re-auth
- [ ] Seam B infrastructure: mock Feishu HTTP server is reusable for the T7-T9 action tests
- [ ] `totemctl` can list connections and their auth state per tenant

## Blocked by

- #3 (T2: Postgres schema + migrations + docker compose)
- #4 (T3: Tenants + API keys + admin API + totemctl CLI)

items.body:
## Functional deliverable — minimum safe Capsule handoff (G2–G3)

**Goal:** Make the existing Capsule Release wizard's already approved/accepted Tenant handoff **actually work**. Stop building standalone proof frameworks.

### Deliver in this issue
- Connect the existing current preflight/approved plan and explicit Platform Admin successor acceptance to ONE guarded runtime handoff path. Use existing components rather than another architecture layer.
- At the moment of operation, verify current Capsule/Namespace/resource UID, RV, ownership/consent and sufficient provider authority; keep v1beta2 Capsule CR/spec, quota/limit policy, workloads, provider-owned objects and foreign RBAC unchanged.
- Perform server `dryRun=All` for the exact **KAORI metadata-only** candidates, then a separately authorized conditional PATCH and complete authoritative read-back, with a durable START attempt recorded before any mutation.
- Report **success / still pending / partial or unknown**. A partial/unknown result blocks Released, supplies a focused manual recovery action and is never auto-retried.

### Exit criteria
**Function complete** only when real path is wired and authorized regression/UAT proves one successful exact-scope handoff plus rejection of stale UID/RV, unsafe ownership/policy change and partial outcome. Source-only hash correlation or a merged PR is **not** PASS.

### Explicitly defer to separate review/audit backlog
New audit-envelope formats, duplicate provenance frameworks, speculative IdP/Vault resolver implementations, additional nonessential tables and exhaustive edge-case matrices **unless a specific test demonstrates they are required to keep this path safe**. Existing relevant contracts/fixtures should be reused or simplified.

**Next:** #1230 finalizer → #1231 Re-Adopt/UAT. #1229 remains OPEN. **HOLD:** tests/CI/CD/DevContainer QA, migration/SQL operational writes, Kubernetes/Vault/IdP/live provider operations, Release, deployment or staging/main promotion require separate operator approval; only source PRs to `kaori/review/staging-uat` are currently allowed. Existing START/proof writers remain disabled until that authorization.

items.title: Domain model for an open-source conformation dog-show platform
items.body:
## Destination — ✅ REACHED

A **domain-model-first technical spec** for an open-source **conformation dog-show** platform. Delivered on `main`: a ubiquitous language (`CONTEXT.md`), a bounded-context map (`CONTEXT-MAP.md`), the core domain invariants (`docs/domain-invariants.md`), and architecture ADRs (`docs/adr/`), plus the open-source license + anti-copy decision. Ready to hand off to a build phase.

The core domain is **kennel-club-agnostic**: kennel-club rules plug in as a policy/ruleset concept rather than being hard-coded, validated first against the pilot's **national FCI member club** ruleset. The model covers the **full online-entry + payment loop** (exhibitors register, enter dogs, pay entry fees). DDD + clean architecture, framework-agnostic ("don't marry the framework").

## Notes

- **Domain:** conformation (breed) dog shows first; other disciplines (obedience, agility, working trials, rally) are out of scope but the model should not preclude them.
- **Jurisdiction:** multi-jurisdiction core with pluggable rulesets; first concrete ruleset = **Belgium — Société Royale Saint-Hubert (SRSH) / Koninklijke Maatschappij Sint-Hubertus (KMSH)**, the Belgian FCI member club. (Belgium is bilingual FR/NL, so terminology must be captured in both languages.)
- **Reach:** full online-entry + payment loop is in scope; the *choice* of payment provider is out of scope.
- **Anti-copy stance:** model from real kennel-club regulations and the real-world domain, **never** from competitors' product text/screens/data. Licence is AGPL-3.0; contributors sign off via DCO (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).
- **Standing preferences:** DDD, clean architecture, clean code; keep the domain core free of framework/infrastructure concerns.
- **Skills every session should consult:** `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling` (default), `/research` (AFK research tickets), `/prototype` (when fidelity is needed).
- **Plan, don't do:** this map produces decisions/spec, not a build. Reaching the edge (the pull to just code it) is the hand-off signal.
- **Artifacts:** glossary in `CONTEXT.md`; context map in `CONTEXT-MAP.md`; invariants in `docs/domain-invariants.md`; ADRs in `docs/adr/`; licence in `LICENSE` + `CONTRIBUTING.md`; research findings on `research/*` branches under `docs/research/`.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket: enough to judge relevance, then zoom the link for the detail the ticket holds -->

- [Research Belgium (SRSH/KMSH) conformation show regulations](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/issues/2) — Belgian shows run under the **FCI Show Regulations** with a thin national layer (national CAC + Belgian titles); classes/grading/CACIB are FCI-fixed, titling is SRSH-defined. Findings: branch `research/belgium-ruleset`.
- [Research FCI international conformation show rules](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/issues/3) — FCI governs **only** the international CACIB layer; nationals own CAC/titles/extra classes. Yields the **10 axes of variation** for the ruleset abstraction. Findings: branch `research/fci-ruleset`.
- [Feature inventory of competitor platforms](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/issues/4) — incumbents are **print-led service bureaux** with bespoke pricing; small-club cost pain = bundled fees that don't scale down. Differentiators: self-serve, digital-first, transparent pass-through payments, portable data, live updates. Findings: branch `research/competitor-inventory`.
- [Establish the core ubiquitous language / glossary](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/issues/6) — core glossary in [CONTEXT.md](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/blob/main/CONTEXT.md): `Show` = single day (+ `Show Cluster`); `Entry` = one Dog/one Class (+ `Collective Competition`/`Team`); `Class`, breed taxonomy, `Grade`, `Award` ruleset-owned; four-way `Grade`/`Placement`/`Award`/`Title` split; three-way `Owner`/`Handler`/`Exhibitor` split.
- [Decide how kennel-club rulesets plug into the core](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/issues/7) — **data-first hybrid**: declarative data + **2** domain policy ports (`ClassEligibilityPolicy`/`AwardPolicy`; titles are owner-asserted, not computed); rulesets compose into a versioned `Effective Ruleset` snapshot (Show Type selects layers); concrete rulesets are pure domain modules. See [ADR-0001](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-kennel-club-rulesets-as-data-first-policies.md).
- [Decide the bounded-context map and context relationships](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/issues/8) — **9 contexts** (Core: Rulesets, Entries & Registration, Judging & Results; Supporting: Show Organisation, Catalogue & Publishing, Platform Administration; Generic/ACL: Payments, Identity & Access; Fog: Membership). Titles are owner-asserted data on the Dog, not a context. Event-driven + reference-by-ID; Rulesets = Published Language. See [CONTEXT-MAP.md](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/blob/main/CONTEXT-MAP.md) and [ADR-0002](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-bounded-contexts-and-event-driven-integration.md).
- [Document the core domain invariants](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/issues/9) — per-context invariants in [docs/domain-invariants.md](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/blob/main/docs/domain-invariants.md): Entry `Confirmed` = paid (only confirmed entries catalogued/judged); no late entries; placement needs min Grade; one CACIB per breed/sex/variety per Show (judge-validated); catalogue after entries close under ruleset timing; **titles owner-asserted, not computed**; conflict-of-interest & cross-show CACIB advisory.
- [Decide the open-source license and anti-copy / clean-room policy](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/issues/5) — **AGPL-3.0** ([LICENSE](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/blob/main/LICENSE)) for network-copyleft protection; **clean-room anti-copy policy + DCO** in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md); rationale in [ADR-0003](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-agpl-license-and-anti-copy-policy.md).


- [Decide the tech stack (language, repo topology, event backbone, persistence)](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/issues/10) — **TypeScript/Node** modular monolith, **API-first (Model A) + thin WordPress connector** (pure adapter); **monorepo** with the connector in its own repo; in-process events via a **transactional outbox** (NATS JetStream the deferred forward-target); **single PostgreSQL**, schema-per-context, `tenant_id` + **Row-Level Security**, **Drizzle** behind the ADR-0001 repository ports. Multi-tenant hosted instance primary; single-tenant deployment supported. See [ADR-0004](https://github.com/pslits/open-dog-show/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-tech-stack-typescript-modular-monolith-postgres.md) (PR #11).

## Not yet specified

<!-- in-scope fog; graduates into tickets as the frontier advances. The spec destination is reached; the items below are for the build phase or future efforts. -->

- **Per-context deep models** — internal aggregate/entity models of Entries & Registration, Judging & Results, Payments, etc. (build-phase work, past this spec's hand-off point).
- **Payment / entry-fee economics** — the model that serves the low-cost-for-small-clubs goal (who pays, fee structure, provider-agnostic boundary).
- **Differentiator add-ons** — live ring / running-order updates, digital catalogue & results publishing, judge app, membership management, analytics.
- **Junior Handling** — a handler-focused competition run at shows (judges the person, not the dog); out of the core conformation glossary, a candidate add-on.
- **Capture the primary competitor's site directly** — it is a client-side SPA the research fetcher couldn't read; revisit via the integrated browser / archive snapshot / public API. (optional AFK follow-up)
- **Belgian per-show operational data** — exact entry windows, closing dates and fee schedules live behind the KMSH portal (`portal.srsh.be`) and weren't publicly extractable; may need a `task` ticket (portal access) before the Payments/Entry economics can be pinned.

## Out of scope

<!-- ruled beyond the destination; never graduates unless the destination is redrawn -->

- UI / visual design.
- Writing production code.
- Non-conformation disciplines (obedience, agility, working trials, rally).
- Specific payment-provider integration.

items.title: [CANONICAL MEMORY][Owner App] ChatGPT operating contract, connectors, serial state & handoff
items.body:
# Owner App — Canonical ChatGPT Operating Memory

This issue is the durable handoff/source-of-truth for ChatGPT/AI work on **Relife Owner App**.

## Trigger phrase
If the user starts a new chat and says **“Owner App” / “Owner Apps”**, treat that as an instruction to:
1. Open this issue first.
2. Open Issue #134 for the active serial execution contract.
3. Check latest GitHub `main`, open PRs/issues, CI, and Render production state before proposing or performing implementation work.
4. Continue from the current serial item; do not restart planning from scratch.
5. Keep Relife Owner App (`avatarbd1/relife-owner-app`) separate from Relife Clinic OS/Telegram bot (`avatarbd1/relife-clinic-os`).

---

## 1. Project identity
- Product: **Relife Owner App / Web App**
- Repository: `avatarbd1/relife-owner-app`
- Stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind + Supabase integrations + Google Sheets operational data during current migration phase.
- Production hosting: Render service `relife-owner-app`
- Canonical brand: **Relife**

## 2. ChatGPT’s role
ChatGPT is not just a code generator. Its job is to act as the **technical director / verifier / release controller** for this repo.

ChatGPT must:
- keep the roadmap and serial order stable;
- convert the user’s intent into precise implementation prompts for Claude/other coding AI when appropriate;
- independently inspect the actual repo instead of trusting AI summaries;
- review PR/diff/tests/CI before accepting claims;
- verify Render deploy state after merges;
- separate `merge`, `deploy`, and `live smoke` as distinct states;
- preserve accounting/security/domain invariants;
- stop duplicate/parallel implementations;
- report exact evidence, not optimistic claims;
- teach the user one small developer concept tied to each real task/message.

## 3. Claude / coding-AI role
Claude may implement code, tests, commits, branches and PRs when instructed.

ChatGPT must independently verify Claude’s:
- branch/base;
- diff and changed files;
- canonical writer/rule reuse;
- tests and their meaningfulness;
- CI/build status;
- PR state;
- merge state;
- deployment state;
- live evidence.

**Claude saying `complete` is never sufficient evidence by itself.**

## 4. User authorization rules
- User saying `start / koro / shuru` authorizes implementation.
- It does **not** automatically authorize merge.
- Merge only after explicit user authorization such as `merge / marge`, unless a previously explicit conditional merge authorization applies to that exact PR.
- Never direct-write application code to `main`.
- Use fresh branch from latest `main`, Draft PR by default.
- Documentation-only GitHub issues/comments may be used without code PRs.

## 5. Connector/tool operating model
Use connected systems directly when relevant.

### GitHub connector
Use for:
- repo truth;
- branches/commits;
- issues;
- PRs/diffs/reviews;
- CI/workflow evidence;
- merge status.

### Render connector
Use for:
- service state;
- deploy status;
- deployed commit SHA;
- logs/errors/5xx;
- health/performance metrics;
- production verification.

Render workspace confirmed: **My Workspace** (`tea-d9akevo458ps73ft87n0`).
Production service: `relife-owner-app` (`srv-d9vhmn5bedkc73bqrbl0`).

### Supabase connector
Use for any Supabase-specific work: schema, database, Edge Functions, Auth, Storage, RLS, migrations, cron/queues, etc. Inspect before changing.

### Google Drive / Sheets connector
Use for connected Sheets/Docs/Drive when live operational sheet structure/data must be inspected or edited. Current migration rules still matter: do not silently replace the operational authority.

### Other connectors
Use any connected connector that materially improves verification or execution; do not substitute guesses for connected evidence.

## 6. Mandatory state check at the start of meaningful Owner App work
Before deciding “what next”:
1. Fetch latest GitHub `main` SHA.
2. Check open PRs.
3. Check relevant open/closed tracker issues.
4. Check CI for the active code state when applicable.
5. Check Render production deployed SHA/status after merges or before live smoke.
6. Compare GitHub vs Render by **tree/content**, not SHA alone when history-only commits exist.
7. Identify active serial item from Issue #134.

## 7. Merge vs deploy vs live verification
These are separate:
- **Merged** = code entered GitHub `main`.
- **Deployed** = Render production is running that app content.
- **Live verified** = real production flow/device/role scenario was executed successfully.

Never use one as proof of another.

## 8. Current Phase 0 serial tracker
Execution/reporting contract: **Issue #134**.

### P0-01 — Dental Billing Forward-Port ✅ MERGED
- PR #131
- Merge commit: `ba077f81654910191fcfbc70f3c0b78015212e9d`
- Dental treatment charge updates billed receivable / patient bill and due.
- Treatment save does not create payment/receipt/cash collection.
- Stable request-id protects retry idempotency.

### P0-02 — Cash Approval RBAC Hardening ✅ MERGED
- Issue #132
- PR #133
- Merge commit: `420e4faa2a5c39612f60298148b00112bd139410`
- signed session → current access context → explicit Owner → Owner PIN → canonical `decideCashMovement()`.
- audit actor = authenticated Owner `staffId`.

### P0-03 — Performance Metrics Verification ✅ COMPLETE
- Issue #135 closed/completed.
- Verification-only; no code change/PR required.
- 514/514 tests, 59 suites, 0 failures reported/verified as supporting repository evidence.
- Missing metrics remain `null`/unavailable, never fabricated `0`.
- Incomplete coverage remains provisional; no official score/rank when incomplete.
- XP, normalized score, Reward Credit, Performance Bonus remain distinct.
- Live verification intentionally deferred to P0-04.

### P0-04 — Live E2E + Device Smoke ⏭️ CURRENT
Deployment gate already checked:
- Render service live and not suspended.
- Render deployed commit: `420e4faa2a5c39612f60298148b00112bd139410`.
- GitHub main later became `fae3aa6de513a2757202797437a8108c6333cb07` because of two history-only commits.
- Compare `420e4f...` → `fae3aa...`: 2 commits ahead, **0 changed files**, therefore deployed application content is equivalent to current main tree.
- Current deploy window had no observed app error and no observed HTTP 500/502/503/504 in checked logs.
- Old Google Sheets HTTP 503 errors existed before this deploy and must not be misrepresented as current-deploy failures.

P0-04 must verify controlled production/device flows for:
- Dental billing + duplicate retry protection + payment boundary;
- Cash approval RBAC Owner/non-Owner/PIN paths;
- Performance null/provisional/official-rank separation;
- role/department isolation;
- at least one Android/mobile production smoke.

### P0-05 — Finance Reconciliation
Not started yet.
Must preserve exact terms:
- Billed Services
- Collections
- Outstanding
- Cash Handover
Cash Handover is custody movement, never revenue.
Physio/Dental remain isolated.

## 9. Frozen roadmap after Phase 0
### Phase 1A — Relife Physio completion + proving
Build:
- Shift Scheduling
- Leave Management
- SMS v1 outbound-only
- Correction Center append-only
- Analytics v1 with Billed Services / Collections / Outstanding / Cash Handover separated

Harden existing, do not rebuild:
- Settings
- Attendance reporting
- Bulk import/export
- Chamber chat
- PWA
- Staff management

### Phase 1B — SaaS conversion
- Next.js + Supabase retained
- tenant/clinic isolation with `clinic_id`/`tenant_id` + RLS
- no clinic-per-database/schema design
- staged provisioning/subscription/platform-admin work only after current system is proven

### Phase 2 — controlled rollout
Wave-based clinic rollout after proof/reconciliation/security gates.

## 10. Architecture invariants
- One user action → one canonical command/query → one domain rule → one repository/transaction → one audit event.
- No duplicate canonical writer.
- No parallel business-rule engine.
- Extend existing route/domain/service first.
- Critical writes fail closed.
- No silent fake/demo data in production.
- Financial/clinical corrections stay append-only/compensating, not destructive.

## 11. Source of Truth / migration rules
During Phase 0 + Phase 1A:
- Google Sheets remains operational authority for legacy/current operational domains unless an already-approved domain is explicitly cut over.
- PostgreSQL/Supabase is used for selected newer transactional/gamification paths and analytics/migration staging.
- Never silently change authority.
- Supabase cutover happens domain-by-domain with rollback/parity verification.

## 12. Finance invariants
- Reception → Home Treasury / Bank = internal cash transfer, not revenue or expense.
- No double count between cash movement and expense.
- Collections source remains canonical payment records (`06_Payments`) for current Sheets authority.
- Billed Services ≠ Collections.
- Outstanding ≠ Collection.
- Salary master ≠ salary paid/advance.
- Physio and Dental accounting stay isolated.

## 13. Booking vs operating invariant
Physio booking and live operation are separate.

Booking:
- 60 min ±5
- capacity/gender/duplicate-patient hard guards
- no fixed bed/machine reservation
- therapist overlap advisory
- machine demand planning only

Live operation:
- Arrived → Start Treatment → machine Start/Finish → Complete
- live resources tracked at execution time
- treatment cannot complete while machine is running

## 14. Role / department model
Roles include Owner, Manager, Receptionist, Therapist, Dentist, Dental Assistant/Auditor paths as implemented.
Departments: Physio / Dental / Owner-All scope.

Core rule:
- Dental staff must not see/edit Physio data without explicit approved scope.
- Physio staff must not see/edit Dental data without explicit approved scope.
- Owner can have All scope.
- Finance/clinical access remains permission-gated by canonical access context.

## 15. User-facing implementation reporting format
After every implementation/PR/merge, report in serial order:
1. Serial + task name
2. What changed
3. Logic/function flow and canonical reader/writer
4. How Owner/staff uses it in app
5. App impact
6. What remains untouched
7. Data/accounting/security invariants
8. Verification evidence: focused tests, full tests, lint, build, CI
9. Live verification YES/NO and exact remaining smoke
10. Branch/PR/head SHA/merge state/merge commit
11. Next serial item

## 16. Teaching / coaching rule
For **every meaningful user message/task**, provide one small developer-learning item tied to the actual work.
Do not dump a full curriculum.
Preferred learning chain:
**Problem → Flow → Function → Rule → Test**

Common concepts to teach gradually:
- Reader vs Writer vs Guard
- `null` vs `0`
- Source of Truth
- canonical Writer
- permission/RBAC
- failure path/fail closed
- idempotency/duplicate safety
- tests vs evidence
- PR/Diff
- CI/Build
- Merge vs Deploy vs Live Smoke
- local/sandbox work vs repo evidence

When Claude is about to do work:
- give the user a tiny relevant concept first;
- provide an exact Claude prompt;
- independently verify afterward;
- then ask one small question.

## 17. Evidence hierarchy
Strongest evidence order:
1. Live production/device evidence
2. Render deploy/log evidence
3. GitHub main/PR/diff/CI evidence
4. Meaningful automated tests
5. Source inspection
6. AI-written summary

Never reverse this hierarchy.

## 18. Known history note
There was an accidental `noop` file commit directly to main and immediate cleanup. Final tree returned byte-equivalent to the pre-accident app tree. Git history contains the two commits; do not claim history untouched. This is why production deploy SHA may differ from current main SHA while app content remains identical.

## 19. New-chat recovery procedure
When a new chat begins with “Owner App”:
- read this issue;
- read Issue #134;
- inspect current GitHub repo state;
- inspect Render if deployment/live status matters;
- identify active serial task;
- report current state before proposing next work;
- continue without making the user re-explain the project.

## 20. Do not do
- Do not confuse Owner App with Telegram bot/Clinic OS.
- Do not trust Claude completion claims without repo evidence.
- Do not direct-write app code to main.
- Do not merge without authorization.
- Do not create duplicate systems/writers.
- Do not call verification-only work “merged”.
- Do not call merged work “deployed” without Render evidence.
- Do not call deployed work “live verified” without executed smoke evidence.
- Do not fabricate metrics, finance rows, patient data, smoke results or coverage percentages.

This issue should remain open and be updated when the operating contract, serial state, connector topology, or canonical workflow changes.

items.title: per-physical-tenant ES/OS schema initialization

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
From [DL tasks breakdown](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hLdPXbKNZvijRxwFn-N1QUW8pAMXX4vZtrrnpAr9TGM/edit?tab=t.jread4etvuh3)

## Context

`SearchEngineSchemaInitializer` today creates a single `IndexDescriptors` instance (from a global `indexPrefix`), opens a single `ClientAdapter`, constructs one `SchemaManager`, and tracks readiness with a single `AtomicBoolean initialized`. `SchemaManagerContainer.isInitialized()` exposes that flag. With multiple physical tenants — each having its own `indexPrefix` and potentially its own ES/OS cluster — schema initialization must run independently per tenant, and downstream components (`CamundaExporter.open()`, backup priorities) must be able to query per-tenant readiness.

`IndexDescriptors` is already parameterized by `(indexPrefix, isElasticsearch)`, so it effectively acts as the per-tenant descriptor factory without further changes.

## What to implement

**Per-tenant schema initialization in `SearchEngineSchemaInitializer`**

- Replace the single `ClientAdapter` / `SchemaManager` / `AtomicBoolean` with a `Map<String, AtomicBoolean>` keyed by physical-tenant id. At startup, iterate the per-tenant `ConnectConfiguration` map from `PhysicalTenantResolver` and for each tenant:
  - construct a tenant-scoped `IndexDescriptors(tenantPrefix, isElasticsearch)` — this is the per-tenant descriptor set consumed by the exporter (TASK-4.3), backup (TASK-4.5), and readers (TASK-4.4)
  - open a `ClientAdapter` from the tenant's `ConnectConfiguration` (reusing the same connector path as today)
  - construct and run a `SchemaManager` wired to the tenant's client and descriptor set
  - set the tenant's `AtomicBoolean` to `true` on success
- Cap parallelism across tenant schema runs (bounded executor) to avoid hammering a shared cluster when operators pick the shared-cluster + prefix deployment mode.

**`SchemaManagerContainer` contract extension**

- Add `boolean isInitialized(String physicalTenantId)` to `SchemaManagerContainer`. Keep the existing no-arg `isInitialized()` as a default that returns `true` only when **all** tenants are initialized, preserving backward compatibility for callers that don't yet carry a tenant id.
- `CamundaExporter.open()` (TASK-4.3) calls `isInitialized(physicalTenantId)` before its first write; the exporter fails fast if the tenant's schema is not ready.

**Descriptor set registry**

- Expose a `IndexDescriptors forTenant(String physicalTenantId)` method on `SearchEngineSchemaInitializer` (or a sibling registry bean) so that TASK-4.3 (writer) and TASK-4.4 (reader) can retrieve the pre-built, tenant-scoped `IndexDescriptors` without re-instantiating descriptors.


Relates to #50782

items.title: Implement log ingestion and correlation with traces
items.body:
## Description
Accept log records with trace/span context and store them so users can jump from a span to its related logs.

## Why
Logs provide critical debugging detail for traces; correlation accelerates root-cause analysis.

## Expected behavior
- `POST /v1/ingest/logs` accepts structured log records with `trace_id`/`span_id`.
- Logs are stored in a dedicated ClickHouse log table; span events remain distinct.
- Log query API returns records related to selected spans; #53 owns trace-viewer integration.
- Bounded text search on log messages with index behavior qualified on the pinned ClickHouse release.

## Dependencies
- #1 - Select Python backend and web portal; freeze architecture before implementation (ADR-001)
- #8 - Implement trace and span normalization pipeline and writer to trace store
- #46 - Implement PII detection and masking at ingestion
- #64 - Qualify the frozen stack for compatibility, tenant isolation, capacity and recovery

## Technical considerations
- Same trace store can hold logs if schema supports message/severity.
- Cap log size and rate per tenant.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Log ingestion endpoint implemented.
- [ ] Logs are queryable by trace_id/span_id.
- [ ] API returns authorized related logs for #53 trace-detail integration.
- [ ] Severity filtering works.


## Technology contract — ADR-001 (2026-09-20)
Blocked by #1. The selected stack and boundaries there supersede conflicting earlier suggestions; preserve the functional scope above. No implementation or testing was performed by this issue update.

### Acceptance criteria — stack alignment
- [ ] Store independent OTLP log records in a dedicated ClickHouse log table, including logs without trace context; do not force every log into a span event.
- [ ] Expose OTLP/HTTP and gRPC logs plus the documented JSON convenience API through the authenticated path; preserve timestamps, severity, resource and optional W3C correlation IDs.
- [ ] Use bounded ClickHouse text/attribute search with qualified index behavior; no parallel search-engine stack. Enforce tenant/size/rate/redaction policy before durable buffering.

## Requirements audit - 2026-09-20
- [ ] Log query APIs own independent logs without trace context, severity/time/resource filters and byte/time/row limits. The trace viewer integrates through #53; no feature UI is required to implement the log receiver.

## Priority / Phase
P1 - Core. Phase 2 - Core Observability.

## Delivery and verification status
Planning reviewed against #66 on 2026-09-20. Implementation is not started by this audit; unchecked criteria require code/test or operational evidence. Follow #1 Python-only backend and shared React/TypeScript portal contracts. The Dependencies section is the complete prerequisite list; other issue links describe integration/ownership, not additional hidden blockers. Use input validation, bounded resource use, graceful unavailable/error states and tenant-isolation/failure-path tests relevant to this feature. No LLM is required for core observability. Production readiness is signed off in #81, never inferred from an issue edit.

## Core existing-environment integrations - 2026-09-20
User-requested required scope, not an enhancement. #82 owns shared contracts; #83 Kafka, #84 Logstash, #85 Solr, #86 onboarding. Implementation evidence remains unchecked.
- [ ] Shared log admission supports normalized external-source envelopes with stable event identity, mapping/provenance and logs with no trace IDs; connector implementations remain in #83-#85. #84 owns the Logstash HTTP compatibility endpoint and plugin-specific batch response semantics, not a second log store.
- [ ] Expose bounded source-connection provenance filters and redacted rejection reasons for the portal; platform-owned Kafka/DLQ/ClickHouse persistence always follows required privacy policy.

## Core enterprise AI usage, prompt supervision and finance audits - 2026-09-20
User-approved required core scope, not an enhancement. Delivery evidence remains unchecked; #101 gates release in #81.
- [ ] Support versioned native assistant OTLP log-event mappings through #90/#89 with safe redaction, source identities and event-time/order scope. Log receipt is not evidence that every original prompt or response exists; preserve truncation and missing-sequence evidence.

items.title: [PE-10] Issuance profile and verification profile entities
items.body:
Persist credential issuance profiles and verification profiles per tenant.
Profiles abstract credential format, schema, and protocol details behind a named+versioned identifier.
Aligns with OID4VCI "Credential Configuration" concept.

Entity: IssuanceProfile
- id UUID PK, tenant_id FK → tenants.id
- name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL — human-friendly identifier (e.g., "drivers-license")
- version VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL — semver-like (e.g., "1.0", "2.0")
- description TEXT — optional display description
- credential_definition_id UUID FK → credential_definitions.id (PE-03)
- format enum — copied from credential_definition for fast access (denormalized)
- connector_id UUID FK → connector_credentials.id — which connector handles this profile
- attribute_schema JSONB NOT NULL — declares attributes/claims the consumer must supply
  - Derived from credential_definition.schema_definition; may add display hints, defaults, optional flags
- defaults JSONB — pre-filled attribute values (e.g., issuer_name auto-injected)
- display JSONB — UI/metadata: { name, description, locale, background_color, logo_url }
- metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}' — extensible key-value store for issuer-specific data
  - OCA bundle resource links (e.g., { "oca_bundle_uri": "https://..." })
  - Trust framework tags (e.g., { "trust_framework": "PCTF-L3" })
  - Credential validity hints (e.g., { "credential_ttl_hint": "P365D" })
  - Revocation policy hints, custom branding, wallet rendering directives
  - Schema-less: validated only for well-formed JSON, not structure
- protocol_hint enum [didcomm, oid4vci, auto] DEFAULT 'auto' — preferred delivery protocol
  - 'auto': determined by adapter capabilities (Traction → didcomm, Credo → oid4vci)
  - Explicit hint overrides auto-detection when adapter supports multiple protocols
- status enum [draft, published, deprecated] DEFAULT 'draft'
  - draft: visible to tenant-admins only, not usable for issuance
  - published: usable for issuance, visible in public discovery
  - deprecated: existing credentials remain valid, no new issuance allowed
- Unique constraint: (tenant_id, name, version)
- Indexes: (tenant_id, status), (credential_definition_id)
- Repository: findByTenant, findPublished, findByNameAndVersion, updateStatus

Entity: VerificationProfile
- id UUID PK, tenant_id FK → tenants.id
- issuance_profile_id UUID FK → issuance_profiles.id — links to what was issued
- name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL — human-friendly (e.g., "age-verification")
- version VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
- description TEXT
- presentation_definition JSONB NOT NULL — pre-built proof request template (DIF PE format)
  - Defines requested attributes, predicates, constraints
  - Format-agnostic: works for AnonCreds proof requests AND OID4VP presentation definitions
- requested_attributes TEXT[] — subset of issuance profile's attribute_schema (quick reference)
- predicates JSONB — e.g., [{ attribute: "birth_date", condition: "<=", value: "2007-01-01" }]
- metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}' — extensible key-value store for verifier-specific data
  - Legal basis / purpose (e.g., { "legal_basis": "FIPPA s.26(c)", "purpose": "Age verification" })
  - Acceptable issuer DIDs or trust anchors
  - UX hints for wallet presentation consent screens
  - Maximum credential age requirements
  - Schema-less: validated only for well-formed JSON, not structure
- public BOOLEAN DEFAULT false — if true, discoverable via public endpoint (CA-14)
- protocol_hint enum [didcomm, oid4vp, auto] DEFAULT 'auto'
- status enum [draft, published, deprecated] DEFAULT 'draft'
- Unique constraint: (tenant_id, name, version)
- Indexes: (tenant_id, status), (issuance_profile_id), (tenant_id, public) WHERE public = true
- Repository: findByTenant, findPublicByTenant, findByNameAndVersion, updateStatus

TypeORM migrations included in this issue (two tables).

### Dependencies
- Blocked by #24
- Blocked by #26
- Blocked by #29

### Definition of Done
- [ ] Implementation complete and builds without errors
- [ ] Unit/integration tests pass
- [ ] PR reviewed and approved
- [ ] No regressions in existing functionality
- [ ] API endpoints documented (if applicable)

items.title: SchemaManager.close() can hang indefinitely when a schema mutation is still in flight

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as a bug

labels.name: severity/high
labels.description: Marks a bug as having a noticeable impact on the user with no known workaround

labels.name: discovered-by/load-tests
labels.description: Marks an issue as discovered during a load test

items.body:
### ### ### ### ### ### Description Two distinct defects in `SchemaManager` combined to permanently hang physical-tenant schema initialization on a 120-tenant cluster: one generates far more Elasticsearch cluster-state work than it needs to, and the other turns any resulting slowness into an unrecoverable hang. They are independent, neither subsumes the other, and both are in scope here. **1. `updateSchemaSettings()` blind-writes settings for every descriptor on every attempt.** It sits outside the `createSchema` block, so it runs unconditionally on every attempt of every tenant — including attempts where nothing is missing — and it fans out over *all* of `allIndexDescriptors` rather than only what needs changing, submitting one virtual thread per descriptor. Each task issues one or two **cluster-state** operations (`putSettings` for everything, `updateIndexTemplateSettings` for templates), which the Elasticsearch master processes single-threaded. `IndexDescriptors` carries ~41 descriptors, so the per-retry-round fan-out is roughly 41 × 120 ≈ **4,900 concurrent cluster-state requests against one master**, repeating every backoff interval whether or not anything needs to change. The writes are largely provably redundant: `updateSchemaSettings` runs *after* `initialiseIndices`, and both derive their values from the same `getIndexSettingsFromConfig(descriptor)`, so for any index created earlier in the same run the write re-applies the value the index was created with seconds earlier. "It's idempotent" is not a defence — Elasticsearch still queues a cluster-state update task on the master even when the resulting state is unchanged, so a no-op write is as expensive to queue as a real one. **2. `SchemaManager.close()` can block forever**, which converts slowness from (1) into a permanent hang. `joinOnFutures()` gives up after `INDEX_CREATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (60s) when a mutation hasn't been acknowledged, but it only abandons the future — it never stops the virtual thread running the request, and `CompletableFuture.cancel()` wouldn't do so anyway (the JDK never uses interrupts for that). `close()` then delegates to `ExecutorService.close()`, whose default shuts down and loops `awaitTermination(1, DAYS)` until every task — including the abandoned one — finishes on its own. `PerTenantSchemaInitialization` builds a fresh `SchemaManager` per attempt and closes the previous one before retrying, which is what puts `close()` on the retry hot path. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Retry as PerTenantSchemaInitialization (retry loop) participant SM as SchemaManager (attempt N) participant ES as Elasticsearch Retry->>SM: new SchemaManager() + startupOnce() SM->>ES: ~41 cluster-state writes (updateSchemaSettings, on virtual threads) Note over SM,ES: x120 tenants -> master queue backs up Note over SM: joinOnFutures times out after 60s,
futures abandoned, NOT cancelled SM-->>Retry: throws (attempt failed) Retry->>SM: close() Note over SM: ExecutorService.close():
awaitTermination(1, DAYS) Note over SM: waits on the abandoned
virtual threads -- forever Note over Retry: tenant never recovers ``` Why both are needed: fixing (1) alone removes the *amplification* but not the trigger — a tenant's first startup still has to create ~41 indices and templates for real, so a cold 120-tenant bootstrap still produces a genuine master burst, which is exactly the incident scenario. Fixing (2) alone leaves the cluster generating thousands of redundant master tasks per retry round. Together, (1) removes the load and (2) bounds the blast radius of any stall that still occurs, from whatever cause. ### Evidence from the incident thread dump Full dump from `camunda-14`, 2026-09-18 (31k lines, 120 tenants). All 120 `schema-init-ptN` threads are `TIMED_WAITING (parking)`: **117 parked in `SchemaManager.close()`**, 3 still inside their attempt in `joinOnFutures` — and those 3 are in `updateSchemaSettings`, not template creation. ``` "schema-init-pt1" #2709 daemon cpu=287.18ms elapsed=659.79s java.lang.Thread.State: TIMED_WAITING (parking) at java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch.await at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPerTaskExecutor.awaitTermination at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPerTaskExecutor.close at io.camunda.search.schema.SchemaManager.close(SchemaManager.java:557) at io.camunda.application.commons.search.SearchEngineSchemaInitializer.initializeTenant(SearchEngineSchemaInitializer.java:150) at io.camunda.application.commons.pt.PerTenantSchemaInitialization.initializeTenant(PerTenantSchemaInitialization.java:244) "schema-init-pt25" #2875 daemon cpu=280.28ms elapsed=659.62s java.lang.Thread.State: TIMED_WAITING (parking) at io.camunda.search.schema.SchemaManager.joinOnFutures(SchemaManager.java:415) at io.camunda.search.schema.SchemaManager.updateSchemaSettings(SchemaManager.java:291) at io.camunda.search.schema.SchemaManager.initializeSchema(SchemaManager.java:197) at io.camunda.search.schema.SchemaManager.startupOnce(SchemaManager.java:138) ``` `elapsed=659.79s` against `cpu=287.18ms` — parked ~11 minutes, not spinning, with no automatic recovery. Note for future captures: the mutations themselves run on virtual threads, and a SIGQUIT/jstack-style dump does not list unmounted virtual threads, so the request side is invisible here (zero `RestClient`, `SyncResponseListener` or `requestConnection` frames anywhere in the dump). Use `jcmd Thread.dump_to_file -format=json ` to capture them. Relevant code: [`updateSchemaSettings()`](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/blob/6ffb42604a4f6177aaa93f13a8d7e55919b7070e/schema-manager/src/main/java/io/camunda/search/schema/SchemaManager.java#L347-L358), [`updateIndexSettings()`](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/blob/6ffb42604a4f6177aaa93f13a8d7e55919b7070e/schema-manager/src/main/java/io/camunda/search/schema/SchemaManager.java#L360-L371), [`SchemaManager.close()`](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/blob/6ffb42604a4f6177aaa93f13a8d7e55919b7070e/schema-manager/src/main/java/io/camunda/search/schema/SchemaManager.java#L644-L646) and [`joinOnFutures()`](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/blob/6ffb42604a4f6177aaa93f13a8d7e55919b7070e/schema-manager/src/main/java/io/camunda/search/schema/SchemaManager.java#L479-L485). ### Out of scope — to be handled in separate issues These surfaced while reviewing the fix. They are real, but none is load-bearing for the hang above, and two of them touch `search/search-client-connect`, a shared library used well beyond schema-manager, so they need their own blast-radius review. Details in the review comments on this issue. - **Unbounded `connectionRequestTimeout` in the ES connector.** Apache HttpClient 4.x defaults it to `-1` and `RestClientBuilder` never sets it, so a request waiting to lease a pool connection has no client-side bound. This matters because bounding `close()` reaps the *thread* but not the *request*: `RestClient`'s sync path is `Future.get()` on the async client, which is interruptible, but interrupting it does not cancel the underlying exchange. Needs its own property rather than being derived from `socketTimeout`, and the OpenSearch side is a consistency tightening rather than a gap (HttpClient 5.x already bounds it at 3 minutes). - **Bounding `SchemaManager`'s in-flight request count** to the client's connection pool. Useful only *together with* the item above — it mitigates lease-timeout failures that only exist once a lease timeout is set — and it relocates the queue rather than reducing work submitted to the master, so it is not a substitute for fixing (1). - **~1,792 Elasticsearch REST client I/O threads** at this tenant count (one reactor per tenant `ClientAdapter`, ~15 threads each). Unrelated to the hang, but a notable per-tenant fixed cost. Also worth dropping rather than tracking: cancelling timed-out futures in `joinOnFutures()`. `CompletableFuture.cancel()` cannot interrupt a task already running on the executor, and the futures are local and discarded immediately after the rethrow, so it changes no behaviour and misleads the reader into thinking cancellation works. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start a cluster with many physical tenants (the incident had 120) sharing one Elasticsearch cluster, so that concurrent per-tenant schema initialization saturates the master's single-threaded cluster-state update pipeline. 2. Observe `updateSchemaSettings()` submitting one request per descriptor per tenant per attempt, regardless of whether any setting needs changing. 3. Let `joinOnFutures()` time out at 60s with mutations still in flight. 4. Observe `SchemaManager.close()` block indefinitely instead of returning, leaving the tenant's schema-init thread parked with no recovery. For (2) in isolation, a Toxiproxy-injected latency in front of Elasticsearch reproduces the `close()` hang without needing a genuinely overloaded cluster. ### Current behavior Every retry round submits thousands of redundant cluster-state requests, and `close()` can hang for an unbounded amount of time. In production this showed up as 117 of 120 tenants' schema-init threads permanently parked in `SchemaManager.close() -> ThreadPerTaskExecutor.awaitTermination() -> CountDownLatch.await()`, with no automatic recovery. ### Expected behavior - `updateSchemaSettings()` should only write settings that actually need changing, and should not scale its request count with descriptor count on every attempt. - `close()` should always return within a bounded amount of time, regardless of whether the underlying search-engine call has completed. ### Workaround _No response_ ### Environment SM ### Version - Component Version: 8.11.0-SNAPSHOT (main); also present on 8.10 ### Rootcause **(1)** `updateSchemaSettings()` is an unconditional blind write: it never reads the current value before writing, so its cost scales with `descriptors × tenants × attempts` and is entirely independent of whether anything needs to change. Because it runs after `initialiseIndices` and both read the same `getIndexSettingsFromConfig(descriptor)`, most of those writes re-apply a value that was set moments earlier. **(2)** `joinOnFutures()` treats its own timeout as fire-and-forget, and `close()` relies on `ExecutorService.close()`'s effectively unbounded wait rather than bounding it itself. Neither cancelling nor abandoning the future is enough: a cancelled `CompletableFuture` doesn't stop the virtual thread already running underneath it, so `close()` itself has to be the one that stops waiting. This is far more likely to trigger with many physical tenants sharing one Elasticsearch cluster than in a single-tenant deployment: every tenant's initialization competes for the same single-threaded cluster-state pipeline, and the retry loop re-submits the whole fan-out each round without cancelling the previous attempt's in-flight requests. The live incident showed up to 26x duplicate requests queued for the same target on the master at once. ### Solution ideas **For (1) — `updateSchemaSettings()`:** turn it from a blind write into a bulk read, diff, and batched write. 1. **Read-diff-write.** One bulk read per tenant, then write only what actually drifted; in steady state this goes from ~41 writes to zero. The precedent already exists in `SearchEngineClient`: `getNumberOfShards(Collection)` is a bulk read that exists precisely to tell whether a configured value is in effect, consumed by `checkShardConfiguration()` to compare-and-report. Mirror it with `getNumberOfReplicas(Collection)`, including its "names that do not exist are absent from the result" convention — a missing index needs no write, since `initialiseIndices` creates it with the right settings. The read is cheap in the way that matters: `GET */_settings` with `name=index.number_of_replicas` is served from any node's local cluster state and never touches the master. 2. **Batch the remaining writes.** Group descriptors by target replica count and issue one `PUT /a,b,c/_settings` per distinct value — normally a single group, so one master task instead of N. `putSettings` took a `List` on 8.10 and was narrowed to a single descriptor on main, so this is re-widening an interface that already had the right shape. 3. **Same treatment for `updateIndexTemplateSettings`**, which is also a cluster-state operation, over the smaller template-only set. Explicitly *not* recommended: gating `updateSchemaSettings` on schema version or on `createSchema`. It sits outside that block deliberately so that a config change to replica count takes effect without a version bump; gating would silently drop legitimate config changes, trading a performance bug for a correctness one. **For (2) — `close()`:** bound its own wait explicitly — `shutdown()`, a short timed `awaitTermination()`, then `shutdownNow()` — instead of relying on `ExecutorService.close()`'s effectively unbounded default. The grace period should be its own short constant rather than a reuse of `INDEX_CREATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`: the only task legitimately still running at close on a successful startup is `startSchemaCleanup()`'s fire-and-forget cleanup, and borrowing the 60s index-creation budget would add a second full minute to every failed attempt before its retry backoff even starts. The escalation to `shutdownNow()` is best-effort and the fix must not depend on it landing — the contract is that `close()` returns whether or not the task can actually be stopped. ### Update (2026-09-21): the same defect also hits ILM/ISM policy creation `createLifecyclePolicies()` has the identical shape to defect (1) above: `SchemaManager.putIndexLifeCyclePolicy()` PUTs the retention / usage-metrics ILM (Elasticsearch) or ISM (OpenSearch) policy unconditionally on every schema-init attempt, regardless of whether the policy already matches configuration. Every physical tenant's own `SchemaManager` writes the *same* policy name and content, so a large tenant fleet turns concurrent startups into a pile of redundant master tasks — the exact `process_cluster_event_timeout_exception` failure mode already described above for index settings, now observed on the ILM policy PUT itself: ``` org.elasticsearch.client.ResponseException: method [PUT], host [http://elasticsearch-es-http:9200], URI [/_ilm/policy/pt26-camunda-retention-policy], status line [HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable] {"error":{"root_cause":[{"type":"process_cluster_event_timeout_exception","reason":"failed to process cluster event (put-lifecycle-pt26-camunda-retention-policy) within 30s"}],"type":"process_cluster_event_timeout_exception","reason":"failed to process cluster event (put-lifecycle-pt26-camunda-retention-policy) within 30s"},"status":503} at io.camunda.search.schema.elasticsearch.ElasticsearchEngineClient.putIndexLifeCyclePolicy(ElasticsearchEngineClient.java:292) at io.camunda.search.schema.SchemaManager.createLifecyclePolicies(SchemaManager.java:263) at io.camunda.search.schema.SchemaManager.initializeSchema(SchemaManager.java:199) ``` Fix follows the same read-diff-write shape as (1), applied to both engines: - **Elasticsearch**: `GET _ilm/policy/{name}` before the `PUT`; skip the write when `phases.delete.min_age` already matches configuration. - **OpenSearch**: reuse the read the code already does before every PUT (`getCurrentISMPolicyState`, previously only used for the `if_seq_no`/`if_primary_term` optimistic-concurrency headers) and skip the write when `min_index_age` already matches. While in there, also consolidated `updateSchemaSettings()`'s replica-count read from one `getNumberOfReplicas` call **per descriptor** down to a single call scoped to `{prefix}-camunda-*,{prefix}-operate-*,{prefix}-tasklist-*` (the three component prefixes every real descriptor uses) — same drift detection, far fewer round trips against the cluster on a large tenant fleet.

items.title: fix(snowflake): health check runs `show schemas` on every tick
items.body:
## Summary

The Snowflake connector's `do_health_check_connector/1` runs `show schemas` via ODBC on every health-check tick. This returns one row per schema in the current database — unbounded in row count, and worse, it forces the Snowflake warehouse to spin up just to answer metadata.

## Where

`apps/emqx_bridge_snowflake/src/emqx_bridge_snowflake_connector.erl:365-373`.

```erlang
do_health_check_connector(ConnectionPid) ->
    case odbc:sql_query(ConnectionPid, "show schemas") of
        {selected, _, _} -> ok;
        ...
```

## Impact

* Snowflake's auto-suspend / auto-resume billing model: every health-check tick on an idle deployment can keep the warehouse from suspending. Customers with auto-suspend timers comparable to the EMQX health-check interval will see continuous warehouse usage charges.
* Multi-tenant / per-tenant-schema accounts may return thousands of rows on each tick.
* `show schemas` requires warehouse compute even though it returns only metadata.

## Suggested fix

Replace with `SELECT 1` (the canonical liveness probe) or `SELECT CURRENT_VERSION()`. Both bypass result-set assembly and complete instantly without warehouse spin-up.

```erlang
- case odbc:sql_query(ConnectionPid, "show schemas") of
+ case odbc:sql_query(ConnectionPid, "SELECT 1") of
-     {selected, _, _} -> ok;
+     {selected, _, [{1}]} -> ok;
```

Snowflake docs reference: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/warehouses-considerations.

## Related

Part of the health-check audit following d94cbde4. Same class of bug — open-ended scan/list on every tick.

## U10A2 dependency closure for #1186 / U10A1 (#1227)

**Status: BLOCKED / DESIGN_REQUIRED; no code migration or target DB modification authorized.** Verified source base `615700e74c25b0f87b33318402e24eeb5a44a032`. U10A1 main-line forward SQL was implemented and locally tested at unpushed worktree commit `c630a4975ee16ee3c9515fe09af3563676073886`, but MUST NOT be marked DONE/merged until this dependency chain is proven.

### Concrete missing dependency

- `supabase/customer-baseline/migrations/0001_shoperation_v1_schema.sql` contains legacy `office_*_store_all` browser RLS based on `can_manage_support(instance_id)`, not modern participant-aware privacy. Searching the canonical ordered customer baseline `0001–0046` found no `public.can_read_office_thread_v1`, `private.current_user_can_read_office_thread_v1`, `private.office_effective_feature_enabled_v1` or `office_thread_participants` migration definitions.

Confirm actual complete ordered dependency DAG and filename/identity; never guess or cherry-pick a subset.
- Live waterk-staging catalog previously reported older RLS and missing helpers/migration versions. Authenticated/anon lacked direct SELECT table grants at last check, so **do not claim a current browser data leak**, but actual staging tenant/RPC proof is BLOCK.
- U10A1 migration explicitly fails preflight on missing privacy/participant helpers instead of granting/assuming them. A naive isolated `0047` copy of the hardening SQL would fail Fresh Install or create a false compatibility claim.

### Required work

1. Source-backed reconciliation: trace modern main Office foundation-to-feature SQL DAG and compare to canonical Fresh Install `0001–0046`; identify whether the target is expected to include Office DB capabilities at launch and how to import the ordered schema/GRANT/RPC features. Respect non-destructive, forward-only lineage; no historical migration rewrite.
