items.title: checks.freshness overrides parses but nothing consumes it (N2 of #1620)

labels.name: decided
labels.description: An owner decision is recorded on the issue; do not re-litigate the approach

items.body:
#1435 named two `rocky.toml` surfaces that parse and validate while nothing reads them. A systematic sweep of all 24 top-level `RockyConfig` fields and their sub-fields found **three more**. All three are sub-fields, not whole sections, and each is documented as if it worked.

Verified on `main` at `c32f28f9`, with a second independent pass.

## N1 — `[cache.schemas] replicate` (strongest)

**Claim in the docs:** `docs/src/content/docs/reference/configuration.md:923` and `:930` — "Replicate the schema cache via `[state]` sync", `replicate = true # opt in to share cache via the remote state backend`. Also in `schemas/rocky_project.schema.json:3631`.

**What happens:** nothing. Setting it to `true` changes neither sync leg.

- **Upload.** `engine/crates/rocky-core/src/state_sync.rs:2341` — `upload_state()` hard-codes `crate::state::LOCAL_ONLY_TABLE_NAMES`, which contains `"schema_cache"` (`engine/crates/rocky-core/src/state.rs:288`). The override `upload_state_with_excluded_tables` (`state_sync.rs:2391`) exists and its own doc at `:2338` says *"Use `upload_state_with_excluded_tables` to override the default when `[cache.schemas] replicate = true` is configured"* — and it has **no caller outside `state_sync.rs`** (one internal call and one test).
- **Download.** `engine/crates/rocky-cli/src/api.rs:1250` documents that `download_state` unconditionally preserves local-only tables.

```
$ grep -rn --include='*.rs' "\.replicate\b" engine/crates engine/rocky
# every hit is a #[cfg(test)] assertion inside config.rs, or a struct
# literal WRITING `replicate: false` (source_schemas.rs:147,
# schema_cache_writer.rs:189). Zero production reads.
```

The implementation hook was built and never wired: the same shape as #1435's grace-period half.

## N2 — `[pipeline.<name>.checks.freshness] overrides`

**Claim in the docs:** `configuration.md:386` shows `{ threshold_seconds = N, overrides = { ... } }` with no caveat. In `schemas/rocky_project.schema.json:1267`.

**What happens:** the check reads only the scalar. `engine/crates/rocky-cli/src/commands/run.rs:5057`:

```rust
let mut check = checks::check_freshness(lag, freshness_cfg.threshold_seconds);
check.severity = freshness_cfg.severity;
```

`check_freshness` (`engine/crates/rocky-core/src/checks.rs:440`) takes one threshold; there is no per-schema lookup on the path. The engine admits the gap internally at `engine/crates/rocky-cli/src/output.rs:171` — *"Per-schema `overrides` … are intentionally not exposed yet"* — but the user-facing page does not carry that caveat. The field is `deny_unknown_fields`-parsed and folded into the config-snapshot hash, so it looks live.

## N3 — `[schedule] poll_interval_seconds`

**Claim in the docs:** `configuration.md:573` — `poll_interval_seconds = 15 # resident-loop cadence; not consumed by the one-shot rocky tick`. That caveat names the wrong exemption: the resident loop does not consume it either.

**What happens:** nothing reads `config.schedule.poll_interval_seconds`. The only production read of `config.schedule.*` anywhere is `timezone` (`engine/crates/rocky-core/src/schedule/reconcile.rs:790`, `schedule_status.rs:91`, `validate.rs:837`).

The cadence comes from the CLI flag only — `engine/crates/rocky-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:155`:

```rust
poll_interval: poll_interval_seconds        // the --poll-interval-seconds arg
    .map(std::time::Duration::from_secs)
    .unwrap_or(crate::commands::scheduler::DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL),
```

The "reserved for a later phase" defence does not hold: `rocky serve --scheduler` shipped, and its loop re-reads `load_rocky_config(config_path)` on every tick (`scheduler/mod.rs:258`) while the interval stays frozen at spawn (`mod.rs:152`).

**Caveat, stated plainly:** the default (15) equals `DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL`, so the key is inert only for a user who *changes* it. That is still the whole point of setting it.

## Checked and deliberately not reported

- `PolicyRule::conditions` (`config.rs:3110`) is unread but **self-documented** as *"Parsed and ignored — captured as opaque JSON so a config authored against a later version still loads."* A deliberate forward-compatibility hatch, not this defect.
- `[pipeline.*.target.governance] auto_create_schemas` was reported under #1435 and **withdrawn** after a baseline delta showed it works. Not re-reported.

## What to do

Each needs the same call #1435 made, per field: wire it, or refuse it loudly with a message naming the remedy. Silently accepting a key that does nothing is the defect, and a docs-only caveat is not a fix — a `deny_unknown_fields` parser that accepts a key is a promise.

N1 is the one to take first: it has a positive doc claim, a schema entry, a built-but-unreachable implementation hook, and both sync legs hard-coded against it.

Refs #1435

items.title: P0 dependency: migrate Zod 3 consumers to patched Zod 4 with regression proof

labels.name: dependencies
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file

items.body:
## Verified P0 dependency blocker (2026-10-30)
Latest npm bulk audit after patch upgrades reports only two HIGH advisory IDs: node-forge (1240912, pre-existing expiring risk approval) and **Zod 1243066** (unwaived). All seven newly observed body-parser/multer/undici advisories were eliminated by patch upgrades in draft PR #1035.

Repository lock contains BOTH `zod@4.6.7` (patched) and **`zod@3.25.76`**, referenced from many first-party apps, platform packages, and transitive packages. GitHub advisory GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 lists versions <4.6.6 as affected. A blanket root override to Zod 4 would cross a major API boundary with a large blast radius and would be unsafe without source migration.

## Required permanent correction
1. Inventory all Zod3 first-party consumers and external peer requirements, group by common v3 API usages.
2. Upgrade/migrate first-party consumers in bounded family batches (parse semantics, `ZodEffects`, schema introspection, enum, error handling and async refinements).
3. Replace v3 transitive dependencies via supported upgrades where upstream allows, preserving compatibility.
4. Add ingress resource caps and negative tests for nested/oversized array validation, multi-tenant request boundaries, and API rate/budget constraints.
5. Reconcile generated pnpm v9 lock, frozen-install, affected TS/typecheck, unit/contract tests and runtime requests.
6. Run current high-severity audit and Trivy; close only when 1243066 is genuinely absent OR a separate explicitly approved and expiring risk decision meets policy. Do not add an unapproved waiver or claim remediation from controls that merely hide the vulnerable dependency.

## Closure proof
Current lock no longer contains vulnerable Zod3 package and consumers remain correct under authentic runtime tests; no false green by skipping audit.

**Status: HOLD; this is not a human-approved waiver or production authorization.**

items.title: [Spike] Close OD-4 — security & domain invariants spec

labels.name: type:spike
labels.description: A timeboxed investigation whose deliverable is an ADR

milestone.title: M0 Foundations
milestone.description: Iteration 0: close the stack/boundary/security/verify spikes and stand up the load-bearing cross-cuttings (tenancy, permissions, identity, connectors, ingestion, upload/storage, audit) for the grounded-chat MVP. Gated on OD-2.

items.body:
## Spike — closes OD-4 (security & domain invariants)

**Goal:** derive the concrete security/domain invariants from the decided scope (spec 0003) and the landed stack (ADR-0003/0004), and turn each into a negative-test category (AGENTS.md §9). Deliverable is a **spec** in `docs/specs/`.

> **This spike is the single gate for the security half of M0.** It blocks CC-2 tenancy (#17), CC-1 permissions (#18), CC-3 identity (#19), CC-8 audit (#23), and the connector framework CC-4 (#20). It needs **human/sponsor input** (these are product-security decisions, like OD-1 was) — recommend deciding it in-session next.

### Decisions OD-4 must make (don't default — ask)
- **Tenancy isolation model:** row-level (`tenant_id` + enforced predicate) vs schema/db-per-tenant; the cross-tenant negative-test set.
- **Permission/ACL model:** how source ACLs are represented and mirrored; deny-by-default semantics; what "permitted to see" means for retrieval + citations.
- **Identity/authn:** session/token model; **and the IdP technology** ADR-0003 deferred to CC-3 (OSS IdP e.g. Keycloak/Authentik vs app-managed OIDC).
- **Audit taxonomy:** which events, required fields, retention, tamper-evidence.
- **Read-before-write:** the approval gate + risk tiers for any future consequential action.

### Seed invariants (from the four mission filters — refine, don't treat as final)
- **Permissioned:** a user must never receive a passage/citation their source ACLs deny → *unauthorized-retrieval → denied*.
- **Tenancy:** a query in tenant A must never return tenant B's content → *cross-tenant access → denied*.
- **Citation integrity:** no asserted fact without a resolvable citation → *uncited-claim → blocked/flagged*.
- **Read-before-write:** no consequential action without explicit approval → *unapproved-action → forbidden*.
- **Auditability:** every retrieval/answer emits an audit event → *missing-audit-event → fail*.

### Deliverable (DoD)
- [ ] Spec in `docs/specs/` enumerating the invariants + the negative-test category for each; the IdP-tech choice recorded (here or a linked ADR).
- [ ] Feeds `AGENTS.md` §9 negative-test set (update in the same change).
- [ ] Strikes OD-4 in `docs/specs/0001-open-decisions.md`.

### Dependencies
- blocked-by: none (OD-1 closed; stack landed). **Ready now** — needs a human decision session.
- blocks: #17, #18, #19, #20, #23.

items.title: Roadmap 2: from first slices to competitor-depth process and task intelligence
items.body:
## Why a second roadmap
Every item in #264 now has a first implementation in `main`. That is not parity with Mimica, UiPath (Task Mining, Process Mining, Task Capture, Automation Hub, Communications Mining), Celonis, Soroco, Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining, SAP Signavio or Skan.ai. #264's own gate ("test competitor-style UX against realistic consenting datasets before calling it parity") has not been met, and most items are breadth, not depth.

This issue tracks the depth needed for an all-encompassing open-source OWG. It keeps OWG's foundations: local-first capture, consent, evidence/policy/permission separation, agent handoff over MCP, Discovery Mode, and no hidden upload or productivity scoring. It is capability parity, not copying proprietary code, branding or UI.

## Current state vs competitors (honest baseline)
| Area | Competitors | OWG in `main` |
|---|---|---|
| Source connectors | Continuous extraction from SAP, Oracle, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Workday… | CSV (now with chosen extra columns kept as attributes, #366); selected Jira/GitHub/Zendesk/Stripe cases; append newer exports to saved logs (#360) |
| Scale | Billions of events, columnar engines | Local SQLite; DuckDB event-log workspace with 10M-event acceptance (#327) |
| Object-centric mining | Linked order/invoice/delivery objects | OCEL 2.0 JSON and XML import/export with per-object-type case notions and literal identities (#327, #331, #338); object-centric maps (#336, #345) |
| Analytics | Root cause, KPIs, benchmarks, simulation, token-replay conformance | Variants, case evidence, KPIs with cohort filters/exports, benchmarks, what-if simulation, root-cause associations, path and saved-graph alignment conformance with fitness/precision, classic token replay (#328, #330, #332, #333, #335, #339, #350) |
| Performance and change | Disco/ProM processing vs waiting, dotted chart, Apromore compare and drift | Processing vs waiting time from lifecycle or end-time data (#366), dotted chart (#367), side-by-side map comparison (#368), concept drift change points (#369) |
| Organizational mining | Handover-of-work and working-together networks, activity/resource views | Pseudonymous handovers, shared cases and activity × resource matrix (#352) |
| Signals and actions | Celonis Action Engine / UiPath process alerts on KPI thresholds | Saved KPI, case and compliance signal rules with evidence cases and new-since-last-check; signals never act (#355, #358, #362) |
| Ad-hoc analysis | Celonis PQL, custom analyses | Typed no-SQL analysis builder with saved analyses (#357) |
| Opportunity pipeline | UiPath Automation Hub idea pipeline and prioritization | Local reviewable pipeline with states, history, ease/impact assessment and quadrants; approval never authorizes execution (#361); scenario calculator and implementation alternatives |
| Compliance rules | ABBYY Timeline / Signavio adherence / ProM Declare, segregation of duties | Declare-style rules incl. four eyes with violation rates and cases, saveable as signals (#362) |
| Predictive monitoring | ABBYY Timeline, IBM Process Mining, Celonis predictive | Backtested remaining-time and outcome-risk predictions for open cases (#363) |
| Map abstraction | Fluxicon Disco / Apromore activity and path sliders, performance overlay | Activity/path sliders with frequency and performance per edge (#364) |
| Model discovery | Apromore Split Miner, PM4Py inductive miner, Signavio | Inductive-miner style discovery into reviewable catalog drafts with BPMN export (#365) |
| Task mining | Automatic cross-team task discovery | Candidate workflows; team-level k-anonymous motifs (#348); cross-day resumption (#347); multi-signal linked work items, identifiable-membership reconstruction F1 0.54 → 0.57 (#349) (target 0.90) |
| Automation runtime | Robots, orchestration, monitoring | Non-executing starters (Codex/Claude/n8n/AI SDK), shadow evaluation, run-report and SDK journal monitoring (#340, #353, #354). Executing robots stays out of scope by design |
| Documentation | AI-written PDDs with step screenshots | Structural PDD/SDD tables; versioned masked-screenshot PDD packages (#337, #344) |
| Communications mining | Email/ticket intent mining | Local intent/entity/volume mining of selected exports, aggregates only (#334) |
| Validation | Years of deployments | No real pilot; A/B/C harness never run on real users |

## A. Task mining and reconstruction quality
- [x] Reconstruction beyond exact record refs: combine resource refs, tab context, clipboard linkage and app/surface continuity with explicit uncertainty. Never merge by time alone (#349): merges on same record, observed clipboard transfer and single-record tabs; multiplexed/unreferenced tabs and app continuity are unmerged ambiguous candidates.
- [ ] Meet the preregistered thresholds in `evals/reconstruction` (assignment F1 ≥ 0.90, contamination ≤ 0.05) on the family holdout, without regressing interruption rejection. Note: deterministic signals reach 0.52 identifiable holdout F1 with #349; accepting every ambiguous candidate reaches 0.65 but 0.125 contamination. The rest is semantic linkage, so 0.90 likely needs an LLM-graded linker run with a user-supplied API key.
- [x] Cross-session and cross-day task continuity (resumed work), with explicit confidence (#347): lease-scoped idle-gap sessions and resumption candidates from shared stable pointers, never time alone.
- [x] Team-level task discovery from consenting, k-anonymous aggregates (#348): per-team and cross-team motifs, k floor per cell, complete weeks only, non-retroactive team membership, rounding, audited.

## B. Event-log interoperability and scale
- [x] OCEL 2.0 (object-centric event log) import and export (JSON and XML), with validation and bounded memory (#327, #331, #338).
- [x] XES import/export for interoperability with PM4Py, ProM, Apromore, Celonis and Signavio (#327).
- [x] Columnar local analytics engine (DuckDB) for multi-million-event logs, with 10M-event acceptance (#327).
- [x] Object-centric process maps: object types, per-object lifecycles and inter-object relations (#336, #345).
- [ ] Enterprise source connectors with real sandbox acceptance: Salesforce, ServiceNow, SAP (export or OData), Microsoft 365/Outlook. Each is opt-in and provider-scoped with incremental extraction. *(open for the agent working on source connectors; #360 provides the append/dedupe path they can load into)*

## C. Analytics depth
- [x] Token-replay or alignment conformance against reviewed BPMN: fitness, precision, deviating cases. Path alignment (#328), paired parallel models (#329), saved process graph comparison (#335), fitness bounds and precision (#339) and classic produced/consumed/missing/remaining token replay with per-activity diagnostics (#350).
- [x] Root-cause and influencer analysis: case attributes associated with slow, reworked or deviating cases, with effect sizes and confidence, never causal claims (#328).
- [x] KPI definitions and dashboards (throughput, wait, rework, SLA breach, automation rate) over saved logs, with filters and exports (#328, #330).
- [x] What-if simulation of TO-BE designs (arrival rates, durations, resources) with stated assumptions (#332, #343).
- [x] Benchmarking between cohorts, teams or periods using existing cohort comparison (#330).

## D. Documentation, communications, runtime
- [x] PDD with optional, consented, redacted step screenshots and an AI-drafted narrative clearly marked as a draft (#337, #344).
- [x] Communications mining over opted-in email/tickets: intents, entities, volumes, without retaining raw text beyond the existing work-text consent (#334).
- [x] Deployment monitoring: ingest outcomes from customer-run automations (n8n, AI SDK, Agents SDK) as event logs with success/handoff/failure, step hotspots and period drift (#340).

## E. Proof
- [ ] Real consenting pilot (2–4 weeks, multiple teams). Grade with `evals/reconstruction`, `evals/product_value.py` (paired McNemar and bootstrap) and source-verified outcomes.
- [ ] Competitor-style UX review against realistic consenting datasets; record what fails.

## F. Gaps found in the second parity review
- [x] F1 Organizational mining over saved event logs: handover-of-work and working-together networks, activity × resource matrix and workload counts. Resources are pseudonymous by default; no per-person speed, ranking or performance scoring (#352).
- [x] F2 KPI signals (Celonis Action Engine / UiPath alert parity): saved, immutable thresholds over event-log KPIs and case conditions, evaluated on demand, producing signals with evidence cases and new-since-last-check. Signals never execute actions (#355, #358).
- [x] F3 Ad-hoc analysis builder (PQL-like): typed, bounded filter/group/aggregate over event logs without raw SQL, exportable and saveable (#357).
- [x] F4 Automation opportunity pipeline (Automation Hub parity): reviewable idea → assessing → approved/rejected/on hold → implemented with history and stale-edit refusal, ease questionnaire and impact modeled from stated assumptions, priority quadrants; never claimed savings or execution (#361).
- [x] F5 Incremental append for saved event logs with duplicate skipping, batch-prefixed IDs, transactional conflict rollback and an append history (#360).

## G. Gaps from other vendors (ABBYY Timeline, Signavio, Disco, Apromore, IBM, PM4Py)
- [x] G1 Predictive monitoring for open cases: remaining time and outcome risk from comparable historical prefixes, with temporal backtesting, calibration and minimum-support suppression. Predictions are estimates, never commitments or performance ratings (#363).
- [x] G2 Declarative compliance rules (Declare-style): response, precedence, existence counts, not-co-existence, response-within-time and segregation of duties (four eyes), with violation rates and violating cases, saveable as signals. Descriptive checks, not verified policy or legal compliance (#362).
- [x] G3 Disco-style process map with activity and path abstraction sliders and a frequency/performance overlay (#364).
- [x] G4 Automatic process model discovery from a log into a reviewable draft (decisions, loops, structured parallel regions) with BPMN export via the existing catalog (#365).

## H. Performance and change analysis (Disco, ProM, Apromore, Celonis)
- [x] H1 Processing vs waiting time from start/complete lifecycle events (XES `lifecycle:transition` or a CSV column) or a per-event end-time attribute: per-activity processing and waiting, flow efficiency, waiting hotspots by transition. No per-person speed. CSV import can keep chosen extra columns as event attributes (#366).
- [x] H2 Dotted chart (Disco/ProM): events over time per case, coloured by activity, with relative or absolute time, sampling and hover (#367).
- [x] H3 Process map comparison (Apromore compare): two cohorts or periods side by side, with case-share and median-gap differences per path and confidence intervals (#368).
- [x] H4 Concept drift detection (Apromore/ProM): changes in directly-follows profiles over time windows, with change points from a permutation test, Bonferroni correction and a practical-size floor (#369).

## Acceptance gates (as in #264, plus)
- Backward-compatible REST/MCP, exports, dashboard, capture and Discovery Mode.
- Cross-tenant isolation, revocation/retention, safe HTML, semantic ambiguity and concurrent-edit tests.
- Performance acceptance at the stated scale for every engine change.
- No derived path or statistical association presented as a verified business workflow, cause or authorization.

## Coordinating parallel agents
To avoid collisions, claim an item before starting it (in a comment or by marking it *claimed* here), work on a branch named after the area (e.g. `feat/ocel-import`), and keep shared files (`tests.yml`, `dashboard/index.html`, the process model) to minimal additive edits. Both agents are extending the event-log workspace files (`server/event_log_*.py`, `shared/event_log_formats.py`, `dashboard/event_log_workspace.js`); merge `main` before pushing to them.

items.title: Service Discovery for Tenant NATS Instances
items.body:
## 🎯 Execution Order: **Issue #21** (Part of #1)

**Dependencies**: #1 (Tenant NATS instances must be provisionable)  
**Blocks**: #4 (Multi-tenant needs discovery), #19 (Auto-scaling needs discovery)  
**Can Run in Parallel With**: #20 (State Tracking)

**NOTE**: Basic implementation should be done as part of #1 Week 3. This issue is for production-ready API and health checks.

---

## Description

Implement service discovery mechanism for workers to connect to all tenant NATS instances.

Related to: #1 (Build Core Platform Foundation)  
Documentation: [docs/NATS_ARCHITECTURE.md](../blob/main/docs/NATS_ARCHITECTURE.md)

## Objectives

**Kubernetes DNS Integration**:
- ✅ Each tenant NATS instance has Kubernetes Service
- ✅ Predictable DNS naming: \`nats-{tenant-id}-{N}.vrsky-tenants.svc.cluster.local\`
- ✅ Service discovery via Control Plane API

**Control Plane API**:
- ✅ \`GET /api/tenants/{tenant_id}/nats-instances\` - Returns list of NATS URLs
- ✅ PostgreSQL tracking table: \`nats_instances\`
- ✅ Real-time updates when new instances provisioned

**Worker Discovery**:
- ✅ Workers fetch NATS instances on startup
- ✅ Workers connect to all instances (comma-separated URLs)
- ✅ Workers reconnect when new instances added
- ✅ NATS client handles automatic reconnection

**Health Checks**:
- ✅ Liveness probe on NATS instances
- ✅ Mark instance as unhealthy if unreachable
- ✅ Remove unhealthy instances from discovery

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Control Plane API returns list of NATS URLs for tenant
- [ ] PostgreSQL table tracks all active NATS instances
- [ ] Workers connect to all tenant NATS instances on startup
- [ ] Workers automatically reconnect when new instance added
- [ ] Unhealthy instances removed from discovery within 60 seconds
- [ ] Health check endpoint validates NATS connectivity
- [ ] API response time: <50ms for instance list

## Technical Specifications

**Database Schema**:
\`\`\`sql
CREATE TABLE nats_instances (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    tenant_id VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    instance_number INT NOT NULL,
    dns_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    status VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, -- active, draining, terminated
    integration_count INT DEFAULT 0,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE(tenant_id, instance_number)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_nats_instances_tenant ON nats_instances(tenant_id, status);
\`\`\`

**API Response**:
\`\`\`json
{
  "tenant_id": "tenant-a",
  "nats_instances": [
    {
      "url": "nats://nats-tenant-a-1.vrsky-tenants.svc.cluster.local:4222",
      "instance_number": 1,
      "status": "active",
      "integration_count": 35
    }
  ]
}
\`\`\`

**Worker Connection**:
\`\`\`go
// Fetch instances from Control Plane
instances := controlPlane.GetNATSInstances(tenantID)
urls := []string{}
for _, inst := range instances {
    urls = append(urls, inst.URL)
}

// Connect to all instances
nc, _ := nats.Connect(
    strings.Join(urls, ","),
    nats.MaxReconnects(-1),
)
\`\`\`

## Timeline

**Estimated**: 2 weeks  
**Target**: Week 3-4 (Feb 10 - Feb 23) - Basic in #1, API hardening here  
**Team Size**: 1 engineer

## Dependencies & Blockers

**Depends On**: #1 (NATS instance provisioning working)  
**Blocks**: #4 (Multi-tenant isolation), #19 (Auto-scaling)  
**Parallel**: #20 (State Tracking - independent work)

## Related Files

- \`internal/api/nats_instances.go\` - API endpoints
- \`internal/repository/nats_instances.go\` - Database operations
- \`pkg/discovery/nats.go\` - Discovery client library
- \`cmd/worker/main.go\` - Worker startup with discovery

items.title: Per-schema namespace profiles ignore namespace_verdicts.yaml, leaking verdict-only default-deny resources into tenant scope
items.body:
## Problem

`NamespaceProfileEnricher._enrich_schemas` writes per-schema `x-f5xc-namespace-profile` values by resolving each schema name through `_match_schema_to_resource`, which matches against the **curated** map only:

```python
resources = self.config.get("resources", {})
...
resource_type = self._match_schema_to_resource(schema_name, resources)
```

`self.verdicts` (the machine-owned, authoritative layer from `config/namespace_verdicts.yaml`) is never consulted. `get_profile_for_resource` and `is_resource_explicit` both layer verdicts correctly; only the per-schema pass is verdict-blind.

Consequence: a resource classified **only** by a verdict — including every `method: default_deny` entry, i.e. `allowed: ["system"]`, `status: restricted` — is correctly system-scoped at the domain/enricher level but its `components.schemas.*` entries silently inherit the tenant domain default `["custom", "default", "shared"]`. That is precisely the leak the policy in `test_all_create_path_resources_have_explicit_namespace_profile` exists to prevent ("under default-deny display it would leak an unverified resource into user namespaces"), just one layer lower and unguarded by any test.

## Evidence

17 resources are verdict-only today (`default_deny`, not curated in `config/namespace_profile.yaml`): `address_allocator`, `authentication`, `authorization_server`, `bigip_http_proxy`, `cdn_purge_command`, `cminstance`, `contact`, `customer_support`, `external_connector`, `fast_acl_rule`, `k8s_cluster_role_binding`, `k8s_pod_security_policy`, `nfv_service`, `report_config`, `tpm_api_key`, `tpm_category`, `usb_policy`.

Reading the committed enriched output shows the split — curated resources get `system` at schema level, verdict-only ones get tenant:

```text
tenant_and_identity.json  authenticationCreateSpecType       allowed=['custom', 'default', 'shared']
marketplace.json          external_connectorCreateSpecType   allowed=['custom', 'default', 'shared']
ddos.json                 infraprotect_asnCreateSpecType     allowed=['system']       # curated
```

(`usb_policy` reads `['system']` only incidentally — it inherits a system domain default from `ce_management.json`, not from its verdict.)

This is why #1098 was fixed with a curated entry rather than a regenerated verdict: a verdict-only entry for `infraprotect_packet_capture` would have left its schemas tenant-scoped and inconsistent with its eight system-only siblings in the same spec file. See PR #1099.

## Scope

- Make the per-schema pass verdict-aware — resolve schema names against the union of curated resources and verdict keys, and take the profile from `get_profile_for_resource` (which already layers verdicts) rather than from the curated map alone.
- Add a test that fails before the fix: a verdict-only, `default_deny` resource must not receive a tenant `constraint.allowed` at schema level.
- Regenerate the enriched output. This flips per-schema `constraint.allowed` from tenant to `["system"]` for the verdict-only resources above, so it is a visible downstream contract change (Terraform provider, VS Code extension) and should land deliberately, with the `Contract-diff gate` reviewed rather than waved through.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A verdict-only `default_deny` resource resolves to `allowed: ["system"]` at both domain/info level and per-schema level.
2. A test covers the verdict-only schema-level case and fails against the current implementation.
3. The two layers agree for every resource: no resource has a `system`-scoped enricher profile and a tenant-scoped schema profile.
4. Regeneration is idempotent — a second run produces no diff.

items.title: Implement JSON Schema identity traits with versioning and migration jobs

labels.name: tier:differentiator
labels.description: tier from the feature catalogs: differentiator

milestone.title: M6: Identity Model, User Management, Migration, and Exit
milestone.description:
the identity data model done without the decade-old paper cuts, plus migration as a product in both directions. Schema-driven user traits, flexible identifiers, complete CRUD, streaming bulk import with foreign hashes, lazy migration, first-party importers, and the exit-friendliness covenant that makes "you can always leave" the trust wedge.

Exit criteria:
- 100k-user import with foreign hashes completes with verify-then-rehash working.
- Users, states, identifiers, and schemas are manageable end to end via API.
- A full export including password hashes round-trips into a fresh instance.

items.body:
> Depends on: #52

## Why
Custom user fields are the top open ask at Hanko (#691) and Zitadel (#6433, 33 reactions). Ory Kratos is the reference implementation for schema-driven identities (its ory.sh/kratos annotation vocabulary declares which trait is a login identifier or recovery address), but Kratos ships no schema migration tooling at all: there is no way to validate existing identities against a candidate schema or transform them in bulk, and arrays in traits have been broken since 2022. Nobody in the market ships schema versioning with dry-run validation and migration jobs; it is a pure differentiator with no shipping competitor. For IronAuth this is the layer that makes the identity model schema-driven without inheriting the operational dead end: a schema you cannot evolve safely is a schema teams learn to fear. Landing versioning and migration together, rather than bolting them on later, is the whole point of doing this greenfield.

## What
- Per tenant-environment schema registry: user traits are validated against a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) on every create and update, via admin API and via self-service flows alike.
- Behavior vocabulary: schema annotations declare which fields are login identifiers, verification addresses (email, phone), and recovery channels. These annotations drive downstream login and recovery behavior; they are the contract the flexible-identifiers issue consumes.
- Trait visibility split: user-readable traits vs admin-only metadata, enforced at the API layer so self-service endpoints never leak admin-only fields.
- Arrays and nested objects in traits must work (the Kratos breakage is a named regression test).
- Validation errors return structured, per-field failures using JSON Pointer paths.
- Schema introspection endpoint: the served schema (plus behavior annotations) is fetchable so forms can generate from it; the signup form product itself is M9's.
- Schema versions: schemas are immutable versions per tenant-environment; each identity records the schema version it was validated against.
- Dry-run validation: submit a candidate schema version and run an async job that validates all existing identities against it, reporting invalid identities with per-record, per-field reasons, without mutating anything.
- Bulk migration jobs: a transform step (declarative field mapping: rename, default, drop) plus re-validation against the target version; per-record failure reporting; progress observable via API. Jobs run on the Postgres-backed job substrate; IronBus is an optional accelerator, never required (covenant).
- Cutover rule: a schema version cannot become the active default while the dry-run or migration reports unresolved invalid identities.

## Out of scope
- Identifier uniqueness, canonicalization, and identifier-first login: Implement flexible identifiers on the central canonicalization seam.
- Invariant-checked migration state machine semantics: Exploratory: model migrations as an invariant-checked state machine.
- Generalized job queue and outbox infrastructure: M11's transactional outbox and job queue issue.
- Signup form rendering and form-as-data product: M9's signup forms issue.

## Spec references
- JSON Schema specification, draft 2020-12 (validation vocabulary).
- RFC 6901 (JSON Pointer): error paths in validation failures.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Creating or updating a user with traits violating the active schema fails with per-field JSON Pointer errors; valid payloads persist the schema version used. (`ironauth-store/tests/traits.rs::traits_validate_against_the_active_version_and_persist_the_version_used`)
- [x] Behavior annotations (login identifier, verification address, recovery channel) drive login and recovery flows in integration tests. (login #684/#682, recovery #623, verification #684)
- [x] Admin-only metadata is invisible and immutable through self-service endpoints, verified by test. (`traits.rs::a_write_needs_an_active_schema_and_the_admin_only_split_holds` + the two self-service tests)
- [x] Arrays and nested objects in traits round-trip through create, PATCH, and export. (store `traits.rs` for create/PATCH; `ironauth-admin/tests/export.rs` for export (#685))
- [x] A schema-change dry-run over a seeded population reports every invalid identity with reasons, before any cutover. (`traits.rs::versioning_is_immutable_and_a_dry_run_reports_and_blocks_the_cutover`)
- [x] A bulk migration job transforms and re-validates identities, reports per-record failures, and blocks activation of the target version while failures remain. (`traits.rs::a_migration_job_transforms_deterministically_idempotently_and_unblocks_the_cutover`)

## Verification
- Unit tests on the validation layer, including the arrays-in-traits regression case named for the Kratos breakage.
- Integration tests: annotation-driven login and recovery, visibility split enforcement, dry-run and migration jobs against a 10k-identity seeded environment in CI.
- Fuzz target: schema validator fed malformed schemas and trait payloads (no panics, bounded memory).
- Job progress and failure reporting asserted via the management API in CI.

## Dependency notes
- Ship complete admin user CRUD with lifecycle states and external IDs: traits validation hangs off the user create, PATCH, and list surface that issue establishes; migration jobs mutate users through the same audited write path.

items.title: Support owned/dynamic keys in Storage for runtime span field injection
items.body:
## Problem

`Storage<'a>` uses `HashMap<&'a str, serde_json::Value>` and `record_value()` requires `key: &'a str`. This works perfectly for declared span fields — `#[instrument]` and `span!()` produce `&'static str` field names baked into the binary via `FieldSet { names: &'static [&'static str] }`.

However, there are legitimate use cases where **span field names are not known at compile time** — they come from runtime configuration, request headers, or dynamic metadata injection. Today, the only way to write such keys into Storage is `Box::leak()`, which converts an owned `String` to `&'static str` by intentionally never freeing the memory.

For startup-time config keys (bounded count, process-lifetime), `Box::leak` is acceptable. But for **per-request dynamic keys** — where field names arrive via request headers or per-request config overrides — `Box::leak` causes unbounded memory growth proportional to request volume × unique keys.

## Use Cases

1. **Config-driven field renaming**: A TOML config maps `"connector" = "gateway"` — the target key `"connector"` is a runtime string that needs to be written into span Storage. Keys are known at startup but not at compile time.

2. **Static value injection**: Config like `[log.static_values] "hostname" = "my-service"` adds flat key-value pairs to spans. Keys are startup-bounded.

3. **Per-request metadata relay**: An upstream caller sends dynamic key-value pairs (via headers or config overrides) that should appear as top-level fields in the span's log output. Field names are not known at startup — they vary per request or per tenant.

4. **Multi-tenant log schemas**: Different tenants require different field names in structured logs. A middleware injects tenant-specific fields into spans at runtime.

All these cases require writing **owned `String` keys** into `Storage`, which the current `&'a str` API does not support without leaking memory.

## Proposed Solutions

### Option 1: Owned `String` keys (simplest)

Change the HashMap to use owned keys. Remove the lifetime parameter entirely.

```rust
// Before
pub struct Storage<'a> {
    values: HashMap<&'a str, serde_json::Value>,
}
pub fn record_value(&mut self, key: &'a str, value: serde_json::Value)
pub fn values(&self) -> &HashMap<&'a str, serde_json::Value>

// After
pub struct Storage {
    values: HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
}
pub fn record_value(&mut self, key: &str, value: serde_json::Value)
pub fn values(&self) -> &HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>
```

**Pros:**
- Simplest API — no lifetime parameter, no generics
- Dynamic keys work naturally, no leak
- Keys are owned by Storage and freed when span closes

**Cons:**
- Small allocation per declared field (`field.name().to_string()`) — ~10-20 bytes per field, 5-10 fields per span. Negligible in practice but non-zero.

**Backward compatibility:**
- `record_value(&'a str)` → `record_value(&str)` — less restrictive, all existing callers compile
- `values()` return type changes — callers iterating `for (k, v)` get `&String` instead of `&&str`, both deref to `&str`
- `Visit` trait implementation is an internal detail — `field.name()` calls `.to_string()` inside, invisible to callers

### Option 2: `Cow<'a, str>` keys (zero-cost for static keys)

Use `Cow` to borrow when possible (declared fields) and own when needed (dynamic fields).

```rust
use std::borrow::Cow;

pub struct Storage<'a> {
    values: HashMap<Cow<'a, str>, serde_json::Value>,
}
pub fn record_value(&mut self, key: impl Into<Cow<'a, str>>, value: serde_json::Value)
pub fn values(&self) -> &HashMap<Cow<'a, str>, serde_json::Value>
```

**Pros:**
- Zero allocation for declared fields — `Cow::Borrowed(field.name())` stores the `&'static str` pointer directly
- Dynamic fields use `Cow::Owned(key)` — no leak, freed with Storage
- Keeps `'a` lifetime parameter (less structural change)

**Cons:**
- Slightly more complex API — callers see `Cow` in signatures
- `Cow<str>` is 24 bytes vs 8 bytes for `&str` (pointer + discriminant + length) per key
- `values()` return type exposes `Cow` to consumers

**Backward compatibility:**
- `impl Into<Cow<'a, str>>` accepts both `&str` and `String` — existing callers compile
- Iteration over values changes from `&&str` to `&Cow<str>` — `Cow` implements `Deref<Target=str>`, so string operations work

### Option 3: No upstream change — caller-side interning

Keep Storage as-is. Callers that need dynamic keys maintain a global intern cache:

```rust
static INTERNED: LazyLock<RwLock<HashSet<&'static str>>> = ...;

fn intern(key: &str) -> &'static str {
    if let Some(&existing) = INTERNED.read().unwrap().get(key) {
        return existing;
    }
    let leaked = Box::leak(key.to_string().into_boxed_str());
    INTERNED.write().unwrap().insert(leaked);
    leaked
}
```

Each unique key leaks exactly once. Bounded by unique key count, not request volume.

**Pros:**
- No upstream change required
- Memory leak bounded by unique key cardinality

**Cons:**
- Global mutable state (RwLock) on every dynamic key write
- Memory is still leaked (intentionally, bounded)
- Every consumer with dynamic keys must independently implement interning
- Does not solve the root cause — the API still cannot express owned keys

## Impact Analysis

- **Public API**: Options 1 and 2 are backward compatible — signatures become less restrictive or use `Into` traits
- **Performance**: Option 1 adds ~80 bytes of allocation per span (negligible). Option 2 adds zero for static keys. Option 3 adds a RwLock read per dynamic key.
- **Tests**: All existing tests pass without modification for Options 1 and 2
- **Other crates**: No other crate in the workspace uses `Storage` directly
- **Visit trait**: Internal implementation detail — `field.name()` handling changes inside the impl, trait interface is unchanged

## Recommendation

Option 1 (`String`) for simplicity or Option 2 (`Cow`) for zero-cost static keys. Both eliminate `Box::leak` for dynamic keys and are backward compatible. The allocation overhead of Option 1 is negligible for typical span field counts (5-10 fields).

items.title: Connector SDK v2 — known follow-ups and limitations
items.body:
Follow-up tracker for items deferred from PR #60. None are blocking the merge; each is documented in the PR's adversarial self-review as defensible-to-defer. Filed in one place so reviewers can see they're tracked.

## Deferred from PR #60

### Security
- [ ] **JWKS signature verification on `id_token`** — `auth-manager.ts:handleOAuthCallback` decodes id_token claims without verifying the JWT signature. Trust model: provider's TLS-secured token endpoint. Adding `jose` / `jwks-rsa` would harden against TLS-interception scenarios with corporate CAs. ~50 lines of net-new crypto + a runtime fetch per OAuth callback. Documented decision in the code comment.

- [ ] **Encryption key rotation tooling** — `BORINGOS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is loaded once at startup and cached for the process lifetime. Documented in README that key loss = data loss. No rotation script. Would need: a re-encrypt utility that reads with key A and writes with key B, plus a documented dual-key window during rollover.

### Robustness
- [ ] **Legacy plaintext-credentials backward-compat branch** — `unpackCredentials` accepts both string (encrypted) and object (pre-encryption) shapes. No explicit removal trigger. Should be controlled by a `BORINGOS_LEGACY_PLAINTEXT_CREDENTIALS` env flag that operators set to false after migration, with the object branch throwing once flipped. Removable in a future major.

- [ ] **HMAC OAuth state TTL** — currently 10 minutes (`auth-manager-state.ts:STATE_TTL_MS`). Matches pre-v2 behavior. Users on slow connections or who tab away during consent see 'Invalid OAuth state'. Worth bumping to 15-30 minutes.

### API / DX
- [ ] **`profileService` API shape** — Google connector exposes identity scopes (openid/email/profile) via a 'hidden' service in `services[]`. Module developers shouldn't see this as a discrete service. Cleaner: a `requiredScopes: ScopeDefinition[]` field on `ConnectorDefinition` that the AuthManager always adds to OAuth flows.

- [ ] **Tool result shape convention** — Documented inline in google.ts: list-style tools wrap with a named key (`{ events }`, `{ messages }`), singular tools return the value directly. Should be hoisted into the module-sdk docs as a first-class convention so third-party module authors follow the same pattern.

### Operational
- [ ] **`lastSyncAt` cosmetic regression** — Connectors screen shows 'Never synced' for all providers because the `connector_accounts` table has no `last_sync_at` column. Ships with Phase 3 UI (#59). Until then, hide the field instead of showing the misleading 'Never synced'.

- [ ] **Per-module rate limiting on connector API usage** — The `connector_token_issuance` audit table records every issuance with `caller_module_id`, giving the data foundation. The enforcement layer doesn't exist yet. Out-of-scope for v1 per the spec.

### Multi-tenant / Multi-account UX
- [ ] **Phase 3 UI work** — Tracked in #59. Backend schema and AuthManager support multi-account, OAuth app overrides per tenant, and module-account bindings. Shell SPA shows one card per provider and has no binding configuration UI. Ships when there's concrete demand.

### Test coverage
- [ ] **AsyncLocalStorage tenant propagation test** — `tenant-context.ts` threads tenantId through `deps.getConnectorToken` and friends. No test verifies the propagation; the AuthManager integration test (#60) sets tenantId explicitly. Worth a test that exercises the tool dispatcher → handler → deps chain end-to-end.

- [ ] **Token refresh path test** — `AuthManager.refreshIfNeeded` exchanges a refresh token when the access token is within 60s of expiry. Integration coverage exists for the issuance path; refresh path is exercised only via the manual test.

### MDK coordination (separate but related — #50)
- [ ] **Publish `@boringos/*` packages to npm** — MDK Phase 1. Currently `0.1.8` in package.json but only installable via workspace symlink. Once published, third-party module developers get the real lego-block experience (`pnpm add @boringos/connector-google` in a fresh project).
- [ ] **`module.json` generation from manifest** — MDK Phase 2.
- [ ] **`ModuleFactoryDeps` formal typing** — MDK Phase 3. Stable contract after #60 merges. The connector slice resolved the 'which builder hooks runtime modules can register' open question.

---

Filed for tracking. Each item can move to its own issue when picked up.

items.title: Policy drift: make action_policy.yaml authoritative before exposing a describe contract

labels.name: set: 4 action-rail
labels.description: PRD ownership — feature set 4 proves this works (docs/prd/04)

items.body:
Context: follow-up to the accepted [error-fidelity direction](https://github.com/aks129/HealthClawGuardrails/discussions/75). The maintainer’s sequencing constraint is load-bearing: enforcement first, description second.

## Current state

`action_policy.yaml` describes itself as the policy matrix “consumed by the compliance-gates CI job and referenced by the agent orchestrator.” On current `main`, neither claim is true.

1. **No runtime or CI reader exists.** Nothing parses the file for enforcement or for `compliance-gates`; the only non-doc code reference is a comment in `r6/models.py`.
2. **The orchestrator image does not contain it.** `services/agent-orchestrator/Dockerfile` copies `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, and `src/`, not the repository-root YAML.
3. **Hardcoded behavior contradicts it.** The YAML marks `fhir_propose_write` as requiring step-up, while the tool description says the preview is safe without step-up and the runtime gate exempts it.
4. **It covers only 13 of the 29 exposed tools.** Missing tools include the connector pair, questionnaire tools, `guardrail_conformance`, `care_gaps`, SHL, wearables/sources, and the entire `action_*` family. Under `defaults.unknown_action: deny`, a literal interpretation would deny most of the current surface.
5. **Its approval vocabulary predates v1.8 actions.** It defines `human_review` as `X-Human-Confirmed: true`, but real-world actions now use out-of-band `ActionConfirmation` and execute only from the confirm route. Clinical FHIR writes still use the header. One undifferentiated “human review” mode can no longer describe both honestly.

For a project whose thesis is “verifiable, not marketing,” a policy document that neither CI nor runtime reads is not a contract. A corrective error must not point an agent at it until that is fixed.

## Proposed work

This should land as two sequential PRs under one tracked issue.

### Stage 1 — make policy authoritative and checked

1. **Define and validate the schema.** Specify required fields, wildcard/default precedence, supported approval mechanisms, and invalid combinations. Startup/build must fail closed on malformed or ambiguous policy.
2. **Compile or load one canonical artifact.** The Node runtime, policy tests, and any Python-facing description endpoint must consume the same generated/validated representation; do not create independent TypeScript and Python interpretations that can drift.
3. **Model the actual ceremonies.** Distinguish at least:
   - automatic/read-only;
   - step-up;
   - clinical FHIR header confirmation;
   - out-of-band `ActionConfirmation` for action rails;
   - deny.
4. **Cover the full exposed surface.** Every name in `tools/list` / `adapters/tools.manifest.json` must resolve to an explicit policy or a deliberately tested default. The current 13/29 coverage must not pass.
5. **Make runtime classification derive from policy.** Tool tier/approval metadata and the orchestrator’s preflight decisions come from the authoritative artifact rather than a second hardcoded list.
6. **Keep Flask defense-in-depth.** Policy may describe and tighten endpoint gates but may never relax the Flask layer’s step-up, tenant, audit, redaction, or human-confirmation invariants. Document which layer owns tool policy and which owns endpoint security.
7. **Ship it and test drift.** The production orchestrator image contains the compiled policy artifact, and CI fails when the YAML, manifest/tool registry, runtime tier, or generated artifact disagree.

Stage 1 is independently valuable and should merge before any `describe` tool exists.

### Stage 2 — expose a bounded `describe(resource_type)` tool

Add a read-only MCP tool that projects the now-authoritative policy plus the search-parameter registry from the strict-search issue:

```json
{
  "resourceType": "MedicationRequest",
  "search_params": [
    {"name": "patient", "type": "reference", "note": "Patient/{id}"},
    {"name": "status", "type": "token"}
  ],
  "tools": [
    {"tool": "fhir_search", "approval": "auto"},
    {
      "tool": "fhir_commit_write",
      "approval": "clinical_header_confirmation",
      "gates": ["step_up", "human_confirmed"]
    }
  ],
  "notes": ["reads are PHI-redacted", "clinical responses carry a disclaimer"]
}
```

Properties:

- **Lazy and bounded:** one resource type per call; no full StructureDefinition or entire policy dump.
- **Honest by construction:** the response is generated from the same artifact runtime classification uses.
- **Static, not caller-aware:** it describes the contract but does not claim to evaluate a tenant, SMART scope, token state, or patient-specific authorization.
- **Useful to corrective errors:** search/policy errors can say `call describe("Observation")` only after the tool is backed by real enforcement.

## Acceptance criteria

### Stage 1

- [ ] CI proves every exposed tool resolves to a policy and that runtime tier/approval matches it.
- [ ] The current `fhir_propose_write` contradiction is resolved deliberately, not hidden by changing only prose.
- [ ] Action tools use the out-of-band confirmation vocabulary; clinical FHIR writes retain their separate header ceremony.
- [ ] A malformed, ambiguous, missing, or stale generated policy fails build/startup closed.
- [ ] The orchestrator production image contains the authoritative runtime artifact.
- [ ] Direct Flask security invariants remain enforced even if the orchestrator is bypassed.

### Stage 2

- [ ] `describe(resource_type)` returns only the bounded static contract for a supported type.
- [ ] Unsupported resource types return a corrective tool error.
- [ ] Tool approvals and search parameters exactly match the runtime policy and search registry in drift tests.
- [ ] Adding the tool updates all manifest/tool-count/docs surfaces required by REVIEW_STANDARDS.
- [ ] Corrective errors reference `describe` only after Stage 1 is merged.

## Scope boundaries

- No caller-aware authorization evaluation.
- No full FHIR schema/StructureDefinition export.
- No per-tenant dynamic policy language in this issue.
- Stage 2 must not merge ahead of Stage 1.

## Blocked by

- Stage 1: none — can start immediately.
- Stage 2: #94, because `describe` consumes its search-parameter registry.

Happy to take Stage 1 first; Stage 2 can follow as a separate PR. cc @aks129 as requested in discussion #75.

items.title: feat(ontology): configurable per-graph pipelines — pack ships default stages, each graph can customise them (CRM-style), stage changes recorded as dated events

labels.name: P2-moderate
labels.description: Beta MODERATE — real but survivable for beta.

items.body:
**O/I/T:**
- Objective: Give stage-driven kinds a **configurable pipeline** — the pack ships sensible default stages, and each graph can add/rename/reorder its own stages without changing the ontology or shipping a new pack. Stage movement is recorded as dated events; the current stage is derived as state. This is the CRM model (Salesforce Opportunity stages / HubSpot deal pipelines / ATS candidate pipelines are all per-tenant configuration, not fixed schema).
- Indicators: (1) a graph can list, edit and reorder the stages of a stage-driven kind without a code change or pack release; (2) the pack's defaults apply to a new graph until overridden; (3) a stage change reported in a later meeting updates the current stage and the prior value is retained as history; (4) an unrecognised stage value reported by extraction is captured (as a new-stage candidate) or flagged, never silently dropped; (5) the current stage is what a query returns, always.
- Targets: at least one test asserting default-apply → override → stage advance → current-stage-read; at least one test asserting an unknown stage value is surfaced, not lost.

**Team:** epistemic-team
**Complexity:** complex

**Why now:** owner decisions on the venture pack (#2725, 2026-09-09). Two explicit requirements:
- "the issue here (and in other kinds) is more about the lifecycle, which is a **customisable property in CRMs**, so we need flexibility somehow"
- "we need our graph to be able to represent **deals**" — a deal's stages cannot be hardcoded in a pack, because two funds (or the same fund over time) use different pipelines.

This subsumes and extends #2729: that issue covers packs *declaring* statuses plus the hardcoded `Object.status` fold. This issue adds the **per-graph customisation layer** and the stage-transition history, which the pack-declaration mechanism alone does not provide.

**Evidence (file:line) — why this is not possible today**
- The status machinery is a hardcoded producer-to-status fold: `tortoise/projection/entities.py:906-934` (keys `pm:card*`, `github.issue.*`). No pack can declare a lifecycle; no graph can override one.
- Fold vocabulary already collides across domains: `open` folds to `in_progress`, `closed` folds to `completed` (same word, two business logics).
- The manifest has no validated `statuses`/`pipelines` field on `kindDefs` (see #2729).
- Stage transitions need dated records: `CommitEvent` is 8 fixed fields with `extra="forbid"` (`tortoise/commit_schema.py:423-460`) and `apply_supersessions` has no Event branch (`tortoise/commit_ops.py:297-305`), so a "stage changed" record is currently expressible only as a generic Event with no stage payload. Confirmed by #2788 (documented event-carried state that nothing reads).
- Object identity is MERGE-by-name (`projection/entities.py:511`) — pipelines must key on the namespaced kind, not the bare name (see #2767).

**Design sketch (to be scoped)**
1. **Declaration:** a kindDef may declare `pipeline: {stages: [{id, label, order, terminal?}], default_stage}` — validated, optional.
2. **Configuration:** a per-graph `:Pipeline` record keyed by namespaced kind holding the *effective* stage list; pack defaults seed it; edits (add/rename/reorder/retire) are graph-scoped.
3. **Movement:** a stage change is a dated record (`stageFrom`, `stageTo`, `at`, `source`) on the Event layer, with the *current* stage derived as state on the Object (latest wins).
4. **Unknown values:** extraction reporting a stage that is not in the effective list becomes a new-stage candidate (open-world) or is flagged for review — never dropped.
5. **Terminal/entry semantics:** terminal stages (closed / written-off / lost) must be declared so the current-state fold does not resurrect a closed thing when a later meeting mentions it in passing.
6. **UI:** exposed where packs are configured (#2728 Settings surface) — view/edit pipeline stages per kind.

**Open decisions**
1. Editing authority: who may change a graph's pipeline (same roles as pack configuration — #2728 Q1)?
2. Migration: existing Objects already carrying status values — backfill into the effective stage list, or map-on-read?
3. Does a pipeline belong to one kind, or can several kinds share a named pipeline definition?
4. Reordering/retiring a stage that Objects currently sit in: block, or migrate those Objects?
5. Relationship to #2729: does #2729 land first as the declaration+fold mechanism with this riding on top, or are they one design?
6. Gate interaction: stage-gates (see #2725 decision 6) sit *between* stages — is a gate an attribute of a stage transition, or an independent kind that governs a transition?

### Verification Checklist
| Surface | Test Layer | Expected Verification |
|---------|-----------|----------------------|
| pipeline config | unit | default seeding + per-graph override |
| stage advance | integration | advance → current stage read; prior value retained |
| unknown stage | unit | surfaced as candidate / flagged, not dropped |
| terminal stages | unit | closed thing not resurrected by a later mention |
| multi-graph isolation | integration | pipeline edits in graph A do not affect graph B |
| UI | e2e | edit stages in Settings; effect visible on the entity |

### Complexity (domain-aware)
| Domain | Rating | Rationale |
|--------|--------|-----------|
| Architecture | complex | New config layer + fold rewrite + Event payloads |
| Ontology | complex | Kind-declared pipelines, terminal semantics, gate interaction |
| UX | standard | Stage editor + consequence copy |
| Config | standard | Per-graph pipeline records, migration |
| Overall | complex | |

### Fractal Fields
- **Level:** task · **Depends on:** #2729 (declaration + fold mechanism) — possibly merges with it · **Blocks:** #2725 deal/investment lifecycles; CRM-style flexibility requirement · **Related:** #2728 (pack config UI), #2782 (money attributes), #2788 (event payloads), #2767 (namespaced fold keying)

items.title: [architecture] 评审并落档 B(K8s原生) vs A(Hadoop原生) 多租户范式的能力缺口与补法决策
items.body:
## 背景

一张「控制面驱动数据面」示意图（RuoYi + 行级 `tenant_id` + Ranger + Kerberos + YARN 队列）引出一个问题：**我们的架构是否只考虑了控制平面、没考虑数据平面？**

结论是否定的——「数据平面」一词被用在两层语义上：
- **多租户语义**（`05` §2）：每租户隔离运行时（namespace/schema-per-tenant），已是一等公民。
- **大数据处理栈语义**（调度/计算/存储/OLAP）：落在 `data-foundation` + `platform-common` + `03-技术选型`，同样已覆盖。

真正的差异不是「缺数据平面」，而是**两套多租户隔离/控制范式之争**，二者**能力覆盖非对称**。本 Issue 沉淀对比，并就 B 的能力缺口给出补法建议，**待架构评审定档**。

## 两套范式

- **A · Hadoop 原生**：RuoYi 控制面 + 行级 `tenant_id`；隔离靠 YARN 资源队列（计算）/ Ranger 行列权限（数据）/ Kerberos（认证）。租户隔离做在**大数据组件内部**。
- **B · K8s 原生（本平台现状，AD-12）**：`control-plane` + Keycloak Organizations；隔离靠 namespace-per-tenant + ResourceQuota/NetworkPolicy（计算）/ schema-db-per-tenant + Doris·Paimon catalog（数据）/ Keycloak OIDC（认证）。租户隔离做在**平台/身份层**。

> 数据平面**组件选型两边高度重合**（DolphinScheduler/Flink/Doris 均在 `03`）；分歧只在**谁来做租户隔离**——组件层 vs 平台层。

## 能力覆盖对照（仅列非对称项）

| 维度 | A 覆盖 | B 覆盖 | 谁独占 / 差异 |
|--|--|--|--|
| 租户边界强度·爆炸半径 | 逻辑（行过滤，易串租户） | 物理/逻辑（ns+schema/db） | **B 独占**强隔离 |
| 租户内行列级数据权限 | Ranger 跨引擎统一行列+脱敏 | 仅租户间；租户内需另建 | **A 更原生** |
| 租户密度/规模 | 万级小租户高密度 | ≤15 大客户（定档） | **A 覆盖海量** |
| 批作业资源治理 | YARN 队列抢占/混部 | pod 粒度，引擎自治 | **A 更细** |
| 认证联邦/多端 | Hadoop 内 Kerberos 互信 | OIDC/SAML/AD 联邦/多端 | **B 覆盖 Web/SaaS** |
| 网络微隔离 | 无 | NetworkPolicy | **B 独占** |
| 整租户自动化开通 | 插行+配 policy（无独立栈） | Helm SDK 一键独立栈+生命周期 | 各覆盖一端 |
| 跨租户全局分析 | 同库聚合顺手 | 跨 schema/db，较难 | **A 更顺** |
| 存量 Hadoop 对接 | 天然贴合 | 需桥接 | **A 覆盖存量** |

## B 的四个缺口 — 逐项分析与补法决策

**① 租户内行列级数据权限（P0 · 必补）**
政企刚需（行级数据权限 + 列级脱敏）。但 A 的强项是「跨多引擎统一策略面」，而我们查询出口集中在 Doris+Paimon，引擎少，**不必上全量 Ranger**。
建议：`governance`（策略定义/分类分级）+ `security`（鉴权下推）做 policy-as-code，编译下推 **Doris 原生 row policy/列授权/脱敏**；**Ranger + Doris 插件作为 escape hatch**，留给强监管/存量 Ranger 客户。

**② 存量 Hadoop+Ranger+Kerberos 对接（P1 · 按需补）**
私有化销售真场景。分两子情形：(a) 存量 Hadoop 当数据源——只需**采集侧** Kerberos（keytab 经 ESO）+ Ranger 管控读；(b) 要求跑在客户 Hadoop 上——属另一交付形态。
建议：**限定补 (a)**——`data-foundation`/`platform-common` Connector SPI 增 Kerberos + Ranger-aware Hive/HDFS 连接器（与 AD-15 采集边界一致）；(b) 划边界、按项目定制，**不退范式**。

**③ 批作业队列级资源抢占/SLA 混部（P2 · 备杠杆）**
K8s ResourceQuota 是 namespace/pod 粒度，给不了 YARN 式跨作业队列抢占。但**无需退回 YARN**：需要时引入 **Volcano / Apache YuniKorn**（K8s 原生批调度器：队列+gang+抢占+公平份额），对接 Spark/Flink Operator。
建议：默认现状（ResourceQuota + Flink slot/Doris resource group）；批作业 SLA 争抢出现时上 Volcano/YuniKorn。**缺口可在 B 范式内闭合。**

**④ 海量小租户高密度 SaaS（P3 · 暂缓）**
超出定位（≤15 大客户，预留数十）。只有「公网 SaaS 转长尾 SMB 自助」才触发。
建议：**暂缓**，保留 `control-plane` 供给档「向下加池化档（共享 ns + 行级 tenant_id）」的演进位（`05` C 分层/Bridge「档位可调」已留概念钩子）。

## 净结论

四缺口中**仅 ① 需现在动手**；② 跟私有化订单走；③④ 可在 B 范式内（或暂不）解决——**无一需把范式退回 A**。A 相对 B 的覆盖优势大多能用 B 范式内工具补齐，而 B 的强隔离/云原生/现代身份优势 A 补不回来。**坚持 B、按上述优先级补缺口为推荐方向。**

## 完成标准（DoD）

- [ ] 架构评审确认 B 为主范式、四缺口优先级与补法档位（或提出修正）
- [ ] ① 行列级数据权限方案定档（policy-as-code 下推 Doris vs Ranger 插件 escape hatch）落 `governance`/`security` 设计
- [ ] ② 采集侧 Kerberos/Ranger 连接器纳入 `data-foundation` backlog，(b) 边界写明
- [ ] ③ Volcano/YuniKorn 记为 P2 演进杠杆（触发条件写明）
- [ ] ④ 海量小租户池化档记为暂缓项，演进位说明
- [ ] 决策沉淀为 ADR 或并入 `docs/architecture/05-多租户与控制平面.md`（含四缺口×补法×escape hatch 决策表）

## 参考

`docs/architecture/05-多租户与控制平面.md`（§2 控制/数据平面、§3 隔离定档）· `03-技术选型.md` · `02-平台治理与网关.md` · `README.md` AD-12/AD-15 · `docs/00-主仓初始化-spec.md` §2.1

items.title: Security: enforce authenticated owner/project scope on task history and live SSE before Syntra activation
items.body:
## Why this is required
Syntra’s planned native, authenticated mission monitor must not expose other users’ tasks or private event payloads. Source inspection at **`65a6262717adcd52ac8d8a16ed6f223e299fd74d`** found an ownership gap that blocks safe activation; this is a *source-level access-control finding*, **not proof of a confirmed real-world exploitation**.

Current observations:
- `orchestrator-service/src/main/java/io/aetheris/orchestrator/api/OperationsStreamController.java`: `GET /api/orchestrator/live/events` calls `TaskEventStreamService.subscribeAll()`.
- `.../task/TaskEventStreamService.java`: a single `globalEmitters` list receives all task events; publisher loops over subscribers without owner/project filtering.
- `.../task/TaskEntity.java`: there is no durable authenticated `ownerId` or `projectId`.
- `.../api/TaskController.java`: `/{id}`, `/{id}/events/history`, and `/{id}/events` check task existence, not caller ownership.
- Gateway bearer `orchestrator:read` is an operation scope, **not** proof of ownership of any given task. Direct runtime access or forged headers must not bypass this boundary.

## Required implementation (separate reviewed PR, fail closed)
1. Define canonical principal/owner binding and trusted upstream identity transport. **Never** trust client-supplied identity headers on directly exposed runtime ports; validate JWT independently or require an authenticated gateway-to-runtime channel. Coordinate the platform gateway and runtime releases.
2. Persist authoritative task owner and (where applicable) project/tenant IDs at creation. Handle pre-existing ownerless tasks as **not readable by arbitrary users** with an explicit migration/policy.
3. Filter recent task list, per-task view, history and per-task live subscriptions by authenticated owner/project; deny 401/403/404 consistently with non-leaking errors. Ensure SSE event publication has no global cross-owner broadcast.
4. Replace or scope `/api/orchestrator/live/events`: either remove owner-client access or filter events server-side before dispatch.
5. Use verified owner context on mission creation, mission task attachment and mission event/history retrieval, not merely caller-supplied task UUIDs.
6. Add two distinct synthetic authenticated accounts with overlapping task lifecycles and verify **no cross-account reads**, subscriber cleanup, reconnect/replay isolation, expiry, logout/revocation, forged identity headers, direct-runtime-port attempts and protected event metadata handling.
7. Keep all previously approved policy/STOP/approval behavior and test suite green. No unrestricted actions or production activation.

## Syntra client safety
Platform draft [PR #227](https://github.com/teldigi5-wq/aetheris-platform/pull/227) adds a fail-closed client owner mission gate with source-backed evidence and Rust test-only scoped grants. Live SSE is intentionally disabled there. Client activation can follow only after server-side ownership proof, native vault/session verification and owner-PC validation.

## Release and validation truth
Security review and hosted integration tests required. No production/physical-PC claims; `BLOCKED_PENDING_HARDWARE` persists. Do not merge protected main or expose live task feeds from this issue alone.

## 28 October 2026 — Containment progress (NOT authorization closure)

- [Draft PR #205](https://github.com/teldigi5-wq/aetheris-ai-runtime/pull/205) exact-head `bef63f77167464e65a733ab51a1269a24af81327`, [CI #40670475066](https://github.com/teldigi5-wq/aetheris-ai-runtime/actions/runs/40670475066) **9/9 passed**: removed unscoped global task SSE broadcast; ownerless event history/replay and global live events deny with HTTP 404; internal journal preserved.
- [Draft PR #207](https://github.com/teldigi5-wq/aetheris-ai-runtime/pull/207) exact-head `4918900fa174b469b25f418a5374f4d91b1af6ac`, [CI #40673524552](https://github.com/teldigi5-wq/aetheris-ai-runtime/actions/runs/40673524552) **9/9 passed**, 7/7 real Java tests: unconditional early 404 for all external task/mission HTTP API routes (read, create, transition, attach, message); even forged headers, guessed UUID and direct-port requests cannot enter controller *when these candidate filters are installed*. Health/other API paths remain separately subject to review.

**These are DRAFT/UNMERGED containment candidates, NOT deployed.** TaskEntity has no durable owner/tenant/project bindings, no independently verified runtime principal, no migration/quarantine for ownerless historical tasks, no per-owner SSE/replay and no tested token revocation; this issue must stay OPEN. Next candidate: introduce verified principal and transactional ownership persistence with independent two-tenant and direct-port tests, then review rollout before restoring HTTP APIs. Stage45 NO_GO; nine independent production certifications outstanding.


### 28 October 2026 — signed-principal and owner-schema security prerequisites (NOT deployed)

- [DRAFT PR #208](https://github.com/teldigi5-wq/aetheris-ai-runtime/pull/208): [exact-head CI #40675324578](https://github.com/teldigi5-wq/aetheris-ai-runtime/actions/runs/40675324578) **9/9 green**, 13/13 Java tests. Independent operator-pinned RS256 JWT verification for Identity issuer, audience, kid, signed UID, role/scope and lifetime; deliberately **not wired to HTTP routes** or considered a verified object owner.
- [DRAFT PR #209](https://github.com/teldigi5-wq/aetheris-ai-runtime/pull/209): [exact-head CI #40676133713](https://github.com/teldigi5-wq/aetheris-ai-runtime/actions/runs/40676133713) **9/9 green**. Disposable PostgreSQL16 synthetic schema supports nullable UID/tenant/project bindings, rejects partial/NULL/zero/bad IDs, shows legacy ownerless tasks remain unbound, and requires matching UID+tenant+project predicates; transaction ROLLBACK and no permanent table. No real DB schema migration, application entity mapping, authenticated tenant membership, ownership grant or user data.

Issue remains OPEN; #205/#207 external task, mission and SSE lockdown still stays in candidate branches. Next work: operator-approved versioned schema, authoritative tenant/project membership and independently authenticated runtime HTTP principal; owner-scoped repository/mission/SSE operations, legacy migration policy, two-tenant integration tests, revocation and actual Gateway/direct-port security. Nine Stage45 gates NO_GO.


### 28 October 2026 — real signed UID to disposable membership SQL checkpoint

- [DRAFT PR #210](https://github.com/teldigi5-wq/aetheris-ai-runtime/pull/210), immutable head `267c1fa7237c1487286d65ae8861d16f028fa2ac`, [real PostgreSQL16 CI #40719365610](https://github.com/teldigi5-wq/aetheris-ai-runtime/actions/runs/40719365610) **9/9 success**: synthetic tenant and project membership records + scoped task query deny cross-tenant/project/UID read, legacy ownerless reads, revoked/expired membership; full transaction rolled back.
- [DRAFT PR #211](https://github.com/teldigi5-wq/aetheris-ai-runtime/pull/211), immutable head `3080b7a244f26550e4957da32c7faa69d8e46d04`, [real JWT+JDBC CI #40720953952](https://github.com/teldigi5-wq/aetheris-ai-runtime/actions/runs/40720953952) **11/11 steps, 18/18 Java tests**: fixed critical type-design weakness by sealing the VerifiedPrincipal constructor behind real pinned RS256 signature verification, then passed real synthetic PostgreSQL16 prepared-statement task read checks, spoofing and cross-tenant/project/UID denials, revocation/expiry, plus inherited task/mission/SSE HTTP lockdown tests. All temp DB tables rolled back and no permanent task/membership tables created.

**Still not closed:** These are isolated review-only prototypes and drafts, not merged or deployed. Signed principal verification is not wired into actual authenticated HTTP, no trusted persistent membership registry or approved versioned owner migration exists, task/mission writes and SSE remain unimplemented/blocked, no direct-port/Gateway mTLS combined real integration or live token/session revocation. The next work is operator-approved persisted membership lifecycle/migrations + actual two-principal resource-server and transactional task/mission authorization with replay/revocation. Keep issue OPEN, all nine Stage45 release attestations **NO_GO**.
